C API Reference#

ovclash ships two public C ABIs (C application binary interfaces) in one shared library:

  • Canonical (<ovclash/ovclash.h>): the engine contract. It covers contexts, settings, scope, pipeline execution and result retrieval.

  • Suite (<ovclash_suite/...>): the product API, built on the canonical one. It adds an object model, SQLite or JSON-directory persistence, and JSON/HTML export.

Neither layer is deprecated. Choosing an API Layer helps you pick one. The C/C++ Quickstart shows how to link and run a first query.

The SDK archive installs the headers under include/. The Python-only wheel ships no headers. The two _ovstage headers extend the API for ovstage, the runtime through which ovclash reads USD: an attached stage is a caller-owned ovstage Stage, an owner operation is work on that Stage, and the matrix decomposition mode selects how ovstage decomposes mesh matrices. This table lists the public headers, with paths relative to the ovclash root:

Header

Contents

include/ovclash/ovclash.h

Canonical C API: types, contexts, settings, pipeline and results.

include/ovclash/ovclash_ovstage.h

Optional ovstage-only extensions: Stage attachment, owner operations and matrix decomposition.

include/ovclash/ovclash_export.h

The single definition of the OVCLASH_API linkage macro.

include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_types.h

Suite handles, strings, enums and plain-data views.

include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_models.h

Suite model objects: query, clash info, frame info and point-cloud settings.

include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_serializer.h

Custom persistence callbacks and the saved-data reader for native fetch-and-save.

include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite.h

Suite runtime, persistence and export entry points.

include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_ovstage.h

Optional ovstage-only Suite extensions: Stage attachment and owner operations.

What the generated pages omit#

Doxygen, the C/C++ documentation generator, renders the eight headers of the table under C API Reference. repo.toml lists them in doxygen_input, and its doxygen_predefined list defines OVCLASH_STANDALONE=1 and an empty OVCLASH_API for that run. Some content does not reach the generated pages:

  • <ovclash/version.h> is generated at build time and is not a Doxygen input. Version constants lists its macros.

  • <ovx/string_types.h> and <ovx/dlpack/dlpack.h> belong to the ovstage SDK. Neither is a Doxygen input, so the pages do not document ovx_string_t or DLTensor, the tensor descriptor of DLPack. Strings gives the string layout. The SDK archive installs ovx/dlpack/dlpack.h, because ovclash.h includes it. It does not install ovx/string_types.h; see Linking.

  • The @defgroup comments in ovclash.h, ovclash_ovstage.h, ovclash_suite.h and ovclash_suite_models.h do not render. They hold each layer’s common contract, including the Suite error catalogues that every Suite function incorporates by reference. C API Conventions summarizes the main rules. Read the group comments in ovclash_suite.h and ovclash_suite_models.h for the full error catalogues.

  • Per-field text of most canonical structs and enums. ovclash.h documents them with plain // trailing comments, which Doxygen does not attach. Those types render with their fields but without per-field text. Each ovclash_settings_t field is documented on its ovclash_set_* setter, which does render. The consumer pages define each field of these structs with its type and values: Canonical C those of ovclash_settings_t, Overlap records those of ovclash_overlap_data_t, Overlap reports those of ovclash_overlap_report_t, and Reading results those of ovclash_stats_t and ovclash_stage_timeline_data_t. Read ovclash.h for the other fields. Easy-to-miss details there include the OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_DEFAULT composition, the -1.0f “not computed” value of maxLocalDepth, how pointSize0 is derived, and why a pair type is tested with == OVCLASH_OVERLAP_PAIR_TYPE_POINT_VS_MESH. The Suite headers use Doxygen comments throughout.

This page renders only as part of the HTML site that the Sphinx documentation generator builds; see Building this documentation. The SDK archive ships that site under docs/html/ when its build rendered it. The page is not part of the shipped consumer set in docs/consumer/. In a plain Markdown viewer, each {eval-rst} block (a fence that embeds reStructuredText in Markdown) shows only its Doxygen directive, so read the headers instead.

Canonical C API#

The engine contract. Create a context, apply settings, set the A/B scope (the two search sets of prim paths), build and run the pipeline, then read overlaps, duplicates and per-overlap reports. Use this layer for the smallest dependency surface, for direct control over the pipeline, or for borrowed zero-copy access to result buffers. The C/C++ Quickstart has a complete minimal program, and Asynchronous Pipelines covers the background run. The OVCLASH_STANDALONE macro lists the entry points that only standalone builds declare.

Functions

ovclash_string_t ovclash_get_result_string(ovclash_result_t result)#

Returns a static, library-owned name for a result status.

Maps OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS to “OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS” and every other value, including values outside the enum, to “OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR”. Both backends return byte-identical literals. The text names the status and does not describe a failure. ovclash_get_last_error() returns the concrete reason; it exists only in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds.

Note

Lifetime: valid for the process lifetime; must not be freed or modified.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; reads no context and no mutable global state.

Parameters:

result – [in] Status to describe.

Returns:

Borrowed view over a static string literal. Never null and never empty.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_backend_info(
ovclash_backend_info_t *out_info,
)#

Reports which clash backend this library was compiled with, plus its capabilities.

The OpenUSD backend writes backend_name “openusd”, native_openusd_linked 1, ovpopulation_runtime_loaded 0, ovstage_cuda_enabled 0. The ovstage backend writes “ovstage”, 0, 1, and ovstage_cuda_enabled 1 only when built with OVCLASH_OVSTAGE_CUDA_ENABLED. Every value is a compile-time constant: nothing is probed at run time and no context is needed.

Note

Lifetime: backend_name borrows a static literal valid for the process lifetime.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently.

Parameters:

out_info – [out] Receives the backend name and capability flags. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if out_info is null or, on ovstage, if the call runs inside an owner-operation callback on the same thread (see ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation). Nothing is written on error.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_settings(ovclash_settings_t *settings)#

Fills a settings struct with the Kit-compatible ovclash default table.

Writes flags = OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_DEFAULT, nbTasks 128, sortMode 0, overlapCode 3, trisPerLeaf 15, triangleLimit 0, broadphaseLimit 0xffffffff, poseEpsilon 1e-6f, boundsEpsilon 0.01f, areaEpsilon 1e-6f, contactEpsilon -1.0f, contactCutoff -1.0f, tolerance 0.0f, pointSize 0.0f, maxLocalDepthMode DISABLED and all three times 0.0. Both backends produce identical values.

This is the Kit product default table, ClashDetection.DEFAULT_SETTINGS in the omni.physx.clashdetection.core extension. A fresh context holds exactly these values, because ovclash_create_context() seeds it from this function. The settings of a fresh context and a reset struct therefore agree field for field. This function touches no context.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through settings.

Parameters:

settings – [out] Struct to fill. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if settings is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_duplicate_mesh_data(
ovclash_duplicate_mesh_data_t *data,
)#

Clears a duplicate-mesh record to a defined empty state.

Sets both name views to {null, 0} and zeroes meshHash0, meshHash1, clashHash, nbTris and time. Identical in both backends. The name views are borrowed from a context, so this only drops the views and never frees anything.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through data.

Parameters:

data – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if data is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_depth_data(ovclash_depth_data_t *data)#

Clears a depth record, setting maxLocalDepth to -1.0f (“not computed”).

Identical in both backends. No entry point in this header consumes or produces an ovclash_depth_data_t: ovclash_compute_max_local_depth() writes a bare float. This helper therefore serves a struct that the ABI does not otherwise use.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through data.

Parameters:

data – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if data is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_depenetration_data(
ovclash_depenetration_data_t *data,
)#

Clears a depenetration record: dir to (0,0,0) and depth to -1.0f (“not computed”).

Identical in both backends. No entry point in this header consumes or produces an ovclash_depenetration_data_t: ovclash_depenetrate_meshes() and ovclash_imm_depenetrate_meshes() write an ovclash_float3_t displacement. This helper therefore serves a struct that the ABI does not otherwise use.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through data.

Parameters:

data – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if data is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_overlap_data(
ovclash_overlap_data_t *data,
)#

Clears an overlap record to a defined empty state.

Clears both name views and all three hashes, and zeroes nbRecords, nbElements, time and minDistance. Sets maxLocalDepth to -1.0f (“not computed”) and type to OVCLASH_OVERLAP_PAIR_TYPE_UNDEFINED (0x7fffffff, not zero). Identical in both backends. Call this before ovclash_get_overlap_data(). That function leaves *data untouched when it fails, so a struct that was not reset cannot be told apart from a filled one.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through data.

Parameters:

data – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if data is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_step_data(ovclash_step_data_t *data)#

Clears a pipeline step record.

Sets name to {null, 0}, stepIndex and nbSteps to 0, progress and stepProgress to 0.0f, and finished to true. The cleared state therefore reads as “finished”, not “not started”, so finished must not be used as an initialized-or-not test. Identical in both backends.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through data.

Parameters:

data – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if data is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_stats(ovclash_stats_t *stats)#

Zeroes a query-statistics record (meshes, shared meshes, cooked meshes, point clouds).

Identical in both backends. It is only a struct initializer and clears no counter held by a context. ovclash_reset_context() does that.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through stats.

Parameters:

stats – [out] Record to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if stats is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_overlap_report(
ovclash_overlap_report_t *report,
)#

Clears an overlap-report view without releasing anything.

Zeroes the four counts and pointSize0 and nulls the four buffer pointers. It never frees memory, which means different things on the two backends. On OpenUSD the engine allocates the buffers, and only ovclash_release_overlap_report() frees them. Calling this on a filled report leaks them, and releasing the context does not free them either. On ovstage the context owns the buffers and the report only borrows them, so dropping the view is harmless. Use this function to initialize a report before ovclash_create_overlap_report().

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently; writes only through report.

Parameters:

report – [out] Report view to clear. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if report is null (nothing written).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_create_context(
ovclash_context_t **out_context,
)#

Creates a clash context, the owner of settings, scope, results and error text.

The OpenUSD backend bootstraps Carbonite before it creates the engine instance, because report creation dereferences the cached tasking interface. The ovstage backend initializes Carbonite lazily, when a phase needs parallel work with the new task manager. Both backends seed a fresh context from ovclash_reset_settings(). OpenUSD pushes that table through ovclash_set_settings(); ovstage calls it from the context constructor. A fresh context therefore holds exactly the ovclash_reset_settings() table. In particular, OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_SINGLE_THREADED is off and OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_NEW_TASK_MANAGER is on.

Note

Lifetime: releasing the context invalidates its borrowed views, async handles and results. Release every overlap report first; OpenUSD report buffers require explicit release and are not reclaimed with the context.

Note

Threading: drive one context from one thread at a time. On ovstage, independent contexts may be created and used concurrently. On the OpenUSD parity backend they may not: cancellation and the out-of-memory condition are process-global there (see ovclash_cancel_pipeline and ovclash_is_out_of_memory), so concurrent contexts interfere and must be serialized. That backend also shares one process-wide Carbonite bootstrap, which the first context creates and which lasts for the process.

Parameters:

out_context – [out] Receives the new context. Must not be null; free with ovclash_release_context().

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success. OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if out_context is null, the Carbonite bootstrap fails (OpenUSD) or an allocation fails. On failure *out_context is left untouched, so initialize it to null before calling.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_release_context(ovclash_context_t *context)#

Destroys a context and everything it owns.

A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR. While an async pipeline handle is outstanding, the call blocks until the run completes. The OpenUSD backend finishes the run and frees the handle; the ovstage backend joins the worker thread in the context destructor. A release therefore never races a running pipeline, but it can block for the rest of the run. The OpenUSD backend also removes the stage of the context from the standalone stage registry and keeps the process-wide Carbonite bootstrap. Releasing any OpenUSD context also clears the process-global cancellation and out-of-memory flags of that backend, including for runs of other contexts.

Note

Errors: the status is the only signal &#8212; after the call there is no context left to query.

Note

Lifetime: invalidates every borrowed string view, async handle and result of this context. On the OpenUSD backend this call does NOT free overlap-report buffers. Call ovclash_release_overlap_report() for each report first, or the memory is lost.

Note

Threading: no other call on this context may be in flight.

Parameters:

context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(), or null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_reset_context(ovclash_context_t *context)#

Drops all results while keeping the context, its settings, scope, opened stage and built pipeline.

Both backends release meshes, cooked data, the BVH, broadphase pairs, overlaps, duplicates and statistics, and clear the out-of-memory and cancelled flags. ovstage also resets its completed-step counter and drops the populated ovstage scene, which the next pipeline run repopulates from the stored stage path. ovstage also releases a stage borrowed with ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage. Such a stage has no stored path, so attach it again before the next run. Neither backend resets settings, scope paths or the opened stage; use ovclash_set_settings() and ovclash_set_scope*() for that. The call is rejected while an async pipeline handle is active.

Note

Errors: rejection records text for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only; a successful call to this function preserves it).

Note

Lifetime: invalidates every string view, overlap index and report obtained from earlier results. OpenUSD report buffers still need their own ovclash_release_overlap_report().

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or the call is rejected.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_settings(
ovclash_context_t *context,
const ovclash_settings_t *settings,
)#

Applies a whole settings struct at once, equivalent to calling every individual setter.

Both backends apply the same validation. poseEpsilon, boundsEpsilon, areaEpsilon, contactEpsilon, contactCutoff, tolerance, pointSize, startTime, endTime and timeCodesPerSecond must be finite. timeCodesPerSecond must be >= 0, trisPerLeaf in 1..15 (PhysX itself validates the BVH34 leaf count against [2,15]) and maxLocalDepthMode <= HIGH. On a violation nothing is stored and the call fails. The OpenUSD backend then applies the struct through the individual engine setters. Both backends clamp nbTasks to 256. Both also clear any scope paths set earlier; the OpenUSD path goes through setFullScene(), which releases them whatever the flag value.

Note

Errors: an active async handle or a validation failure records its reason for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky); null arguments record nothing.

Note

Results: changing settings neither recomputes nor discards completed results. The threading settings also govern later report extraction, so they can change after the pipeline finishes and before fetching. Finish an active async handle first.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). Must not be null.

  • settings – [in] Settings to apply. Must not be null; the struct is copied.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success. OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if context or settings is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or validation fails (both backends).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_log(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Enables the backend’s per-phase timing/progress logging to stdout.

Both backends honor the flag and write with printf to stdout. There is no log callback and no way to redirect the output. Default on a fresh context: disabled. The backends emit different text (”–Serial: …” and “–ovstage: …”), so the output is not a stable format.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero enables logging.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_coplanar(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Controls whether coplanar triangle pairs count as overlaps.

Both backends map this onto the PhysX mesh-mesh query flags. Enabled selects PxMeshMeshQueryFlag::eDEFAULT. Disabled adds eDISCARD_COPLANAR, so coplanar faces that touch exactly are ignored. Default on a fresh context: enabled.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero keeps coplanar contacts; zero discards them.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_any_hit(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Stops each mesh pair at the first colliding triangle instead of enumerating all of them.

Both backends force the per-pair triangle result limit to 1, which overrides ovclash_set_triangle_limit(). Overlaps are still reported, but nbElements and the face and outline report buffers then hold one representative hit. Derived values such as maxLocalDepth come from that one pair only. Default on a fresh context: disabled.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero enables any-hit (first-hit) mode.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_quantized(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Selects the quantized BVH34 midphase when cooking triangle meshes.

Both backends set PxCookingParams::midphaseDesc.mBVH34Desc.quantized. Quantized trees use less memory at some cost in accuracy and speed. Default on a fresh context: disabled. The cooking phase reads the value, so it only affects meshes cooked by the next pipeline run.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero cooks quantized midphase trees.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_tight_bounds(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Requests tight (rotated-mesh-aware) world bounds instead of cheap loose bounds.

Both backends map this to PxMeshGeometryFlag::eTIGHT_BOUNDS when they compute per-mesh world bounds. Tight bounds shrink the broadphase candidate set for rotated meshes, at some extra cost in bounds computation. Default on a fresh context: enabled. The value is read while bounds are computed, so it applies from the next pipeline run.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero enables tight bounds.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_subcomponent_filtering(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Skips clash pairs whose two prims belong to the same USD subcomponent.

Both backends drop a broadphase pair when the two meshes resolve to the same subcomponent root prim, so parts of one assembly do not clash with each other. Two meshes outside any subcomponent resolve to the same empty root and are dropped too. Enabling the filter therefore suppresses every pair between meshes that sit outside any subcomponent.

OpenUSD resolves the root with UsdUtils::getSubComponentRoot() behind SUPPORT_EXPERIMENTAL_FILTERING, which the ovclash build turns on by default. ovstage resolves the nearest ancestor with kind = "subcomponent" from the composed model kinds that it populates from the opened file. Kinds authored in referenced, sublayered or binary layers, or in a selected variant, therefore count as they do on OpenUSD. A mesh of an instanced asset resolves per placement, like an OpenUSD instance proxy: from the asset content up through its instance root and the ancestors of that root. A stage attached with ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage() is read as its owner populated it. When the owner population holds no kind (or usd-metadata:kind) values, every mesh resolves to the empty root, and enabling the filter drops every pair.

Default on a fresh context: disabled. Applies from the next pipeline run. On ovstage, a call between the steps of a run leaves the rest of that run unchanged, because ovstage fixes the value when the run selects meshes. OpenUSD applies it to the remaining steps of the run.

Note

Errors: a null context is reported through the status and records no text anywhere; while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only). A successful call to this function leaves that message unchanged.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero enables subcomponent filtering.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_use_usdrt(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Stores the USDRT flag, which selects nothing in either ovclash backend.

In the Kit extension this bit selects the USDRT/Fabric stage traversal. In ovclash it is inert. The only reader on the OpenUSD path sits inside #if !defined(OVCLASH_STANDALONE) and is compiled out. The ovstage backend has no second traversal to switch to, because ovstage population is its only scene path, so the flag has no reader there at all. Toggling it produces byte-identical results on both backends. Default on a fresh context: enabled. The flag remains because it belongs to the Kit-compatible settings table that persisted query settings serialize. ovclash_get_settings() reports the stored bit, so the only observable effects are that read-back and the serialized text, never the clash results.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Stored in the settings bitmask; otherwise ignored.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_single_threaded(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Forces serial execution of the clash phases.

Both backends honor it. On OpenUSD it feeds MultithreadParams::mSingleThreaded, and multi-threaded detection also requires the Carbonite tasking interface. On ovstage it overrides both task managers: geometry preparation, mesh cooking, pose and bounds computation, broad phase and narrow phase run serially. It also turns off sampled-matrix prefetch and the numeric-population helper thread described below.

With the flag off, ovclash_set_new_task_manager() selects Carbonite tasking or bounded std::thread workers on ovstage. Eligible dynamic playback can then prepare a future matrix window while collision work reads the current one. Source updates and numeric composition stay sequential, with one source owner at a time. The one exception is a file-backed static run: it can open its numeric transform population on one helper std::thread while mesh selection keeps extracting geometry. Neither task manager nor ovclash_set_nb_tasks() governs that thread. The thread holds the process-wide ovstage lifecycle gate for the population. It is joined before those transforms are read and before the selection is replaced, reset or released.

On ovstage, pairs are tested independently, and their overlaps are sorted back into canonical mesh-path order after parallel collection. Counts, membership, per-pair data and even the ovclash_get_overlap_data() index order are therefore identical to a single-threaded run. Default on a fresh context: disabled on both backends, as in the Kit product table (SETTING_SINGLE_THREADED: False). A standalone OpenUSD caller that hits instability in the carb-tasking paths of the engine can turn it on. The flag also makes later report extraction run serially. It can change after detection finishes, without rerunning the pipeline or discarding its results.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero forces serial execution.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_new_task_manager(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Selects the task-manager implementation for multi-threaded phases.

On ovstage, true selects the statically linked Carbonite tasking for geometry preparation, mesh cooking, pose and bounds computation, broad phase, narrow phase and eligible sampled-matrix prefetch. It uses the worker budget of the scheduler and ignores ovclash_set_nb_tasks(). False selects std::thread workers bounded by the task count, the hardware concurrency and the available work (see ovclash_set_nb_tasks()). ovclash_set_single_threaded() overrides either choice. Carbonite initializes lazily when parallel work is needed. When initialization fails, the phase fails with context error text and no other scheduler is selected. Default on a fresh context: enabled.

On OpenUSD, MultithreadParams::mUseNewTaskManager chooses between the two broadphase and narrowphase task managers of the engine. Both detection managers use Carbonite. Standalone report extraction uses Carbonite when the flag is true and bounded std::thread workers when it is false. Changing the flag after detection affects later extraction without recomputing the results.

Note

Results: the flag selects an implementation, not a policy. It does not change WHICH pairs overlap or what is reported about them. ovstage keeps the same ordered reports under either manager. On OpenUSD the newer manager hands pairs to workers from a shared counter, so the ovclash_get_overlap_data() index order depends on the run, and repeated runs at identical settings can differ. Index order is never part of the contract (see ovclash_get_overlap_data); this setting is the one most likely to show that.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero selects the newer task manager.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_purge_permanent_dynamic_overlaps(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Drops overlaps that are present in every sampled frame of a time-sampled query.

Hides pairs that interpenetrate permanently, such as modelling artifacts, rather than clashing because of motion. Both backends honor it, and it affects only dynamic (time-sampled) queries; see ovclash_set_times(). ovstage removes any accumulated overlap whose record count equals the sampled frame count. Default on a fresh context: disabled.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero purges permanently-overlapping dynamic pairs.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_purge_permanent_static_overlaps(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Drops overlaps between two transform-static meshes during a time-sampled query.

Both backends honor it. A dynamic (time-sampled) run classifies each mesh as static or animated, and suppresses pairs whose two sides are static. Classification follows active authored transform animation on the prim or its ancestors. Several effective samples can mark a prim animated even when every sampled value is identical. A single sample is not animation by itself. When ovstage cannot resolve the initial value of an active operation, the mesh stays conservatively non-static, unless another active operation proves it animated. The sampled fallback validates numeric matrices and may cache them, but derives no animation flag from pose equality or text-layer hints. Only conclusive raw static flags allow static-pair suppression or freezing a future pose. Because of this conservative rule, ovstage does not claim full authored-animation parity for every composed input. The flag has no effect on a static (startTime == endTime) query. Default on a fresh context: enabled.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero purges static-vs-static pairs in dynamic runs.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_compute_max_local_depth(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_max_local_depth_mode_t mode,
)#

Selects how (and whether) maximum local penetration depth is computed per overlap.

Valid values are the four ovclash_max_local_depth_mode_t enumerators, in increasing cost:

  • DISABLED computes no depth, so a mesh-vs-mesh overlap_data.maxLocalDepth stays -1.0f (see the point-vs-mesh note below);

  • MINIMAL is the original fast estimate;

  • MEDIUM and HIGH refine the estimate, and HIGH adds 64 sampling directions.

Both backends implement all four modes. Both use contactEpsilon and contactCutoff to bound the refinement and, while depth computation is on, to cull overlaps shallower than contactEpsilon. Default on a fresh context: DISABLED. A mode greater than OVCLASH_MAX_LOCAL_DEPTH_MODE_HIGH is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous mode stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

The setting is mesh-only. A point-vs-mesh overlap reports maxLocalDepth 0.0f in every mode, DISABLED included, and never the -1.0f “not computed” value. A 0.0f on a point-cloud overlap is therefore not a measured zero-depth contact.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when mode is greater than OVCLASH_MAX_LOCAL_DEPTH_MODE_HIGH, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous mode in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • mode – [in] One of the ovclash_max_local_depth_mode_t enumerators.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or mode is greater than OVCLASH_MAX_LOCAL_DEPTH_MODE_HIGH (nothing is stored, the previous mode stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_nb_tasks(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t nbTasks,
)#

Sets how many worker tasks the multi-threaded phases split their work into.

Both backends clamp the value to 256 (MultiThreader::MaxNbTasks and kMaxNbTasks); 0 is accepted. On ovstage the value controls only the std::thread manager (ovclash_set_new_task_manager(false)). The parallel mesh preparation and collision phases then use at most min(max(nbTasks, 1), hardware concurrency, available work) workers. An unknown hardware concurrency counts as one. A running sampled-matrix prefetch callback reserves one slot of the std::thread budget; keeping its completed window reserves none.

In OpenUSD detection the value controls only the task split of the legacy Carbonite manager. There 0 selects one task when work is available, while the stored and read-back setting stays 0. An empty work range schedules no tasks. Standalone OpenUSD report extraction bounds its std::thread workers with the same formula as ovstage, where 0 selects one worker. Both backends ignore the value while single-threaded mode or the new task manager is on; the new manager uses the worker budget of the Carbonite scheduler. Default on a fresh context: 128, stored but unused by the default new-manager configuration.

Note

Results: the task count is a performance knob only. It changes neither which pairs overlap nor what is reported about them. ovstage collects parallel results without per-pair slots and restores canonical mesh-path order before reporting. The OpenUSD legacy manager concatenates contiguous task slices. Changing the value therefore keeps the serial order wherever the value applies. The OpenUSD new manager ignores it and keeps its run-dependent order.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • nbTasks – [in] Desired task count; silently clamped to 256.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_pose_epsilon(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float epsilon,
)#

Tolerance used when comparing two world transforms for equality.

Both backends use it in the same places: detecting shared/instanced meshes with identical poses, deciding that a mesh pair is a duplicate rather than a clash, and short-circuiting the immediate-mode depth queries when both matrices are the same. Units are those of the matrix components (stage units for translation), compared per element. Default on a fresh context: 1e-6f. A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when epsilon is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • epsilon – [in] Per-component comparison tolerance. Negative values make the comparison never match.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or epsilon is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_bounds_epsilon(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float epsilon,
)#

Inflation applied when computing each mesh’s world bounds.

Both backends pass it to PxGeometryQuery::computeGeomBounds as both the additive offset (stage/world units) and the scale factor 1 + epsilon. Nonnegative values widen the broadphase and can only add candidate pairs; the narrow phase still decides. Finite negative values are accepted and can shrink bounds, so that monotonicity guarantee does not apply. Default on a fresh context: 0.01f. A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when epsilon is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • epsilon – [in] Bounds inflation in stage units; 0 disables inflation.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or epsilon is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_area_epsilon(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float epsilon,
)#

Minimum triangle area kept during mesh cooking; smaller triangles are discarded.

Both backends pass it to PxCookingParams::meshAreaMinLimit, so the unit is squared stage units and 0 disables the filter. Discarded triangles never appear in results, so a larger value both speeds up cooking and hides slivers. The cooking phase reads the value, so it applies to meshes cooked by the next pipeline run, not to meshes already cooked. Default on a fresh context: 1e-6f. A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when epsilon is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • epsilon – [in] Minimum triangle area in squared stage units; 0 keeps all triangles.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or epsilon is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_contact_epsilon(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float value,
)#

Minimum penetration depth for an overlap to be reported, in stage units.

Active only while max-local-depth computation is enabled (see ovclash_set_compute_max_local_depth); with depth disabled the value is ignored. Both backends behave identically. A negative value disables the feature: no culling and no depth cutoff. Otherwise overlaps whose computed maxLocalDepth is below the value are dropped, and the value serves as the minimum-depth cutoff of the refinement. Default on a fresh context: -1.0f (disabled). A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when value is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • value – [in] Minimum depth in stage units; any negative value disables culling.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or value is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_contact_cutoff(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float value,
)#

Upper depth cutoff for the refined max-local-depth search, in stage units.

Both backends use it identically, and only in the refined depth path. It is the maximum-depth cutoff while contactEpsilon-based culling is active (contactEpsilon >= 0) and the max-local-depth mode is above MINIMAL. A negative value leaves the cutoff unset. The setting is ignored while contactEpsilon is negative or depth computation is disabled. Default on a fresh context: -1.0f. A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when value is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Parameters:

  • value – [in] Maximum depth in stage units; negative leaves the cutoff unset.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or value is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_tolerance(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float value,
)#

Clearance distance, in stage units: prims closer than this count as clashing.

Both backends inflate broadphase bounds by the tolerance and pass it to the PhysX mesh-mesh queries, so a positive value reports mesh near-misses as overlaps. The point-vs-mesh narrow phase ignores it on both backends, so near-miss points are not reported. Both backends clamp a negative value to 0; there is no “shrink” mode. Default on a fresh context: 0.0f (touching geometry only). A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error().

Parameters:

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or value is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_sort_mode(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t mode,
)#

Selects the sort key stored with each overlap, and whether duplicate triangles are counted.

The backends differ sharply. On OpenUSD the value picks the per-overlap sort key: 0 = number of overlapping elements, 1 = internal narrow-phase cost, 2 = max local depth. Any other value leaves the key at 0. 0xffffffff also suppresses the duplicate-mesh triangle count, so nbTris reads 0. On ovstage only the 0xffffffff case exists: it zeroes duplicate nbTris, and no other value changes anything. Neither backend validates the value. Default on a fresh context: 0.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • mode – [in] 0, 1, 2 or 0xffffffff. Other values leave OpenUSD’s sort key at zero; on ovstage only 0xffffffff changes behavior.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_overlap_code(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t code,
)#

Chooses which triangle-triangle intersection kernel PhysX uses.

Both backends map the value identically onto PxMeshMeshQueryFlag: 0 = the regular kernel, 1 = eRESERVED1 (Moller variant), 2 = eRESERVED2 (SAT), 3 = eRESERVED3 (SIMD SAT). Any other value silently behaves like 0. The kernels differ in speed and can differ marginally in how they classify borderline hits. Default on a fresh context: 3. Neither backend validates the value.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_tris_per_leaf(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t trisPerLeaf,
)#

Number of triangles per BVH34 leaf used when cooking meshes.

Both backends pass it to PxCookingParams::midphaseDesc.mBVH34Desc.numPrimsPerLeaf. Larger leaves cook faster and use less memory; smaller leaves query faster. The cooking phase reads the value, so it applies to meshes cooked by the next pipeline run. Default on a fresh context: 15, which is also the maximum.

The accepted range is 1..15. PhysX validates numPrimsPerLeaf against [2,15], so 15 is a hard ceiling, not a tuning suggestion. A larger value would fail every mesh cook. A failed cook does not fail a pipeline step, so such a run would report success with zero overlaps on a model full of them. Values outside 1..15 are rejected on both backends: nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error(). A value of 1 is accepted and reported back by ovclash_get_settings(). PhysX rejects 1 too, so both backends retry the cook at 15 and build the mesh with 15 triangles per leaf. The reported overlaps do not change; only cooking time and memory do.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when trisPerLeaf is outside 1..15, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • trisPerLeaf – [in] Triangles per leaf; must be in 1..15.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or trisPerLeaf is outside 1..15 (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_triangle_limit(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t limit,
)#

Caps how many colliding triangle pairs are recorded per mesh pair.

Both backends treat 0 as unlimited (internally 0xffffffff), and on both ovclash_set_any_hit() overrides the value with 1. The limit truncates the recorded results, nbElements and the face and outline report buffers. It does not stop a pair from being reported. Default on a fresh context: 0 (unlimited). Neither backend validates the value.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • limit – [in] Maximum triangle pairs per mesh pair; 0 means unlimited.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_broadphase_limit(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t limit,
)#

Caps the number of candidate pairs the broadphase is allowed to produce.

A guard against combinatorial explosion on pathological scenes. Once the broadphase has collected all of its candidate pairs, both backends compare their count against this limit. When the count exceeds it, they cancel the run rather than silently truncate results. The pair array is not bounded while it is collected. Default on a fresh context: 0xffffffff, effectively unlimited. 0 is a real limit, not “unlimited”. Neither backend validates the value.

Note

Errors: the status covers only this call. Exceeding the limit requests cancellation instead of failing the phase that exceeded it. In a static stepped run both backends report success for the broadphase step (index 7). The next step is rejected for pending cancellation and, like every such rejection, records no last-error text. An ovstage time-sampled frame step that exceeds the limit fails itself. The cancellation stays pending, per context on ovstage and process-global on OpenUSD. Later ovclash_run_pipeline_step calls fail, even step 0 of a new pipeline, until ovclash_reset_context clears it (see ovclash_cancel_pipeline). An async run reports it as OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR from ovclash_finish_pipeline, which clears it. While an async handle is active this call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky).

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • limit – [in] Maximum broadphase pair count; 0xffffffff is the practical “no limit” value.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_times(
ovclash_context_t *context,
double startTime,
double endTime,
double timeCodesPerSecond,
)#

Selects a static or time-sampled query and its sample spacing, in seconds.

startTime == endTime selects a single-sample (static) query. Otherwise the run is dynamic: it starts at exactly startTime and adds 1.0/timeCodesPerSecond in double precision until the next time exceeds endTime. There is no endpoint clamp, so rounding may exclude an endpoint that is exact in theory. Both backends disable the duplicate-mesh search for dynamic runs, and use one startTime sample for a zero rate or a descending range. Both backends require all three values to be finite and timeCodesPerSecond >= 0. Otherwise nothing is stored and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error(). Defaults on a fresh context: 0, 0, 0. ovstage also reads “all three zero” as “no times requested”.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when startTime, endTime or timeCodesPerSecond is not finite or timeCodesPerSecond is negative, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous values in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • startTime – [in] First sampled time, in seconds (the USD time code is the value multiplied by the stage’s timeCodesPerSecond).

  • endTime – [in] Sampling endpoint, in seconds; equal to startTime means a static query.

  • timeCodesPerSecond – [in] Samples per second; 0 collapses the run to one sample.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or startTime, endTime or timeCodesPerSecond is not finite or timeCodesPerSecond is negative (nothing is stored, the previous values stand, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_full_scene(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Selects whole-stage traversal instead of a scoped prim set.

Both backends clear any scope paths set earlier, whatever the flag value. OpenUSD does it through ClashDetectionParams::releasePaths(), ovstage through clearScopePaths(). To keep a non-empty explicit scope, call this before ovclash_set_scope() or ovclash_set_scope_paths(). A set scope wins. With no scope and this flag cleared, both standalone backends select nothing at all, because the Kit “current selection” path is compiled out. On both backends ovclash_set_scope_paths() with a non-empty scope also clears this flag; the legacy ovclash_set_scope() does not. Default on a fresh context: enabled.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero traverses the whole stage.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_only_find_duplicates(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Runs duplicate-mesh detection only, skipping clash detection entirely.

Both backends honor it. The OpenUSD narrow phase stops after the duplicate test, and ovstage skips the BVH, broad-phase and narrow-phase steps after its duplicate search. ovclash_get_overlap_count() then reports 0, and only ovclash_get_duplicate_mesh_count() and ovclash_get_duplicated_meshes_data() return anything. Duplicates are pairs of prims with identical mesh data and equal poses (within poseEpsilon). Default on a fresh context: disabled. Both backends turn duplicate detection off for time-sampled runs, so combining this flag with a dynamic ovclash_set_times() yields no results.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero restricts the run to duplicate search.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_ignore_redundant_overlaps(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Suppresses overlaps that merely repeat an already reported identical-geometry pair.

Both backends honor it after the broad phase. They drop pairs whose meshes and relative poses make the contact a repeat of one already recorded, typically instanced or shared geometry laid out identically. Default on a fresh context: disabled. During a time-sampled query that purges permanent static overlaps, identical static copies still share one representative contact. The representative is an actual eligible pair, so scope or subcomponent exclusions do not remove the only remaining contact.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero drops redundant overlaps.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_ignore_invisible_prims(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Excludes invisible prims from mesh and point-cloud selection.

Both backends honor it during scene traversal and population, so invisible prims never reach cooking or the broadphase. Selection reads the value, so a change takes effect on the next pipeline run. Default on a fresh context: enabled, so invisible geometry does not clash by default.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero skips invisible prims.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_point_clouds(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Enables UsdGeomPoints point-cloud vs mesh clash detection.

Both backends implement point-vs-mesh and gate it on this flag; with the flag off, point-cloud prims are not even selected. Results are overlaps of type OVCLASH_OVERLAP_PAIR_TYPE_POINT_VS_MESH. Their element indices are point indices, available through OVCLASH_OVERLAP_REPORT_FLAG_POINTS0. Selection reads the value, so it applies from the next pipeline run. Default on a fresh context: disabled.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero enables point-cloud queries.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_point_clouds_experimental(
ovclash_context_t *context,
bool flag,
)#

Selects the experimental point-cloud narrow-phase implementation.

The backends differ. On OpenUSD the flag picks an alternative multi-threaded point-vs-mesh pipeline, and is ignored unless multi-threading is active (see ovclash_set_single_threaded). On ovstage the bit is stored but never read, so it does nothing. It also matters only while ovclash_set_point_clouds() is enabled. Default on a fresh context: disabled.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • flag – [in] Non-zero selects the experimental path.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_point_size(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float size,
)#

Overrides the point diameter used for point-cloud clash tests, in stage units.

The value is a width (twice the radius), not a radius, and excludes any scaling from the prim transform. Both backends treat a value > 0 as an explicit override for every point, and report it back as ovclash_overlap_report_t::pointSize0. A value <= 0 falls back, in order, to a single authored USD width, to per-point authored widths, or to an automatically derived size. With per-point widths pointSize0 is 0.0 and the caller reads the widths per index. ovstage collapses a uniform per-point array back to its single value, where the OpenUSD parity backend reports 0.0. The value matters only while ovclash_set_point_clouds() is enabled. Default on a fresh context: 0.0f. A non-finite value is rejected on both backends: nothing is stored and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error(). A call between the steps of a run changes the size that ovstage tests and reports from the next sample of that run on. OpenUSD keeps the size it computed before the first sample of the run.

Note

Errors: while an async pipeline handle is active, or when size is not finite, the call is rejected and text is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error() (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only, sticky). A rejected call stores nothing and leaves the previous value in place. A null context is reported through the status alone and records no text.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). A null context returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • size – [in] Point width in stage units; <= 0 restores automatic sizing.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null, an async pipeline handle is active, or size is not finite (nothing is stored, the previous value stands, and the reason is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error()).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_scope(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint64_t stageId,
const uint64_t *paths1,
uint32_t nbPaths1,
const uint64_t *paths2,
uint32_t nbPaths2,
)#

Replaces the query scope using encoded absolute prim paths.

This is the legacy low-level counterpart of ovclash_set_scope_paths(). Every path value must come from ovclash_sdf_path_to_int(). With both arrays empty the engine falls back to OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE, which is enabled on a fresh context; with the flag cleared, nothing is selected. With only paths1 populated the query searches that set. With both populated it searches paths1 against paths2. The arrays are resolved and copied during this call.

The backends handle stageId differently. OpenUSD resolves the stage from the standalone process registry. It reports an invalid id through the engine error callback, but the legacy C wrapper does not propagate that failure. The id is resolved during this call only. When nothing is registered under it at that moment, pipeline steps, an async run and both immediate queries fail with “no stage is open”. They keep failing even after a stage is registered under that id, until ovclash_open_stage, ovclash_set_scope_paths() or another ovclash_set_scope() call supplies a stage. ovstage ignores stageId and uses the stage already opened on context. Standalone callers should prefer ovclash_set_scope_paths(), which supplies the stage identity of the context and validates UTF-8 paths directly.

Note

Preconditions: paths2 without paths1 is not a documented scope shape.

Note

Side effects: replaces the context’s previous scope. On ovstage, validation completes before replacement, so a rejected request preserves the previous scope.

Note

Lifetime: context copies the scope; the caller retains ownership of both arrays and may release them after this function returns.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context(). Must not be null.

  • stageId – [in] OpenUSD standalone stage-registry id; ignored by ovstage.

  • paths1 – [in] First encoded-path array, or null when nbPaths1 is zero.

  • nbPaths1 – [in] Number of entries in paths1.

  • paths2 – [in] Second encoded-path array, or null when nbPaths2 is zero.

  • nbPaths2 – [in] Number of entries in paths2.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the request is accepted; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null/invalid, an async pipeline handle is active, an array is null with a non-zero count, or (on ovstage) an encoded id is unknown.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_create_pipeline(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t *out_step_count,
)#

Builds the clash pipeline for the current settings and reports its step count.

A valid context always yields at least 8 steps: 11 for a static query (start time == end time), otherwise 7 plus one step per sampled time, and a sampled range always includes its start time. A successful call therefore never reports “no work to do”. Call ovclash_set_times or ovclash_set_settings first, because the step count derives from startTime, endTime and timeCodesPerSecond. Neither backend checks that a stage is open or a scope is set; those failures surface later from ovclash_run_pipeline_step. OpenUSD rebuilds and stores the concrete phase list and discards any previous one. ovstage builds an immutable timing snapshot and sample-time vector, installs them only after construction succeeds, and resets its completed-step counter to 0. Later changes of the timing settings apply to the next pipeline, not to the installed snapshot. ovstage rejects a dynamic schedule that does not progress, and a step count that does not fit in uint32_t together with the seven fixed phases. An allocation failure may also reject a large schedule. Such a failure keeps the previous pipeline. These safeguards are ovstage-only and leave the OpenUSD engine unchanged.

Note

Errors: the status says only that the call failed. ovclash_get_last_error, which exists only in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds, returns the reason. A null context records no text at all.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context. Rejected while an async handle is live.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Mutated by this call.

  • out_step_count – [out] Receives the number of pipeline steps (>= 8 on success). Left untouched on failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context or out_step_count is null, the context has no engine, an async pipeline handle is live, or a C++ exception was caught.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_step_data_t *data,
uint32_t index,
)#

Describes one planned pipeline step (name, index, count, progress, finished flag).

Describes the plan built by ovclash_create_pipeline, not live progress. Both backends set progress = index / nbSteps, stepProgress = 0.0f and finished = (index == nbSteps - 1). For live progress during an async run, use ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data_async. On failure *data is left completely untouched, so check the returned status.

Note

Lifetime: data->name borrows a static, library-owned string literal that is valid for the process lifetime; it is never freed and is not invalidated by later calls.

Note

Threading: serialize on one context. Rejected while an async handle is live.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context that owns a pipeline created by ovclash_create_pipeline.

  • data – [out] Receives the step description. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based step index, in [0, step count from ovclash_create_pipeline() - 1].

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when data or context is null, the context has no engine, an async handle is live, no pipeline has been created, or index is out of range.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_run_pipeline_step(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t index,
)#

Runs one pipeline step synchronously on the calling thread.

Steps carry state and must run in ascending order 0..count-1. A run out of order is not diagnosed. Both backends execute each non-final step by index against whatever state exists. The final ovstage step reports success without doing the work when the preceding steps have not completed. OpenUSD reports OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS as soon as it has invoked the phase function. Per-phase failures are invisible here, so check ovclash_is_out_of_memory and the result counts. ovstage reports OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when the phase itself fails, and records the reason as the last error of the context.

Note

Errors: ovclash_get_last_error (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only) carries ovstage phase failures. On ovstage, a rejected index (out of range, or before ovclash_create_pipeline) records its own text; OpenUSD records none for it. A rejection for pending cancellation records nothing on either backend. It is not a misuse, and the last-error string stays unchanged across it. On ovstage, a failure while a sampled frame runs discards its current and accumulated overlaps. Restart at step 0 before treating results as a complete query. After a stage replacement during a started pipeline, both backends reject nonzero steps with “stage changed; restart the pipeline at step 0”. The rejection lasts until step 0 restarts execution, an async run starts the pipeline again, or ovclash_create_pipeline installs a new pipeline.

Note

Lifetime: release overlap reports before advancing to another step. Sampled ovstage steps can replace borrowed result buffers, even within the same pipeline run.

Note

Lifetime: on ovstage, index 0 clears the last error of the context, so a message read after a run belongs to that run. That makes the report of a successful run, described on ovclash_get_last_error, safe to attribute; see also ovclash_stats_t::nbCookedMeshes.

Note

Threading: serialize on one context; the step itself may fan out to internal worker tasks.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context with a pipeline created by ovclash_create_pipeline.

  • index – [in] Zero-based step index in [0, step count from ovclash_create_pipeline() - 1].

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the step ran (see caveat above), or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or has no engine, an async handle is live, index is out of range, a nonzero step follows a stage replacement in a started pipeline, cancellation is pending, no stage is open (OpenUSD rejects every step of a created pipeline, ovstage the first step that reads the stage), or (OpenUSD) the process-global out-of-memory flag is set. No stage is open before ovclash_open_stage succeeds and after a failed ovclash_open_stage drops the previous one. On ovstage, a successful ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage also opens one, and ovclash_ovstage_detach_stage or ovclash_reset_context of an attached stage leaves none.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_run_pipeline_async(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_async_t **out_async,
)#

Starts the prepared pipeline on a background worker and returns an async handle.

At most one async handle exists per context; a second call while one is live is rejected. While a handle is live, almost every other context entry point (settings setters, scope, stepping, result getters, reset) is rejected with “not allowed while an async pipeline handle is active”. OpenUSD immediately starts a run of the phase list on the PhysX task manager. ovstage starts the whole pipeline on a std::thread, without an intentional startup delay. A call without ovclash_create_pipeline is not an error on either backend: the worker performs no work and reports success.

On ovstage, the worker runs with a snapshot, taken at launch, of the floating-point controls of the calling thread: rounding, denormal handling and exception masks. Later changes on the calling thread do not affect that run. Launch and finish keep the controls of the caller. The worker restores its own previous controls on every exit, cancellation and failure included.

Note

Lifetime: there is no ovclash_async_destroy. ovclash_finish_pipeline destroys the handle, and the pointer dangles after it returns. ovclash_release_context also reclaims a live handle: OpenUSD finishes it first, ovstage joins the worker. ovclash_reset_context is rejected while a handle is live.

Note

Threading: until the run is finished, poll only through ovclash_is_pipeline_running, ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data_async, ovclash_async_is_cancelled and ovclash_cancel_pipeline. On ovstage the worker also writes the last-error string of the context. The access is synchronized, but which message ovclash_get_last_error returns during the run is nondeterministic. On OpenUSD, while the worker runs, these calls access the volatile process-global cancel flag and the unsynchronized progress state of the shared engine. That gives no C++ thread-safety guarantee; see the note of each call.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context to run. Mutated by the worker thread until the pipeline finishes.

  • out_async – [out] Receives the owned async handle. Left untouched on failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context or out_async is null, the context has no engine, a handle is already live, (OpenUSD) a created pipeline would run with no stage open, the engine failed to start the run, or a C++ exception was caught. ovstage launches without a stage and ovclash_finish_pipeline then reports it missing.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_is_pipeline_running(
ovclash_async_t *async,
bool *out_running,
)#

Polls whether the asynchronous pipeline is still executing.

Both backends report not-running as soon as cancellation is requested, before the worker has actually stopped. Do not use the answer to decide that the handle is safe to drop. ovclash_finish_pipeline is the only call that joins the worker and releases the handle, and it must be called on both backends either way.

Without cancellation the contract is the same on both backends. It concerns convergence, not any single reading: poll until the call reports false; once it does, it stays false. Finish the handle before reading results, because the live-handle guard stays closed until ovclash_finish_pipeline returns. Do not assume a value from the first poll. A small fixture can complete before the first poll, so expecting either “running” or “not running” there is a race. This holds even when ovclash_create_pipeline was never called, because the call still starts a zero-work run. The backends reach the answer differently: ovstage reads its own worker flag, and OpenUSD asks the engine whether results are available. That is mechanism, not contract.

Do not derive the answer from the finished flag of ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data_async.
