That flag means “this is the last step index”, so it turns true when the final step starts, not when the run completes. On OpenUSD an empty handle reports finished while this call still reports running. Treating finished as done would read results before the worker published them.

Note

Lifetime: async must not have been passed to ovclash_finish_pipeline yet; the handle is destroyed there and polling afterwards is a use-after-free.

Note

Errors: a null handle is reported through the status alone and records no error text, because the owning context is unreachable through it.

Note

Threading: may be polled from another thread while the worker runs, but not concurrently with or after ovclash_finish_pipeline on the same handle. ovstage reads atomic flags. OpenUSD reads the shared engine’s volatile process-global cancel flag, which provides no C++ thread-safety guarantee, and then tests the engine’s completion event.

Parameters:

  • async – [in] Handle from ovclash_run_pipeline_async. Must not be null.

  • out_running – [out] Receives true while the run is considered active; false when it has completed or as soon as cancellation was requested. Left untouched on failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when async or out_running is null.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data_async(
ovclash_async_t *async,
ovclash_step_data_t *data,
)#

Snapshots live step/progress information from a running asynchronous pipeline.

Both backends refine progress with the counted work of the current step. OpenUSD uses the work-item counter of the shared engine. ovstage snapshots per-context operation labels and counted work under a mutex. stepProgress advances through reserved portions of the step, and progress includes that fraction. Opaque operations report a label without estimating completion. ovstage async names may append the current operation to the canonical phase name; synchronous plan names stay unchanged. Neither fractional progress nor an operation label is a time estimate. Before ovclash_create_pipeline, ovstage clears data through ovclash_reset_step_data, which sets finished to true rather than zero-filling it. A poll made before the pipeline exists therefore reports a finished step. As on ovclash_reset_step_data, finished is no test of whether the record is initialized.

Note

Errors: with a null handle the owning context is unreachable, so not even ovclash_get_last_error (OVCLASH_STANDALONE only) shows anything. *data is left untouched, and the status is the only signal.

Note

Lifetime: data->name borrows a static library-owned literal valid for the process lifetime. The handle must not already have been passed to ovclash_finish_pipeline.

Note

Threading: never call it concurrently with or after ovclash_finish_pipeline on the same handle. ovstage supports polling while its worker runs, and reports a locked snapshot clamped to the counted work. OpenUSD still reads the shared-engine progress without synchronization. Its mutex-protected copy of the step record does not make polling fully safe. A poll that races the work-counter reset of a phase can briefly report progress or stepProgress outside [0.0, 1.0], or non-finite. Consumers clamp the values and treat a non-finite value as unknown. Clash results are unaffected.

Parameters:

  • async – [in] Handle from ovclash_run_pipeline_async. A null handle returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

  • data – [out] Receives the current step snapshot. A null pointer returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when async or data is null.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_finish_pipeline(ovclash_async_t *async)#

Waits for the asynchronous pipeline to complete and destroys the async handle.

Call it exactly once per handle, also after ovclash_cancel_pipeline: cancel only requests a stop and never joins or frees. On return the cancel flag is cleared, the process-global one on OpenUSD and the per-context one on ovstage. The active-async slot of the context is released, which enables the rest of the API again. OpenUSD maps the fetch status of the task system to the result: OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS means the worker was joined cleanly, and per-phase detection failures are invisible here. ovstage maps the success flag of its worker to the result, and reports OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when a pipeline phase failed. Both backends also report OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when cancellation was requested before finish, even after the worker completed, and even for a zero-work run without a created pipeline. The stop that the engine requests itself when the broadphase limit is exceeded counts as cancellation, whether or not the caller polled ovclash_is_pipeline_running first. A failed ovstage sampled frame discards the current and accumulated overlaps, as described on ovclash_run_pipeline_step. Start a new run before treating results as a complete query.

Note

Lifetime: the handle is freed here. Any later use, including a second ovclash_finish_pipeline, ovclash_is_pipeline_running or ovclash_cancel_pipeline, is a use-after-free. Set the caller’s pointer to null right away.

Note

Threading: blocks the calling thread until the worker exits; call it from one thread only.

Parameters:

async – [in] Handle from ovclash_run_pipeline_async. May be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the run completed, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when async is null, the worker reported failure, or cancellation was requested (including by the broadphase limit). An uncancelled zero-work run without a created pipeline succeeds. For a valid handle, even an error outcome joins the worker, frees the handle and leaves the context reusable, so the status never means “finishing failed”.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_cancel_pipeline(ovclash_async_t *async)#

Requests cancellation of a running asynchronous pipeline.

Returns immediately. It neither joins the worker nor frees the handle, so the caller must still call ovclash_finish_pipeline afterwards. The scope of the request differs by backend. OpenUSD sets a process-global volatile flag that aborts every in-flight pipeline in the process; ovstage sets a per-context atomic. On both backends a set flag also makes later ovclash_run_pipeline_step calls fail, on OpenUSD for every context in the process. ovclash_finish_pipeline or ovclash_reset_context clears the flag. On OpenUSD, ovclash_release_context of any context clears it too.

Note

Errors: with a null handle no error text is recorded either, because the owning context is unreachable; the status is the only signal.

Note

Lifetime: async must not already have been passed to ovclash_finish_pipeline.

Note

Threading: may be called from another thread while the worker runs, but not concurrently with or after ovclash_finish_pipeline on the same handle. It cannot interrupt a finish already in progress, so cancel first, then finish. ovstage sets an atomic per-context flag. OpenUSD writes the volatile process-global flag of the shared engine, which worker threads read without synchronization; that gives no C++ thread-safety guarantee.

Parameters:

async – [in] Handle from ovclash_run_pipeline_async. A null handle returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when async is null.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_duplicate_mesh_count(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t *out_count,
)#

Returns the number of duplicate mesh pairs found by the last pipeline run.

Duplicates are pairs of meshes with identical mesh data at equal poses (within poseEpsilon); see ovclash_set_only_find_duplicates. The count is 0 before any run. A query interrupted by cancellation can return 0 with OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, and on OpenUSD so can a native out-of-memory. Zero therefore does not by itself mean “no duplicates”. Cancellation requested after completion does not erase the results produced. For async runs, check the finish outcome, and note the cancellation state before finish clears the flag and consumes the handle. On ovstage, a stage replacement or a direct mesh-selection step can keep this aggregate count while its table-indexed details turn stale; ovclash_get_duplicated_meshes_data then fails.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • out_count – [out] Receives the duplicate-pair count. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if context or out_count is null, or an async pipeline handle is still active on this context.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_duplicated_meshes_data(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_duplicate_mesh_data_t *data,
uint32_t index,
)#

Reads names, hashes, triangle count and time for one duplicate mesh pair.

index must be < ovclash_get_duplicate_mesh_count. For a genuine duplicate pair data->meshHash0 equals data->meshHash1; clashHash hashes the two prim paths. *data is written only on success. The ovstage backend also fails when the extraction generation of the pair differs from the current selected-object table, or when the stored mesh indices are otherwise invalid. The generation changes, for example, after any stage replacement, successful or failed, and after a direct mesh-selection step. The OpenUSD backend fails when one of the two prims has been deleted.

Note

Lifetime: data->name0 and data->name1 borrow backend-owned path storage. The next pipeline run, ovclash_release_memory, ovclash_reset_context and ovclash_release_context invalidate them. On ovstage, every call that retires the selected-object table invalidates them too: an ovclash_open_stage call that gets past argument validation, whether or not the open succeeds; a successful ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage; ovclash_ovstage_detach_stage; ovclash_ovstage_set_matrix_decomposition with a changed mode (see ovclash_ovstage.h); and an ovclash_get_prim_matrix failure that retires the selection population. The aggregate counts that survive do not keep them alive. Copy the bytes to keep a name. Never free them.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • data – [out] Receives the duplicate-pair record. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based duplicate-pair index.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or data, an out-of-range index, stale/invalid results, a deleted prim, or an active async pipeline.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_delete_duplicate_meshes(
ovclash_context_t *context,
)#

No-op in ovclash: does not delete duplicate meshes on either backend.

The stage-editing implementation lives in the Kit-only KitClash override, which ovclash does not compile. The OpenUSD backend therefore reaches an empty base-class virtual, and the ovstage backend has an explicitly empty body. The call still validates the context and is rejected while an async pipeline is active, but it never changes results, the stage or any counter. Duplicate records stay visible through ovclash_get_duplicate_mesh_count afterwards.

Note

Errors: a rejected call also records text retrievable through ovclash_get_last_error, which itself exists only under OVCLASH_STANDALONE.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or the call is rejected.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_overlap_count(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t *out_count,
)#

Returns the number of detected overlap groups (one group per colliding prim pair).

Each group holds ovclash_overlap_data_t::nbRecords per-frame records, always 1 for a static query. The count is 0 before any pipeline has run. A query interrupted by cancellation can return 0 with OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, and OpenUSD also reports 0 after a native out-of-memory. A zero count alone therefore does not prove that the scene is clash-free. Cancellation requested after completion does not erase the results produced. For async runs, check the finish outcome, and note ovclash_async_is_cancelled before finish clears the flag and consumes the handle. Also check ovclash_is_out_of_memory. On ovstage, a stage replacement or a direct mesh-selection step can keep this aggregate count while the table-indexed record details turn stale; ovclash_get_overlap_data then fails.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context. Rejected while a pipeline started by ovclash_run_pipeline_async has not been finished. Cancellation still requires ovclash_finish_pipeline to release the active handle.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • out_count – [out] Receives the overlap-group count. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if context or out_count is null, or an async pipeline handle is still active on this context.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_overlap_data(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_overlap_data_t *data,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
)#

Reads names, hashes, element count, time and depth for one overlap record.

index selects the overlap group (< ovclash_get_overlap_count), and recordIndex the frame inside that group (< the nbRecords of the group). Both backends range-check both indices. On failure *data is left completely untouched, and an unwritten data->type is not OVCLASH_OVERLAP_PAIR_TYPE_UNDEFINED, so always check the result code. minDistance and maxLocalDepth are in stage linear units. On a mesh-vs-mesh overlap maxLocalDepth stays -1.0f unless max-local-depth computation ran. A point-vs-mesh overlap always reports 0.0f, because depth is mesh-only (see ovclash_set_compute_max_local_depth). The ovstage backend also fails when the extraction generation of the record differs from the current selected-object table. That happens after a stage replacement, successful or failed, and after a direct step-1 re-selection. The check keeps an old clash from being relabelled with new paths.

Note

Lifetime: data->name0 and data->name1 borrow backend-owned path storage and must not be freed. The next pipeline run, ovclash_release_memory, ovclash_reset_context and ovclash_release_context invalidate them. On ovstage, every call that retires the selected-object table invalidates them too: an ovclash_open_stage call that gets past argument validation, whether or not the open succeeds; a successful ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage; ovclash_ovstage_detach_stage; ovclash_ovstage_set_matrix_decomposition with a changed mode (see ovclash_ovstage.h); and an ovclash_get_prim_matrix failure that retires the selection population. The aggregate counts that survive do not keep them alive. Copy the bytes to keep a name.

Note

Ordering: index is an identifier, not a rank. Which group sits at which index is NOT part of the contract. Two runs over the same stage with the same settings report the same set of groups with the same data, but not necessarily in the same order. On the OpenUSD backend, ovclash_set_new_task_manager() makes the order genuinely run-dependent. Match groups by name0 and name1 (or clashHash) rather than by index, and sort in the consumer when a deterministic order matters.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • data – [out] Receives the overlap record. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or data, an out-of-range index or recordIndex, stale results, an active async pipeline, or a backend fetch failure (for example a deleted prim).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_compute_max_local_depth(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float *depth,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
)#

Recomputes the maximum local penetration depth for an already detected record.

Mesh-vs-mesh records only; point-vs-mesh records fail on both backends. The value is in stage linear units. It is 0.0f when the record has no hard triangle pairs, which touch or interpenetrate at zero distance, so a record made only of tolerance near-misses reports 0.0f. The mode set through ovclash_set_compute_max_local_depth affects only how far the SAT estimate is refined. Unlike ovclash_imm_compute_max_local_depth, this call is NOT rejected in mode OVCLASH_MAX_LOCAL_DEPTH_MODE_DISABLED; it returns the cheap estimate. *depth is left untouched on failure.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active. The computation itself is synchronous and can be expensive on dense pairs.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • depth – [out] Receives the maximum local depth. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or depth, an out-of-range index/recordIndex, a point-cloud overlap, stale results, an active async pipeline, or a backend computation failure. On stale failure *depth remains untouched.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_estimate_motion_vector(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_float3_t *motionVector,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
)#

Estimates the world-space relative motion between the two prims of a dynamic record.

Meaningful only for time-sampled queries. Every record of a static query fails, and the first sampled frame of a run yields a zero or degenerate motion vector rather than failing. Mesh-vs-mesh records only; point-vs-mesh records fail on both backends. *motionVector is left untouched on failure. ovclash_depenetrate_meshes normalizes the result and uses it as the direction of OVCLASH_DEPENETRATION_AXIS_MOTION_VECTOR.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • motionVector – [out] Receives the estimated motion vector. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or motionVector, an out-of-range index/recordIndex, a record without previous-frame transforms, a point-cloud overlap, stale results, or an active async pipeline. Both backends check staleness before record-type/previous-frame state and leave the output untouched on failure.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_depenetrate_meshes(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_float3_t *disp,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
ovclash_depenetration_axis_t axis,
const ovclash_float3_t *userDir,
)#

Computes the displacement that separates the two meshes of a record along an axis.

Mesh-vs-mesh records only; point-vs-mesh records fail on both backends. userDir is required, and must be non-null, exactly for OVCLASH_DEPENETRATION_AXIS_USER_DEFINED; other axes ignore it. OVCLASH_DEPENETRATION_AXIS_MOTION_VECTOR fails unless the record carries previous-frame transforms. Both backends silently treat an axis value outside the enum as the zero direction, and still return success with a meaningless displacement. disp is a world-space vector in stage linear units and is untouched on failure.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • disp – [out] Receives the separating displacement. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

  • axis – [in] Depenetration direction selector.

  • userDir – [in] Direction for OVCLASH_DEPENETRATION_AXIS_USER_DEFINED; may be null otherwise.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or disp, an out-of-range index/recordIndex, a point-cloud overlap, USER_DEFINED with a null userDir, MOTION_VECTOR without previous transforms, stale results, or an active async pipeline. On stale failure *disp remains untouched.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_create_overlap_report(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_overlap_report_t *report,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
ovclash_mesh_index_t meshIndex,
uint32_t flags,
)#

Legacy single-mesh overlap report: colliding faces of one mesh plus the outline.

Honors only OVCLASH_OVERLAP_REPORT_FLAG_DEFAULT (0), _FACES and _OUTLINE. It ignores _FACES0, _FACES1 and _POINTS0; use ovclash_create_overlap_report_ex for those. meshIndex chooses whose face indices land in report->collidingFaces0, and collidingFaces1 always stays empty here. meshIndex must be OVCLASH_MESH_INDEX_0 or _1 whenever faces are requested. Point-cloud overlaps are unsupported and fail on both backends. *report is written only on success.

Note

Floating point: both backends compute outline segments under the calling thread’s floating-point controls, so reports requested under different rounding or denormal modes can differ. The ovstage-only OVCLASH matrix decomposition instead replays the controls in effect when the record was detected.

Note

Lifetime: every pointer in *report is borrowed, never owned by the caller. On the OpenUSD backend they point at engine heap buffers that ovclash_release_overlap_report frees; skipping that call leaks them. On ovstage they alias context-owned result vectors, and release only clears the struct. Release every report before the next pipeline step or run, ovclash_release_memory, ovclash_reset_context or ovclash_release_context. On ovstage, advancing a sampled pipeline can replace these borrowed buffers. ovstage rejects report acquisition when the extraction generations of the record and the selected table differ. A borrowed view acquired earlier cannot be checked afterwards.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • report – [out] Receives the report view. Must not be null; pass to ovclash_release_overlap_report when done.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

  • meshIndex – [in] Which mesh of the pair the face indices refer to.

  • flags – [in] Bitmask of ovclash_overlap_report_flag_t.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or report, an out-of-range index/recordIndex, a point-cloud overlap, an invalid meshIndex, stale ovstage results, an active async pipeline, or a backend extraction failure.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_create_overlap_report_ex(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_overlap_report_t *report,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
uint32_t flags,
double *matrixData0,
double *matrixData1,
)#

Extended overlap report: per-mesh faces, outline, cloud points and both world matrices.

Honors OVCLASH_OVERLAP_REPORT_FLAG_FACES0, _FACES1 and _OUTLINE for mesh-vs-mesh records, and _POINTS0, which also fills pointSize0, for point-vs-mesh records. Both backends ignore the legacy _DEFAULT and _FACES bits here. matrixData0 and matrixData1 are OUTPUT buffers, not inputs. When non-null, each receives exactly 16 doubles (128 bytes, row-major 4x4): the world transform of its prim captured at that record. Each must therefore point at storage for 16 doubles. The identically named const double* parameters of ovclash_imm_compute_max_local_depth and ovclash_imm_depenetrate_meshes go the opposite direction. Nothing is written to *report or to the matrices on failure.

Note

Floating point: both backends compute outline segments under the calling thread’s floating-point controls, so reports requested under different rounding or denormal modes can differ. The ovstage-only OVCLASH matrix decomposition instead replays the controls in effect when the record was detected.

Note

Lifetime: all report pointers are borrowed. On OpenUSD they are engine heap buffers that ovclash_release_overlap_report frees; skipping that call leaks them. On ovstage they alias context-owned vectors. Release every report before the next pipeline step or run, ovclash_release_memory, ovclash_reset_context or ovclash_release_context. On ovstage, advancing a sampled pipeline can replace these borrowed buffers. ovstage rejects report acquisition when the extraction generations of the record and the selected table differ. A borrowed view acquired earlier cannot be checked afterwards.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • report – [out] Receives the report view. Must not be null; pass to ovclash_release_overlap_report when done.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

  • flags – [in] Bitmask of ovclash_overlap_report_flag_t.

  • matrixData0 – [out] Optional 16-double row-major world matrix of mesh/cloud 0. May be null.

  • matrixData1 – [out] Optional 16-double row-major world matrix of mesh 1. May be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on a null context or report, an out-of-range index/recordIndex, stale results, an active async pipeline, or a backend extraction failure.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_release_overlap_report(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_overlap_report_t *report,
)#

Releases a report produced by ovclash_create_overlap_report[_ex] and clears the struct.

On the OpenUSD backend this frees the four engine-allocated buffers that *report references. Call it for every successful create, or the memory leaks. On the ovstage backend the context owns the buffers, and the call only clears the view. On both backends *report is then reset to the ovclash_reset_overlap_report state, which makes a second release harmless. A zero-initialized or reset empty report is also safe to release with a live context. Otherwise pass only a struct that a create call filled in and that has not been edited since: the OpenUSD path rebuilds the engine record straight from these fields and would free arbitrary pointers. Unlike the other report functions, this one is NOT rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context that created the report. Must not be null.

  • report – [in,out] Report to release; cleared in place. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if context or report is null (OpenUSD also if the context holds no engine instance).

ovclash_result_t ovclash_imm_compute_max_local_depth(
ovclash_context_t *context,
float *depth,
uint64_t meshPath0,
const double *matrixData0,
uint64_t meshPath1,
const double *matrixData1,
)#

Computes maximum local penetration depth for two meshes without running a pipeline.

meshPath0 and meshPath1 are encoded absolute prim paths from ovclash_sdf_path_to_int(). Each matrix is exactly 16 doubles holding the row-major 4x4 world transform of its mesh. The call loads and cooks the two meshes synchronously with the current context settings. In mode OVCLASH_MAX_LOCAL_DEPTH_MODE_DISABLED the operation fails. No prior clash query is required. On success *depth receives the computed value; on failure it is left unchanged.

Note

Preconditions: both matrix pointers must address 16 readable doubles; a null matrix pointer is rejected with OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on both backends.

Note

Side effects: may allocate and cook temporary mesh/query data; it does not publish or replace pipeline overlap results.

Note

Lifetime: all input pointers are borrowed only for the duration of the call.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context with an open stage. Must not be null.

  • depth – [out] Receives maximum local depth. Must not be null.

  • meshPath0 – [in] Encoded absolute prim path of the first mesh.

  • matrixData0 – [in] Pointer to 16 row-major doubles for the first world transform.

  • meshPath1 – [in] Encoded absolute prim path of the second mesh.

  • matrixData1 – [in] Pointer to 16 row-major doubles for the second world transform.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when depth is computed; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR for a null/invalid context or output, an active async pipeline, no open stage, disabled depth computation, null matrices, unknown paths, missing/invalid mesh data, a duplicate identical mesh pose, a backend query/cooking failure, or, on ovstage, a matrix with a non-finite or out-of-float-range value.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_imm_depenetrate_meshes(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_float3_t *disp,
uint64_t meshPath0,
const double *matrixData0,
uint64_t meshPath1,
const double *matrixData1,
const ovclash_float3_t *dir,
)#

Computes a directed depenetration vector for two meshes without running a pipeline.

meshPath0 and meshPath1 are encoded absolute prim paths from ovclash_sdf_path_to_int(). Each matrix is exactly 16 doubles holding the row-major 4x4 world transform of its mesh. The call runs synchronously with the current stage and cooking settings. No prior clash query is required. On success *disp receives the direction-and-magnitude vector that the mesh query returns. On failure *disp is left unchanged.

Note

Preconditions: both matrix pointers must address 16 readable doubles; a null matrix pointer is rejected with OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR on both backends.

Note

Side effects: may allocate and cook temporary mesh/query data; it does not publish or replace pipeline overlap results.

Note

Lifetime: all input pointers are borrowed only for the duration of the call.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context with an open stage. Must not be null.

  • disp – [out] Receives the depenetration vector. Must not be null.

  • meshPath0 – [in] Encoded absolute prim path of the first mesh.

  • matrixData0 – [in] Pointer to 16 row-major doubles for the first world transform.

  • meshPath1 – [in] Encoded absolute prim path of the second mesh.

  • matrixData1 – [in] Pointer to 16 row-major doubles for the second world transform.

  • dir – [in] Direction in which to solve the depenetration. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when disp is computed; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR for a null/invalid context, output, or direction, an active async pipeline, no open stage, null matrices, unknown paths, missing/invalid mesh data, a backend query/cooking failure, or, on ovstage, a matrix with a non-finite or out-of-float-range value.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_create_overlap_meshes(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t index,
uint32_t recordIndex,
bool printNames,
uint32_t mode,
)#

Not supported in ovclash: always fails on both backends.

Debug-mesh creation is a Kit-only feature of the KitClash override, which ovclash does not compile. Both backends stop after validating the record, so neither reaches the engine. Both record a “not supported” diagnostic for ovclash_get_last_error: “not supported by the ovclash

OpenUSD backend” on OpenUSD, “not supported by the ovstage backend” on ovstage. index and recordIndex are still range-checked first, and stale result details are rejected before the call reports that it is unsupported. printNames and mode are ignored. The function remains only for ABI compatibility with the Kit clash interface.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • index – [in] Zero-based overlap-group index.

  • recordIndex – [in] Zero-based record/frame index inside the group.

  • printNames – [in] Ignored.

  • mode – [in] Ignored.

Returns:

Always OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_release_overlap_meshes(
ovclash_context_t *context,
)#

No-op in ovclash: there are never any overlap debug meshes to release.

Counterpart of ovclash_create_overlap_meshes, which always fails here. The OpenUSD backend calls an empty base-class virtual, and the ovstage backend has an empty body. Only the context validation and the async-pipeline rejection run.

Note

Errors: a rejected call also records text retrievable through ovclash_get_last_error (available only under OVCLASH_STANDALONE).

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context; rejected while an async pipeline is active.

Parameters:

context – [in] Context created by ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null or the call is rejected.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_timeline_data(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_timeline_data_t *out_data,
)#

Reads the host timeline state.

Both standalone backends report a fixed stub timeline: startTime 0.0, endTime 0.0, currentTime 0.0, timeCodesPerSecond 24.0. OpenUSD takes those values from the FixedTimeline stub that replaces the Kit timeline; ovstage hard-codes the same four values. Nothing here reflects the open stage or ovclash_set_times, and no ovclash entry point can change it. Treat it as a constant, and drive time-sampled queries through ovclash_set_times instead. Neither backend validates the context argument, which may be null, and the active-async guard does not apply. Only the ovstage owner-operation rejection uses the context: it records its text on a non-null context.

Note

Lifetime: out_data is caller-owned plain data; nothing is borrowed.

Note

Threading: reads no context state; safe from any thread, including during an async run.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Not validated. May be null. On ovstage a non-null context receives the owner-operation rejection text; nothing else is read from or written to it.

  • out_data – [out] Receives the four timeline doubles. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when out_data is null or, on ovstage, when the call runs inside an owner-operation callback on the same thread (see ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation). Nothing is written to out_data on error.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_stage_timeline_data(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_stage_timeline_data_t *out_data,
)#

Reads the timeline metadata of the open stage.

A file-backed operation like ovclash_open_stage, but declared outside the OVCLASH_STANDALONE fence. ovclash_get_timeline_data mirrors a host timeline that standalone builds do not have; this function reads the stage itself. It returns the root-layer startTimeCode, endTimeCode, timeCodesPerSecond and framesPerSecond of the stage passed to ovclash_open_stage. A caller can then convert a static time or a dynamic range in seconds into stage time codes (seconds = time code / timeCodesPerSecond), or take the range from the stage. Unauthored start and end time codes read 0.0, and an unauthored framesPerSecond reads 24.0. Both backends resolve timeCodesPerSecond from the authored timeCodesPerSecond, else the authored framesPerSecond, else 24.0. This is the effective rate of native stage-time conversion, so an authored timeCodesPerSecond of 24.0 still overrides a different framesPerSecond. ovstage requires a positive finite effective rate when it opens the stage. OpenUSD may report a nonpositive authored rate, so callers must reject a nonpositive or nonfinite rate before converting time. On ovstage, a stage attached with ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage reports the start_time_code, end_time_code, time_codes_per_second and frames_per_second of its binding instead. All fields are zeroed before any validation, so a call that fails after the null checks leaves a well-defined all-zero record. Nothing is written when out_data is null.

Note

Lifetime: a null out_data records an error; otherwise a valid context’s last error is cleared before the remaining checks. out_data is caller-owned plain data.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • out_data – [out] Receives the four stage timeline doubles. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the record is written; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context or out_data is null/invalid, an async pipeline handle is active, or no stage is open.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_query_stats(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_stats_t *stats,
)#

Reads mesh and point-cloud counters for the current query.

Reports how many meshes were selected, how many of them were shared instances, how many were cooked, and how many point clouds were selected. The values are meaningful only after the pipeline has run; before that they are zero. OpenUSD copies the accumulated statistics of the engine, which ovclash_reset_context clears. ovstage computes them live from context state, which ovclash_release_memory clears.

Note

Lifetime: stats is caller-owned plain data; nothing is borrowed.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • stats – [out] Receives the four counters. Must not be null; left untouched on failure.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS on success; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when stats is null, context is null/invalid, or an async pipeline handle is active. Detail via ovclash_get_last_error.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_release_memory(ovclash_context_t *ptr)#

Releases memory held for the current query.

The two backends drop different amounts of state, but both leave the context usable. ovstage clears the query results: source data, meshes, point clouds, overlaps, duplicates, cooked and shared counters, dynamic state and the broadphase BVH. An attached stage stays attached. OpenUSD releases only the overlap debug meshes of the engine, which ovclash never creates (see ovclash_create_overlap_meshes), so it frees nothing and keeps every result. On both backends the context can still be reconfigured and run again. ovclash_reset_context drops all query state.

Note

Errors: the status reports the rejection. Both backends reject an active async pipeline handle and report it through ovclash_get_last_error, which exists only in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. A null ptr records nothing anywhere.

Note

Lifetime: on ovstage this invalidates every borrowed view previously handed out by result getters and reports for this context.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive.

Parameters:

ptr – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. A null ptr returns OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when ptr is null or an async pipeline handle is active.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_is_out_of_memory(
ovclash_context_t *context,
uint32_t *out_is_oom,
)#

Queries whether the backend recorded an out-of-memory condition.

OpenUSD reads the process-global out-of-memory flag of the engine. The clash allocator sets it when an allocation returns null. ovclash_reset_context, the release of any OpenUSD context and the first phase of an async run clear it. Because the flag is global, every context in the process shares it, and the context argument serves only the active-async guard. ovstage records, per context, a std::bad_alloc from a required allocation that reaches its C API or async-worker boundary. That flag survives the pipeline finish. A reset, an accepted stage-open attempt or a new run clears it. An optional allocation that fails and recovers does not set it. A dependency may report an allocation failure through an error status or text without setting this flag, so also check the call status and ovclash_get_last_error. A null ovstage context reports 0.

Note

Lifetime: out_is_oom is caller-owned plain data; nothing is borrowed.

Note

Threading: the OpenUSD flag is a plain volatile bool that worker threads write without synchronization; read it only after the pipeline has finished. The ovstage flag is atomic, but a query is still rejected until the async handle has been finished and destroyed.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. May be null. On ovstage selects the recorded condition; both backends reject an active async pipeline handle.

  • out_is_oom – [out] Receives 1 or 0. Must not be null; left untouched on failure.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when out_is_oom is written; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when out_is_oom is null or an async pipeline handle is active on a non-null context.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_async_is_cancelled(
ovclash_async_t *async,
uint32_t *out_cancelled,
)#

Reports whether cancellation has been requested for an asynchronous pipeline.

The OpenUSD backend never dereferences the async argument, because the underlying bridge exposes cancellation only as a process-global flag. It answers for the whole process and accepts a null handle. The ovstage backend reads the per-context flag reached through the handle. For a null handle or a handle without a context it reports 0 and still returns success. The flag stays set until ovclash_finish_pipeline or ovclash_reset_context clears it. On OpenUSD, finishing, resetting or releasing any context clears the process-global flag for every context. This call may be polled while the handle is live.

Note

Lifetime: pass null or a live handle. ovstage dereferences the handle, so it must not already have been passed to ovclash_finish_pipeline. OpenUSD never dereferences it, but finishing has already cleared the flag, so a finished handle reports nothing about its run.

Note

Threading: may be polled from another thread while the worker runs, but not concurrently with or after ovclash_finish_pipeline on the same handle. ovstage reads an atomic per-context flag. OpenUSD reads the shared engine’s volatile process-global flag, which provides no C++ thread-safety guarantee.

Parameters:

  • async – [in] Handle from ovclash_run_pipeline_async. May be null on both backends.

  • out_cancelled – [out] Receives 1 when cancellation was requested, otherwise 0.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when out_cancelled was written; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR only when out_cancelled is null, or a C++ exception was caught.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_open_stage(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_string_t path,
)#

Opens a file-backed USD stage as the clash source.

Only present in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. Both backends require an existing local filesystem path. A std::filesystem::exists check runs before any USD or ovstage resolution, so an asset URI that is not a plain file is rejected up front. OpenUSD opens a pxr::UsdStage, swaps the entry of this context in the process-global standalone stage registry, and immediately pushes an empty scope and the new stage id into the engine. ovstage populates the stage through ovstage, clears the scope lists of the context, and advances the selected-table extraction generation.

Result details computed earlier then fail with a “result details are stale” message on both backends until matching results are published. Aggregate counts computed earlier are kept, but the name0 and name1 views that the result getters already returned are not. The installed pipeline shape stays available, but a started pipeline must restart at step 0, or be recreated, before it runs further steps against the new stage. A path with the same spelling is still a replacement and reads the file again. On OpenUSD, a layer that another holder in the process keeps open, such as the stage of another context, stays shared through the Sdf layer registry and is not read again. Neither backend restores OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE after ovclash_set_scope_paths cleared it.

Note

Lifetime: clears the last error of the context on entry, so read ovclash_get_last_error only after this call returned OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive. The OpenUSD stage registry is mutex-protected and shared process-wide.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • path – [in] UTF-8 filesystem path. ptr may be null only when length is 0, which is then rejected as an empty path. Copied during the call.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the stage is open; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null/invalid, an async pipeline handle is active, path has a null ptr with a non-zero length, is not valid UTF-8, contains an embedded NUL, is empty, does not exist, or fails to open. When the open itself fails (missing file or USD/ovstage error), the previous stage is dropped, so the context has no source until the next successful call. Argument, UTF-8, embedded-NUL and empty-path errors are rejected before the replacement point and leave the current source and result details unchanged. An actual open attempt, successful or failed, retires them on both backends.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_prim_matrix(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_string_t prim_path,
double time,
double *out_matrix,
)#

Reads a prim’s local-to-world transform from the open stage.

Only present in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. time is a USD time code, not seconds. Both backends fill out_matrix with identity before doing any work, so a call that fails after context validation still leaves a well-defined matrix. Nothing is written when out_matrix is null or the context is null or invalid. OpenUSD evaluates a fresh pxr::UsdGeomXformCache per call against the open stage, and fails when the prim does not exist.

For a finite time, ovstage uses a separate, lazy, selector-only numeric population of the source. Reads at the same time reuse it. A forward read applies the new time and reads the local and reset columns at the new sealed population ordinal; a rewind reopens the population. ovstage converts USD time codes to population seconds with the effective composed stage rate: timeCodesPerSecond, else framesPerSecond, else 24.0. The resolved rate must be positive and finite. Conversion fails when a finite USD time code overflows population seconds, or when a nonzero time code underflows to zero seconds. This applies to text and binary stages alike. The numeric path composes world matrices itself, without a separate hierarchy pass. It never advances the USD-default RENDERING population that selection uses. Numeric reads check that the requested prim exists, including identity and instance-proxy prims. An explicit source-read error fails the call with that error.

ovstage never substitutes the pipeline pose of a selected mesh or point cloud, which belongs to the last evaluated sample rather than to time. A read that yields neither a matrix nor its own error fails with “Failed to query prim transform: “ followed by prim_path. A prim missing at the default time keeps a valid selection state. A genuine read or resource failure that resets the selection population invalidates its selected-table details and installed pipeline. Recreate the pipeline after addressing the error, rather than continuing its remaining steps. Direct queries join any matrix-prefetch callback before they access the source. They keep its copied future window, unless the query retires the selection population.

Note

Lifetime: clears the last error of the context on entry; out_matrix is caller-owned.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • prim_path – [in] UTF-8 absolute prim path. ptr may be null only when length is 0, which is then rejected as empty. Copied during the call.

  • time – [in] USD time code at which the transform is evaluated.

  • out_matrix – [out] Receives a row-major 4x4 transform. Must point to 16 writable doubles.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the transform is written; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when out_matrix or context is null/invalid, an async pipeline handle is active, prim_path is an invalid span, non-UTF-8, contains an embedded NUL or is empty, no stage is open, or the prim cannot be resolved.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_sdf_path_to_int(
ovclash_string_t prim_path,
uint64_t *out_encoded,
)#

Encodes an absolute USD prim path into the uint64 id used by the scope and immediate-mode entry points.

Only present in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. The path must be an absolute prim path. OpenUSD enforces that through pxr::SdfPath, ovstage through an equivalent USD-identifier check. The two encodings are unrelated, and only the backend that produced an id accepts it. Both backends keep what an id names in a mutex-protected, process-global registry. The id therefore stays valid and stable for the same path for the process lifetime, whether or not a stage holds that path. OpenUSD returns the raw bit pattern of a pxr::SdfPath, a refcounted path-node handle. Its registry keeps the node alive, but the id must never be persisted, hashed for storage or shared across processes. ovstage interns the path string and returns a small non-zero id. Neither registry is ever pruned, not by ovclash_release_context and not by opening another stage. Encoding an unbounded number of distinct paths therefore grows memory until exit.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently. Both registries are mutex-protected. OpenUSD path construction relies on the concurrency guarantees of pxr::SdfPath.

Parameters:

  • prim_path – [in] UTF-8 absolute prim path. ptr may be null only when length is 0, which is rejected. Copied during the call.

  • out_encoded – [out] Receives the encoded id. Must not be null; left untouched on failure.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when out_encoded is written; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when out_encoded is null, or prim_path is an invalid span, non-UTF-8, contains an embedded NUL, is empty, or is not an absolute prim path, or, on ovstage, when the call runs inside an owner-operation callback on the same thread (see ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation). There is no context argument, so the return code is the only failure signal. Nothing is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_set_scope_paths(
ovclash_context_t *context,
const ovclash_string_t *paths1,
size_t paths1_count,
const ovclash_string_t *paths2,
size_t paths2_count,
)#

Restricts clash detection to one or two sets of USD prim paths.

Only present in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. Prefer it over ovclash_set_scope, which needs pre-encoded ids. paths1 alone means “paths1 against itself”, both non-empty means “paths1

against paths2”, and both empty means no scope. A scope entry also covers its descendants. Meshes that match both scopes belong to paths1 only: the two-scope mesh query compares paths1 against paths2 minus paths1. Identical scopes therefore produce no mesh-vs-mesh pairs. Validation is all-or-nothing: the scope of the context is replaced only after every entry passes.

No scope is NOT the same as whole-stage traversal. Selection reads two independent pieces of state, this scope and OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE:

scope non-empty -> the scope, whatever the flag says scope empty, FULL_SCENE set -> whole stage scope empty, FULL_SCENE cleared -> nothing at all

The flag starts set on a fresh context and can be restored explicitly. Side effect: when either scope is non-empty, this call clears the flag on both backends. Clearing the scope paths does not restore it. Neither does a successful ovclash_open_stage or, on ovstage, ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage, although both clear the scope, so set the scope after them. Restore full-scene traversal with ovclash_set_full_scene(context, true), or with settings that enable OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE. Both of those calls also clear the scope: the engine scope paths on OpenUSD, the scope lists of the context on ovstage. To keep a non-empty explicit scope, apply them before setting the paths.

OpenUSD converts the strings to SdfPath ids and pushes them into the engine with the current stage id. ovstage stores the strings and prefix-matches them during selection. Both backends read the scope only when a run selects meshes. A call between the steps of a run therefore leaves the selected meshes and the two-scope grouping of that run unchanged.

Note

Lifetime: clears the last error of the context on entry. The caller keeps ownership of every string and array passed in.

Note

Threading: serialize per context; rejected while an async pipeline handle is alive.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context from ovclash_create_context. Must not be null.

  • paths1 – [in] First scope. May be null only when paths1_count is 0. Copied during the call.

  • paths1_count – [in] Entry count of paths1.

  • paths2 – [in] Second scope. May be null only when paths2_count is 0. Copied during the call.

  • paths2_count – [in] Entry count of paths2.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS when the scope is stored; OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR when context is null/invalid, an async pipeline handle is active, an array is null with a non-zero count, or any entry is an invalid span, non-UTF-8, contains an embedded NUL, is empty, or is not an absolute prim path.

ovclash_string_t ovclash_get_last_error(
const ovclash_context_t *context,
)#

Returns the last error message recorded on a context.

Only present in OVCLASH_STANDALONE builds. It is the only diagnostic channel of the canonical ABI, with no thread-local fallback. The context-free entry points never record anything here: ovclash_sdf_path_to_int, ovclash_get_backend_info, ovclash_get_result_string, ovclash_get_version, ovclash_get_version_string, ovclash_overlap_report_get_dltensor and the ovclash_reset_* helpers. ovclash_get_timeline_data records only on ovstage, and only when it is rejected inside an owner-operation callback with a non-null context.

A success does NOT always clear the text. Calls that clear it include ovclash_open_stage, ovclash_get_prim_matrix, ovclash_get_stage_timeline_data, ovclash_set_scope_paths and, on ovstage, the start of a run and the optional attach and detach operations. A message can outlive the call that produced it. On ovstage, a run clears the text on entry to ovclash_run_pipeline_step with index 0, and for ovclash_run_pipeline_async the worker clears it when the run begins, so a synchronized read during the run may see the message of the previous run or of the current one. Read the text after a call returned OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR. A non-empty string never means by itself that the last call failed.

One message is recorded by a call that SUCCEEDS. On ovstage, a run that dropped meshes it could not cook reports that here (see ovclash_stats_t::nbCookedMeshes), while every step still returns OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS. The message belongs to its run, and the next run clears it on entry. Any call in between that records or clears an error still replaces it, so read it before doing anything else with the context. nbCookedMeshes below nbMeshes minus nbSharedMeshes is the durable signal.

Note

Lifetime: on ovstage the view points at a thread-local copy, which the next ovclash_get_last_error on the same thread invalidates. While the out-of-memory flag of the context is set, ovstage returns a static diagnostic that needs no allocation instead. Once the thread-local storage of the thread is destroyed, a static notice stands in for a recorded message; glibc destroys that storage of the main thread at exit, before static destructors run. On OpenUSD the context owns the text. The next call on that context that records or clears an error invalidates it, and so does ovclash_release_context. Copy the bytes to keep them on either backend.

Note

Threading: access is synchronized on ovstage, where the async pipeline worker writes the same string while a pipeline runs. A read during the run is safe, but which message it returns is nondeterministic.

Parameters:

context – [in] Context to query. May be null, which yields an empty { NULL, 0 } view.

Returns:

Borrowed UTF-8 view of the recorded message. It is null-terminated and the reported length excludes the terminator; the view is empty when nothing has been recorded.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_settings(
const ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_settings_t *out_settings,
)#

Reads back the settings currently applied to a context.

The inverse of ovclash_set_settings(). A fresh context reports exactly the ovclash_reset_settings() table on both backends.

Every individual ovclash_set_* setter is reflected here too, so the result always describes the live configuration, not only the last whole-struct assignment. nbTasks reads back clamped to 256, as both backends store it.

Note

Threading: must not run concurrently with a setter on the same context. It is not rejected while an async pipeline handle is active. The setters are, so a read during an async run is stable.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] Context to query. Must not be null and must be valid.

  • out_settings – [out] Receives the current settings. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if either argument is null or the context is invalid (nothing written). No error text is recorded.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_get_version(
uint32_t *out_major,
uint32_t *out_minor,
uint32_t *out_patch,
)#

Reports the runtime version of the loaded ovclash library.

Use it to check that the loaded shared library matches the headers the caller compiled against. The compile-time constants are OVCLASH_VERSION_MAJOR, _MINOR and _PATCH in <ovclash/version.h>.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently. Reads no context and no global state.

Parameters:

  • out_major – [out] Major version. Must not be null.

  • out_minor – [out] Minor version. Must not be null.

  • out_patch – [out] Patch version. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if any argument is null (nothing written).

ovclash_string_t ovclash_get_version_string(void)#

Returns the runtime version as a “MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH” string, for example “1.2.3”.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently.

Returns:

An explicit-length, null-terminated string with static storage duration. The library owns it. It stays valid for the lifetime of the process and must not be freed or modified.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_overlap_report_get_dltensor(
const ovclash_overlap_report_t *report,
ovclash_report_buffer_t buffer,
ovclash_dltensor_view_t *out_view,
)#

Describes one overlap-report array as a DLPack tensor, without copying.

The tensor borrows the memory of the report: tensor.data aliases the matching pointer inside report. Nothing is allocated and there is nothing to free.

Note

Results: an array that the report flags did not request has count 0. That is reported as success with a zero-length tensor and tensor.data == NULL, not as an error.

Note

Lifetime: the tensor is valid only while report is; it dangles after ovclash_release_overlap_report(). It carries no deleter, so it must never reach a consumer that expects to own a DLManagedTensor.

Note

Device: always kDLCPU, device_id 0.

Note

Threading: safe to call concurrently with distinct out_view storage; the call only reads report.

Parameters:

  • report – [in] A report previously filled by ovclash_create_overlap_report() or ovclash_create_overlap_report_ex(). Must not be null.

  • buffer – [in] Which array to describe.

  • out_view – [out] Receives the tensor and its shape/stride storage. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS, or OVCLASH_STATUS_ERROR if report or out_view is null or buffer is not a valid enumerator. There is no context, so nothing is recorded for ovclash_get_last_error.

struct ovclash_backend_info_t#
#include <include/ovclash/ovclash.h>

struct ovclash_result_t#
#include <include/ovclash/ovclash.h>

Result of a canonical ovclash entry point.

The struct holds one ovclash_status_t field named status. Test it as result.status == OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS. OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS is 0, so a truthiness test of the status reverses the success check.

The struct owns no memory and is safe to copy by value. It carries no detail: where a context exists, ovclash_get_last_error() returns the diagnostic. ovclash_suite_result_t has the same shape, so both public C layers report results the same way.

uint32_t nbMeshes#
uint32_t nbSharedMeshes#
uint32_t nbCookedMeshes#

Unique source meshes successfully cooked for this run; on OpenUSD, the number of cooks attempted.

Shared meshes are cooked once, so a healthy run reports nbMeshes minus nbSharedMeshes. A lower nbCookedMeshes means geometry is missing from the results. A mesh that PhysX cannot cook, for example because of degenerate triangles, is dropped from every phase after cooking. The pipeline step does not fail, so one unusable mesh does not discard the rest. Such a run still reports success and still returns overlaps. The overlaps of the dropped meshes are absent, which looks exactly like a clean scene.

The comparison is an ovstage signal: on OpenUSD a failed cook never lowers this count. On ovstage, compare the counts, then read ovclash_get_last_error(). A mesh that PhysX could not cook records the number of dropped meshes and the first of them, whatever the logging flag. A mesh whose triangulation produced no triangles is dropped with only a log line. Enable logging to name every dropped mesh.

struct ovclash_dltensor_view_t#
#include <include/ovclash/ovclash.h>

A DLTensor plus inline storage for its shape and strides.

DLTensor::shape and strides are pointers, so their arrays need storage. This transparent struct holds that storage inline, so the view can live on the stack and needs no allocation or cleanup: 

ovclash_dltensor_view_t view;
if (ovclash_overlap_report_get_dltensor(&report, OVCLASH_REPORT_BUFFER_FACES0, &view).status ==
    OVCLASH_STATUS_SUCCESS)
{
    consume(&view.tensor);
}
A copy of a filled struct still has tensor.shape and tensor.strides pointing into the original. Fill a fresh view instead of copying a filled one.

Linkage macro#

ovclash_export.h is the single definition of OVCLASH_API. Linkage macro gives its expansion on each platform. The Doxygen run predefines OVCLASH_API as empty, and the header has no Doxygen comments, so this section renders almost nothing.

ovstage backend extensions#

ovclash_ovstage.h and ovclash_suite_ovstage.h declare optional symbols that only the ovstage build of the library exports: Stage attachment, owner operations and, on the canonical layer, matrix decomposition selection. ovstage Integration covers the backend check, the owner-operation gate and its reentry rules, the binding descriptor and the authored-transform-updates capability. Comparing ovstage matrix decompositions covers the decomposition selector.

Defines

OVCLASH_OVSTAGE_CAP_AUTHORED_TRANSFORM_UPDATES#

Opts in to authored transform classification on the borrowed Stage.

The owner must populate every composed raw xformOp:* value and the USD-default xformOpOrder:usd-metadata:default for all prims, ancestors and prototypes. A missing order must mean that no default order is authored, not that the property was left out of the population. No source edits, topology changes or manual raw-op writes may occur during a query.

The evaluator may be called twice at identical finite seconds. Between those two committed ordinals, the raw-op update records must contain exactly the initially valued operations that have more than one effective composed USD time sample. Equal-valued samples count. Single samples, and defaults that mask weaker samples, must not produce raw-op updates. Unused operations may be populated. Classification follows the default order and all ancestors, also across reset-stack boundaries. A missing initial active value stays unresolved.

The owner must preserve the complete intervening update interval until the callback returns. Canonical local and reset writes are allowed. A derived matrix change is never an authored-animation signal. The capability requires evaluate_time. Without the capability, attached meshes stay conservatively non-static. An attachment with a composition classifies from its own population and must leave capabilities zero.

Typedefs

typedef struct ovstage_instance_t ovstage_instance_t#
typedef int32_t (*ovclash_ovstage_owner_operation_fn)(void *user_data)#

Performs one synchronous caller-owned ovstage operation.

The callback must not throw or enter any clash runtime. Nested owner-operation calls are allowed.

Param user_data:

[in] Caller-owned operation state, used only during the call.

Return:

1 on success, or any other value on failure.

typedef int32_t (*ovclash_ovstage_evaluate_time_fn)(void *user_data, double seconds, uint64_t *out_committed_ordinal, const char **out_error)#

Evaluates the borrowed stage at a time in seconds, where NaN means Default.

Never called for an attachment with a composition.

On success the callback returns 1 with a newly committed ordinal. On failure it returns any other value, conventionally 0, and may set a UTF-8 diagnostic. The diagnostic must remain valid until the enclosing ovclash call returns. The callback runs on the calling pipeline thread, which may be a native worker. It must not throw or enter any clash runtime.

Before it returns success, the callback must publish the complete sampled canonical local transforms and reset-stack opinions, and then seal the ordinal. The publication includes invisible instance placements and prototype operands. A rendering-only time update may omit invisible placements.

ovclash invokes the callback as an owner operation: the calling thread already holds the process-wide gate of ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation. Nested owner operations on that thread are allowed. The callback must never wait for another thread that acquires the gate, because that deadlocks. Owner locks taken in the callback are acquired after the gate, as that function requires.

Note

Threading: one context invokes the callback serially. The owner serializes callbacks and the external use of any Stage shared by several contexts.

Param user_data:

[in] The binding’s caller-owned callback state.

Param seconds:

[in] Evaluation time in seconds, or NaN for Default.

Param out_committed_ordinal:

[out] Receives the sealed read ordinal on success.

Param out_error:

[out] Optional borrowed diagnostic on failure.

Return:

1 on success; any other value, conventionally 0, reports failure. The ordinal must strictly increase and fit the ordinal type of the supplied ovstage implementation (ovstage_ordinal_t, a uint64_t in the pinned ovstage).
