Functions

ovclash_result_t ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation(
ovclash_ovstage_owner_operation_fn operation,
void *user_data,
)#

Runs an owner operation under the process-wide ovstage lifecycle gate of ovclash.

The gate coordinates external Stage creation, destruction, population, source edits, inspection composition and renderer lifecycle with native file populations. The callback runs synchronously on the calling thread and is never retained. Nested calls on the same thread share the gate, up to 64 levels deep. Inside an owner callback, every guarded canonical entry point and every Suite function that returns ovclash_suite_result_t fails with a reentry error. Nested owner operations stay allowed. So do the unguarded ovclash_get_settings, ovclash_get_last_error and the version, result-string, DLPack tensor-view and reset helpers. Acquire this gate before any owner-specific lock. Attached evaluate_time callbacks already run under it. Data-plane reads and collision work do not acquire it. The OpenUSD backend does not export this optional symbol.

Before and after the callback, the gate looks for the loaded client that sits beside the ovstage runtime. The first successful client discovery, through SDK instance creation or this gate, reads OVCLASH_OMNI_CLIENT_RETRY_MAX_MS and configures the client retry window once per process. The default 0 disables reconnect retries; a positive value allows that many milliseconds. A value that is not an unsigned 32-bit integer is reported on stderr and treated as 0. The policy also affects other callers that share the process-wide client. While the client is not available, configuration stays pending and a later discovery retries it. SDK instance creation reports a missing client once per process on stderr when an explicit retry setting cannot be applied. The checks made by this gate are silent.

Note

Threading: owner operations on different threads are serialized. Nested calls on one thread run synchronously under the gate that thread already holds.

Parameters:

  • operation – [in] Operation callback. Must not be null.

  • user_data – [in] Borrowed callback state. May be null.

Returns:

Success when the callback returns 1. Error for a null callback, callback failure, excessive nesting or a native exception. The gate is released on every exit. Callback diagnostics remain the caller’s responsibility.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage(
ovclash_context_t *context,
const ovclash_ovstage_binding_t *binding,
)#

Borrows an existing ovstage data-plane instance for one context.

Never writes, evaluates on its own or destroys the instance.

Without a composition the attachment is owner-evaluated and opens no file. Every read uses the borrowed Stage, and a time other than time_seconds calls evaluate_time. Without a callback only the supplied evaluation is available, and Default selection reads that frozen snapshot.

With a composition the attachment is engine-evaluated:

  • Default selection, geometry, visibility, subcomponent kinds, immediate queries and Default-time matrix queries read the borrowed Stage at committed_ordinal. committed_ordinal must stay retained until detach. Units and the timeline come from the binding, as without a composition.

  • ovclash evaluates every finite time itself. That covers numeric transforms, static/dynamic classification, matrix prefetch and direct matrix queries at finite time codes. It replays the composition into private ovstage instances under the gate of ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation, at the first finite-time read, and destroys them at detach, reset, ovclash_release_memory or replacement.

  • ovclash never calls evaluate_time and never advances the Stage.

  • The owner guarantees that, at every finite time, its canonical local transforms and reset-stack opinions equal those of a fresh population of the composition. A transform the owner writes only into the data plane is therefore seen by Default selection and by no finite-time read.

  • ovclash reopens the root by its string at every replay, including the first finite-time read, the next finite-time read after a failed replay, the first one after ovclash_release_memory, a read at an earlier time than the last one, each classification and, for an ambiguous rate, the first direct matrix query at a finite time code. The root file and every file that the root or a layer references must therefore stay unchanged on disk until detach; a changed file gives wrong finite-time poses without an error, or fails the run. A relative root resolves against the process working directory at each replay, so open the Stage from an absolute path or a URL and pass that string.

  • meters_per_unit and time_codes_per_second must equal the values the composition resolves; otherwise the first finite-time read fails. One exception: when the root resolves timeCodesPerSecond 24 together with a framesPerSecond F other than 24, an authored 24 cannot be told from an absent rate that falls back to F, so a binding rate of 24 or F is accepted. The first direct matrix query at a finite time code, such as ovclash_get_prim_matrix, then resolves the root’s effective rate and fails on a mismatch. Until then, sampling and classification, which work in seconds, do not detect a wrong rate, and ovclash_get_stage_timeline_data keeps reporting the binding’s rate. Once detected, a mismatch fails every later finite-time read and classification of the attachment with the same diagnostic and without another replay, also after ovclash_release_memory, until the next attach.

  • A composition that ovstage cannot replay fails the first finite-time read with the ovstage diagnostic.

  • The owner must never hold that gate while it waits for a clash call.

In both modes, while clash operations use the instance, the owner excludes rendering, edits, time changes and destruction. A replacement invalidates geometry, results and pipelines. ovclash_release_memory keeps the attachment; ovclash_reset_context, ovclash_ovstage_detach_stage and ovclash_open_stage release it. Active async handles are rejected, including completed handles that are not yet released.

A successful attachment, first or replacement, also clears the scope paths and last error of the context. Like ovclash_open_stage, it does not restore OVCLASH_SETTINGS_FLAG_FULL_SCENE after ovclash_set_scope_paths cleared it, so a run would then select nothing. Set the scope after attaching, or call ovclash_set_full_scene(context, true) for an unscoped run.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] An ovstage context from ovclash_create_context().

  • binding – [in] Caller-owned Stage, metadata, optional callback and optional composition. Must not be null. The descriptor and the composition are copied; the Stage is borrowed.

Returns:

Success, or error for a null context or binding, an invalid size, metadata, ordinal, Stage or composition, or active work. An invalid binding leaves the previous attachment and scope intact. ovclash_get_last_error reports the context diagnostic.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_ovstage_detach_stage(
ovclash_context_t *context,
)#

Releases a borrowed stage after all operations finish, without destroying it.

Invalidates results and pipelines and clears the last error of the context. Active async handles are rejected. On a context without an attachment the call also succeeds: it still clears results and forgets any stage opened with ovclash_open_stage.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

context – [in] An ovstage context from ovclash_create_context().

Returns:

Success, or error for an invalid context or active work.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_ovstage_set_matrix_decomposition(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_ovstage_matrix_decomposition_t implementation,
)#

Selects mesh matrix decomposition for one ovstage context.

A changed mode clears results, invalidates borrowed reports, and discards the current pipeline and the cached geometry and poses. Release reports before the call, and create a new pipeline for the next run. Reapplying the same mode keeps the native results and pipeline state. Immediate mesh queries also use the selected mode. Raw reported world matrices and point-cloud scaling do not depend on it.

The setting survives a context reset and a stage replacement. New contexts use OPENUSD. OVCLASH can change which pairs clash at zero tolerance and what they report. In both modes, mesh decomposition rejects non-finite matrix values and values or linear row magnitudes outside the float range. It also rejects resulting poses or scales that are non-finite or not representable, including rotation quaternions that are not unit length. An affected pipeline or immediate call reports an error.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context. Different contexts select independently.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] An ovstage context from ovclash_create_context().

  • implementation – [in] OPENUSD or OVCLASH.

Returns:

Success, or error for a null context, an invalid mode, an active async handle (including a completed handle that is not yet released) or a native failure. A failure leaves the selected mode unchanged. ovclash_get_last_error() reports context errors.

ovclash_result_t ovclash_ovstage_get_matrix_decomposition(
ovclash_context_t *context,
ovclash_ovstage_matrix_decomposition_t *implementation,
)#

Reads the selected decomposition of an ovstage context.

Does not change results or pipeline state.

Note

Threading: serialize all calls on one context.

Parameters:

  • context – [in] An ovstage context from ovclash_create_context().

  • implementation – [out] Receives the selected mode on success.

Returns:

Success, or error for a null context or output pointer.

struct ovclash_ovstage_composition_t#
#include <include/ovclash/ovclash_ovstage.h>

Composition of an attached Stage, for time evaluation by ovclash.

Names the ovstage population calls whose surviving effect is the borrowed Stage’s USD source:

  • root is the exact string the owner passed to ovstage_population_open_usd_from_file or its _with_desc variant (OVCLASH_OVSTAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT_FILE: a path or an omniverse:// URL), or to ovstage_population_open_usd_from_string or its _with_desc variant (OVCLASH_OVSTAGE_COMPOSITION_ROOT_USDA). The replay does not depend on which variant the owner called.

  • layers are the USDA texts of the owner’s surviving ovstage_population_add_usd_reference_from_string(stage, text, “/”) merges, in the order the owner added them, earliest first. A merge the owner removed, for example to mute it, is left out.

ovclash replays the same calls with the same strings in the same order into ovstage instances of its own. The strength order and the anchoring of inline layers therefore follow the owner’s. A composition cannot express references at other target paths, file references, or values written directly into the owner’s data plane. An owner that relies on any of them at finite times must not supply a composition.

Set struct_size to sizeof(ovclash_ovstage_composition_t). root_kind holds an ovclash_ovstage_composition_root_t value. root and every layer are non-empty UTF-8 without an embedded NUL. layers may be null only when nb_layers is 0. The attach call copies every string.

Public Members

uint64_t struct_size#
ovclash_string_t root#
uint32_t root_kind#
uint32_t nb_layers#
const ovclash_string_t *layers#
struct ovclash_ovstage_binding_t#
#include <include/ovclash/ovclash_ovstage.h>

Binding of an existing ovstage Stage.

The owner resolves the metadata. Without a composition, ovclash opens no file and probes no file metadata. Set struct_size to the size of this structure. The stage and callback stay caller-owned and must outlive the attachment and every operation on it.

time_seconds describes the current evaluation of the stage. It must be finite, or NaN for Default. Reads at that time use committed_ordinal without calling evaluate_time until another time is evaluated. That publication must therefore be as complete as one made by evaluate_time. meters_per_unit and both rates must be finite and positive. The timeline endpoints must be finite. committed_ordinal must be positive, retained and covered by the global write floor. The instance bundle and its version-query slot must be valid pointers, and the instance must report the ovstage API major and minor version that ovclash was built against, those of the pinned ovstage. evaluate_time may be null. user_data is passed to evaluate_time unchanged.

ovstage_instance_t *stage#

double start_time_code#
double end_time_code#

double frames_per_second#

Optional tail guarded by struct_size: a struct_size that ends right before this field is accepted and means no capabilities.

Zero keeps the conservative classification. Unknown bits are rejected, and a nonzero value requires evaluate_time.

const ovclash_ovstage_composition_t *composition#

Optional tail guarded by struct_size: a struct_size that ends right before this field is accepted and means no composition.

Null keeps the owner-evaluated attachment.

A non-null composition makes the attachment engine-evaluated; see ovclash_ovstage_composition_t and ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage. time_seconds must then be NaN, evaluate_time must be null and capabilities must be zero.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_run_ovstage_owner_operation(
ovclash_ovstage_owner_operation_fn operation,
void *user_data,
)#

Runs a synchronous owner operation under the native ovstage lifecycle gate.

Only the ovstage build of the library exports this function, like every function of this header. Nesting and lock ordering are those of ovclash_ovstage_run_owner_operation. No runtime or Stage is created or retained. Inside the callback, every Suite function that returns ovclash_suite_result_t fails with OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR. This includes data-store, model, export and utility helpers that touch no runtime. Only nested ovclash_suite_run_ovstage_owner_operation calls and the last-error getters are allowed.

Parameters:

  • operation – Caller-owned callback. Must not be null.

  • user_data – Borrowed callback state. May be null.

Returns:

Success when the callback returns 1. Error for an invalid callback, excessive nesting, callback failure or a native exception.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_attach_ovstage(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
const ovclash_ovstage_binding_t *binding,
)#

Borrows an existing ovstage Stage for the runtime.

Ownership and evaluation follow ovclash_ovstage_attach_stage. Active async and fetch handles are rejected, including completed handles that are not yet released. A successful attachment clears the scope set by ovclash_suite_set_scope. Replacing a Stage also clears results and pipelines. A non-empty scope turns the full-scene selection of the engine off. Like ovclash_suite_open_stage, a successful attachment turns it back on when the run settings in effect enable enable_full_scene. The settings in effect are those last applied with ovclash_suite_set_run_settings or, before any successful apply, the engine defaults, which enable it. A failed attachment keeps the previous binding.

The runtime is thread-compatible: serialize calls on one runtime, and do not reenter it from the owner evaluation callback.

Parameters:

  • runtime – An initialized Suite runtime using the ovstage backend. Must not be null.

  • binding – Caller-owned Stage, metadata and optional callback.

Returns:

Success, or error for invalid arguments, active work or attachment failure.

enum ovclash_suite_status_t#

Public C type contract.

Ownership: every ovclash_suite_string_t that the API returns is a borrowed view, owned by the handle or report that produced it. The producing API sets its lifetime. A noncursor data getter also replaces the previous scratch view of the same kind on its next read. A cursor view lasts until the cursor advances again or is destroyed. Copy the bytes before these events, before any mutation and before the owner is destroyed. Input strings and arrays are copied unless the function documents otherwise. On ovstage, report pointers can borrow runtime result storage. Destroy a report before advancing another pipeline step, rerunning or resetting its runtime, or invalidating that runtime’s results, and always before destroying the runtime. Copying a pointer does not extend its lifetime.

Units and layout: times are in seconds unless a function names USD time codes. Matrices are row-major 4x4 arrays of 16 doubles. Boolean fields use 0 for false and non-zero for true. Counts are element counts, not byte counts. All paths and text are UTF-8.

Threading: handles are not internally synchronized for concurrent mutation. Use a handle from one thread at a time, and serialize access when a handle is shared. The only exception is the concurrency that the async fetch snapshot and drain functions document. Independent data and model handles remain subject to database and filesystem locking. Runtime calls also follow the backend’s shared-state limits. Serialize OpenUSD runtimes across handles, because their cancellation, out-of-memory and underlying error state are process-global. Last-error text is thread-local for Suite operation failures, and handle-local where a handle-specific getter exists.

Error behavior: every public function returning ovclash_suite_result_t catches C++ exceptions, returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR and updates the thread-local last-error string. Destroy and cleanup functions return a result too. Call them explicitly, outside object finalizers, and check that result. Status code carried by ovclash_suite_result_t.

Values:

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS#

The call completed.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR#

The call failed; the documented last-error getter describes why.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE#

Only report-creation APIs return this: the record exists but its report is unavailable.

Accepted, persisted and read back, but has no effect in ovclash. 

In the Kit extension this setting selects a Fabric/USDRT scene traversal instead of
UsdStage::Traverse. Neither ovclash backend compiles that traversal. The ovstage backend
cannot have an equivalent toggle. Its only scene path is ovstage population, which reads
Fabric attributes, so there is no second traversal to switch to.

The setting is kept because it belongs to the Kit-compatible
ClashDetection.DEFAULT_SETTINGS table and is serialized into the stored settings of every
query. Setting it changes that serialized text and nothing else.
ovclash_suite_get_run_settings, and ovclash_get_settings on the canonical ABI, report the
stored value, so it round-trips without affecting clash results.

struct ovclash_suite_string_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_types.h>

Borrowed UTF-8 byte span.

Field catalogue:

  • ptr: first byte of the UTF-8 span. May be null only when length is 0.

  • length: byte count, excluding any trailing null. It counts bytes, not Unicode scalar values. Returned non-null spans are null-terminated for C compatibility. Read them by length, which excludes the trailing null. An empty returned string may be {NULL, 0}. Input spans are copied unless the receiving function documents borrowing, and need not be null-terminated.

This is a transitional local type. Its layout is byte-identical to ovx_string_t of ovx/string_types.h, which the canonical ovclash/ovclash.h uses as ovclash_string_t.

The local type remains because the core Suite headers (ovclash_suite.h, ovclash_suite_types.h, ovclash_suite_models.h and ovclash_suite_serializer.h) install as a self-contained group that includes no ovx/ header. An SDK consumer can then use the Suite API without the producer include tree. The optional ovstage extension ovclash_suite_ovstage.h includes ovclash/ovclash_ovstage.h, so it needs the ovstage ovx/ include tree, as the canonical header does.

This type is to become ovx_string_t once the Suite headers can always depend on the shared ovx/ tree, as the canonical header already does. The layouts are identical, so the change is a typedef swap, not an ABI break.

struct ovclash_suite_run_settings_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_types.h>

Runtime clash settings.

Field catalogue:

  • enable_log, enable_full_scene, dynamic, purge_permanent_dynamic_overlaps, purge_permanent_static_overlaps, only_find_duplicates, ignore_redundant_overlaps, enable_point_clouds, ignore_invisible_prims, use_usdrt, single_threaded, new_task_manager, coplanar, any_hit, quantized, tight_bounds, subcomponent_filtering, compute_max_local_depth, discard_touching_contacts, set_times: boolean flags; 0 is false and non-zero is true. dynamic is query metadata that the native runtime does not read; see the time fields below. set_times only enables the end_time >= start_time check. It does not decide whether start_time and end_time apply.

  • max_local_depth_mode: a mode selector, not a flag, although it sits between two flags in the struct. It selects one of three depth algorithms and must be in [0, 2]: 0 is minimal, the legacy fast estimate; 1 is medium, the default; 2 is high, medium refined with 64 sampling directions. Every accepted value computes a depth. The three algorithms can return different depths for the same pair, so “non-zero is true” does not hold for this field. It is read only while compute_max_local_depth is non-zero. That flag is the on/off gate, and this scale has no “disabled” value. The scale is therefore offset by one from ovclash_max_local_depth_mode_t in ovclash.h, where 0 is DISABLED and 1, 2 and 3 are MINIMAL, MEDIUM and HIGH. The two scales are not interchangeable: a canonical enumerator passed here selects the next higher algorithm, and 3 is rejected. The Suite maps between the two scales explicitly.

  • nb_tasks, tris_per_leaf: non-negative task and element counts stored as uint32_t. Their validation differs, so neither is a precedent for the other. tris_per_leaf must be in [1, 15]; other values are rejected. Default 15. The value goes to PxBVH34MidphaseDesc::numPrimsPerLeaf, which PhysX accepts in [2, 15]. Mesh cooking retries with a larger value, which recovers 1. A value above 15 would fail every mesh cook, and the run would report zero clashes instead of an error. nb_tasks accepts any value up to 1000000 and rejects larger ones. The backend then clamps it to its 256-task maximum without notice. The settings read back hold the value passed in, not the clamped one: a request for 5000 reads back as 5000 while canonical storage holds

    1. Only the legacy task manager uses this cap, and ovstage further bounds its workers by hardware concurrency and available work. The new task manager ignores nb_tasks, and single_threaded overrides both managers. Default 128. Fetch-and-save frame preparation for directory stores and for custom serializers with prepare_frame follows the same settings on both backends. The new manager uses Carbonite’s worker budget. The legacy manager uses std::thread workers bounded by nb_tasks, hardware concurrency and available work. single_threaded keeps preparation serial. Built-in SQLite frame encoding and all serializer writes stay on the driving thread. On ovstage, Suite face and outline preparation also follows the live runtime threading settings. Its workers drain before buffers are published or released.

  • overlap_code: an algorithm selector, not a count. Only 1, 2 and 3 select an algorithm. 0 and every other value, including values above 3, behave identically. Neither backend validates it, so an out-of-range value is accepted without an error. Default 3.

  • triangle_limit: the maximum number of triangles reported per overlapping pair. 0 means unlimited, not none. any_hit overrides it to 1. No maximum is validated. Default 0, unlimited.

  • dynamic_start_time, dynamic_end_time, static_time, start_time, end_time: source sample times in seconds. USD time-code conversion uses the stage’s effective rate, the time_codes_per_second of ovclash_suite_stage_timeline_data_t. Only start_time, end_time and time_codes_per_second select the sampled range, as startTime and endTime do in ovclash_settings_t. start_time == end_time is a single static sample at that time; otherwise the run samples [start_time, end_time]. dynamic, static_time, dynamic_start_time and dynamic_end_time are Kit-compatible query metadata. They are validated as finite, persisted into the query-settings JSON and round-tripped by ovclash_suite_get_run_settings, but the native runtime does not read them to choose samples. Resolve them into start_time and end_time before applying the settings, as the Python layer and the C++ sample do.

  • time_codes_per_second: sampling frequency in samples per second, independent of the stage’s effective rate. Zero keeps the single-sample fallback of legacy settings. Positive values set the spacing of multiple samples. Negative values are rejected.

  • tolerance, pose_epsilon, bounds_epsilon, depth_epsilon, contact_cutoff, point_size_override: finite tolerances or point sizes in source scene units. area_epsilon is an area in squared scene units. Finite negative values are accepted. Their meaning depends on the setting; a negative value is not a general unset sentinel. The engine stores these values as float, so each must fit the float range (depth_epsilon only while discard_touching_contacts is set). ovclash_suite_set_run_settings rejects a struct with any out-of-range field. It then keeps the previous settings and names the field in the last-error text.

struct ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_types.h>

Persistent clash-frame database record view.

Field catalogue:

  • identifier: persistent frame id, or -1 before insert.

  • clash_info_id: owning overlap id.

  • timecode: source sample time in seconds.

  • min_distance, max_local_depth: source scene-unit distances/depths.

  • overlap_elements: collided element count for this frame.

  • nb_usd_faces0/usd_faces0 and nb_usd_faces1/usd_faces1: authored USD face-index buffers; pointer may be null only when the matching count is 0.

  • nb_collision_outline_values/collision_outline_xyzxyz: outline float values in xyzxyz order, from hard triangle pairs only; clearance near-misses add none. The pointer may be null only when count is 0.

  • object_0_matrix/object_1_matrix: row-major 4x4 local-to-world transforms with 16 values. In-memory frame models copy these values without finite validation; JSON persistence rejects non-finite values.

  • penetration_depth_px/nx/py/ny/pz/nz: per-axis source scene-unit penetration depths.

  • nb_usd_points0/usd_points0: point index buffer for point-cloud clashes.

  • nb_usd_points0_sizes/usd_points0_sizes: point-size buffer with its own count; the pointer may be null only when this count is 0. Runtime-generated frames store one cloud-wide width when point indices are present. That width is the 0.0 sentinel when the scalar width varies or is unavailable. Imported records may carry per-point widths, so never infer this count from nb_usd_points0. Pointer fields are borrowed on output and copied on input.

Suite C API#

Runtime orchestration, synchronous and asynchronous pipelines, SQLite or JSON-directory persistence, and JSON/HTML export. Threading and Ownership gives the threading rules of runtime, data and model handles and the size-query rule of the functions that write text. Suite Workflows walks through a complete Suite program.

Runtime API

Per-function error catalogue for the runtime API: each runtime function returning ovclash_suite_result_t returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the requested stage, settings, scope, pipeline, query, report or persistence operation completed and the documented outputs are initialized.

It returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when:

  • a runtime handle, output pointer or required matrix pointer is null;

  • a string span is invalid or not UTF-8;

  • no stage is open, or the selected backend does not support the settings or scope;

  • the pipeline is in the wrong state, or a step, overlap, record or duplicate index is out of range;

  • native clash execution fails, or report buffers are missing or inconsistent;

  • a data handle supplied to the fast-save path is not writable;

  • allocation fails, or a C++ exception is caught.

ovclash_suite_get_last_error returns the runtime-specific detail, and ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error the thread-local detail.

Threading: callers serialize all access to a shared runtime or async handle. A runtime and every async handle it created share one serialization domain. No call on such an async handle may overlap any call on its runtime, ovclash_suite_get_last_error and ovclash_suite_destroy_runtime included. The async calls update the active-run guard and error text of the runtime, and destroying the runtime detaches its async handle. Poll progress from another thread only while no call on the runtime is in flight. Independent ovstage runtime handles may be used concurrently. OpenUSD runtime calls must also be serialized across handles, because cancellation, out-of-memory and underlying error state are process-global.

Ownership: the caller owns runtime-created report and async handles until it calls their matching destroy function. Runtime string and report views are borrowed from the owning runtime or report handle. On ovstage, report arrays borrow runtime result storage: destroy reports before rerunning or resetting the runtime or invalidating its results. Always destroy reports before their runtime.

A live fetch-and-save operation reserves its runtime until the fetch is destroyed, also after completion or failure. During that reservation, runtime destroy and reset, stage, settings and scope changes, pipeline creation and execution, and depth computation fail. Read-only access to results stays available during a synchronous fetch. An asynchronous fetch rejects every runtime call outside its worker until the fetch is destroyed. The guard relies on serialized caller access; it is neither a mutex nor a lease for separately created report handles. Destroy the fetch before retrying a rejected operation.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_create_runtime(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t **out_runtime,
)#

Creates a suite runtime handle.

Parameters:

out_runtime – Receives the created runtime handle. Must not be null and must be destroyed with ovclash_suite_destroy_runtime.

Returns:

Success when the handle is allocated. Failure when out_runtime is null, allocation fails, or an exception is caught.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_destroy_runtime(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
)#

Destroys a suite runtime handle.

Destruction does not cancel an unfinished pipeline started by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. Like ovclash_release_context, it blocks until that run completes and discards its results. Call ovclash_suite_async_cancel first to stop the run early. The async handle stays caller-owned; release it with ovclash_suite_async_destroy afterwards. No call on that handle may be in flight during destruction. Afterwards every call on it except ovclash_suite_async_destroy fails.

Parameters:

runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. May be null.

Returns:

Success when the handle is released or runtime is null. Failure if a fetch is alive or cleanup catches an unexpected exception. An active-fetch rejection retains the runtime; destroy the fetch before retrying runtime destruction.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_reset_runtime(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
)#

Clears runtime state while keeping the handle alive.

Parameters:

runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success, or error for a null runtime, an active async pipeline or fetch, or a reset the backend rejects.

ovclash_suite_string_t ovclash_suite_get_last_error(
const ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
)#

Returns the last error message recorded on a runtime handle.

While an async fetch owner is alive, returns the thread-local access-rejection diagnostic of the caller without reading runtime state. ovclash_suite_fetch_async_get_last_error returns the diagnostic of the operation. Destroy that owner before querying runtime state.

Parameters:

runtime – Runtime handle to query. May be null. A null handle, or one with no recorded error, falls back to the thread-local last error; the view is empty only when that is empty too.

ovclash_suite_string_t ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error(void)#

Returns the last thread-local error recorded by a Suite API without a handle-local error channel.

Once the thread-local storage of the calling thread is destroyed, a failure records a static notice instead of its detail. At exit, glibc destroys that storage of the main thread before static destructors run.

Returns:

Library-owned UTF-8 string view, valid until the next Suite API call on the same thread.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_named_constant(
ovclash_suite_string_t name,
int64_t *out_value,
)#

Looks up a public numeric ABI constant by its C identifier.

Dynamic language bindings use it to derive enum, flag, schema-version and compatibility constants from the native library instead of duplicating integer literals. The supported names are:

  • the enumerators of the OVCLASH_SUITE_* enums;

  • the alias spellings OVCLASH_OVERLAP_TYPE_* and OVCLASH_OVERLAP_REPORT_*, without the PAIR or FLAG infix of ovclash.h;

  • the schema versions OVCLASH_SUITE_CLASH_QUERY_VERSION, OVCLASH_SUITE_CLASH_INFO_VERSION, OVCLASH_SUITE_CLASH_FRAME_INFO_VERSION and OVCLASH_SUITE_POINT_CLOUD_SETTINGS_VERSION;

  • the model default OVCLASH_SUITE_POINT_CLOUD_SETTINGS_MAX_LOD_LEVEL.

The enumerator names of the canonical ovclash.h are not looked up, and an unknown name fails.

Parameters:

  • name – Length-prefixed constant identifier, for example OVCLASH_SUITE_SETTING_DYNAMIC.

  • out_value – Receives the constant value. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_stage_timeline_data(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_stage_timeline_data_t *out_data,
)#

Reads the timeline metadata of the currently opened stage.

Fails when no stage is open. Use it to convert between the time codes of the stage and the seconds in start_time and end_time of ovclash_suite_run_settings_t, which select the sampled range: seconds = time code / time_codes_per_second. It can also supply a dynamic range from the stage. static_time, dynamic_start_time and dynamic_end_time are persisted query metadata only; the runtime does not read them. Available on both backends without the OpenUSD Python bindings.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_data – Receives the stage timeline record; zeroed before validation. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_open_stage(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_string_t stage_path,
)#

Opens a file-backed USD stage for clash detection.

A successful open clears the scope set by ovclash_suite_set_scope; set it again for a scoped run on the new stage. A failed open keeps it. A non-empty scope turns the engine’s full-scene selection off; a successful open turns it back on when the run settings in effect enable enable_full_scene, so a run with no new scope covers the whole new stage. Those are the settings last applied with ovclash_suite_set_run_settings or, before any successful apply, the engine defaults, which enable it.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • stage_path – Length-prefixed filesystem path to the USD stage.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_set_run_settings(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
const ovclash_suite_run_settings_t *settings,
)#

Applies clash runtime settings.

The threading settings may change after the pipeline finishes and before ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin, for example parallel detection followed by single-threaded fetching. Completed results are kept. To switch the fetch mode, read the current settings first (ovclash_suite_get_default_run_settings when none were applied, because ovclash_suite_get_run_settings then returns a zeroed struct) and change only the threading fields. Finish or cancel an active async pipeline, and destroy any live fetch operation, before changing settings.

A scope set by ovclash_suite_set_scope survives a settings change, in either call order. The floating-point fields that the engine stores as float must lie within the float range: pose_epsilon, bounds_epsilon, area_epsilon, contact_cutoff, tolerance, point_size_override, and depth_epsilon while discard_touching_contacts is set.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • settings – Settings to apply. Must not be null. The struct is copied.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the engine accepted the settings. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR, keeping the previous settings, when an argument is null, an async pipeline or a fetch is alive, a double is non-finite, a float-stored field exceeds the float range, max_local_depth_mode exceeds 2, nb_tasks exceeds 1000000, tris_per_leaf is outside [1, 15], time_codes_per_second is negative, set_times is non-zero with end_time below start_time, or the engine rejects them. A failure to re-apply the cached scope afterwards also returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR, with the new settings already in effect.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_run_settings(
const ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_run_settings_t *out_settings,
)#

Reads back the run settings currently applied to a runtime.

The inverse of ovclash_suite_set_run_settings. Reports the last settings that the engine accepted; a rejected apply leaves the previous values in place. Before any successful apply it reports a zero-initialized struct. That struct differs from ovclash_suite_get_default_run_settings, and the runtime does not use it either: until then, detection and fetch preparation run with the engine defaults, the ovclash_reset_settings table.

Suite-only fields that the canonical settings struct cannot carry (dynamic, static_time, set_times, depth_epsilon, …) round-trip here, although the engine cannot return them.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_settings – Receives the current settings. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS, or an error status if either argument is null or an async fetch owner is alive (nothing is written).

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_set_scope(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
const ovclash_suite_string_t *prim_paths1,
size_t prim_paths1_count,
const ovclash_suite_string_t *prim_paths2,
size_t prim_paths2_count,
)#

Restricts clash detection to one or two sets of USD prim paths.

The paths are copied into runtime state and forwarded to ovclash_set_scope_paths. paths1 alone means paths1 against itself, both non-empty means paths1 against paths2, and both empty means no scope. The runtime handle is mutated only after argument validation succeeds. The runtime applies the copy again after each ovclash_suite_set_run_settings, and before ovclash_suite_create_pipeline builds, so scope and settings may be set in either order. A successful ovclash_suite_open_stage or ovstage attachment clears the scope.

A non-empty scope turns the full-scene selection of the engine off. A both-empty scope, a successful open or an attachment turns it back on when the run settings in effect enable enable_full_scene. The settings in effect are those last applied with ovclash_suite_set_run_settings or, before any successful apply, the engine defaults, which enable it. An unscoped run therefore selects the whole stage, whichever of scope and settings was set last. With enable_full_scene cleared, an unscoped run selects nothing.

Threading: callers serialize access to a shared runtime while changing the scope. Independent ovstage runtime handles may be configured concurrently.

Example: 

ovclash_suite_string_t a[] = { { "/World/A", 8 } };
ovclash_suite_string_t b[] = { { "/World/B", 8 } };
ovclash_suite_set_scope(runtime, a, 1, b, 1);

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • prim_paths1 – Array of first-scope prim paths. May be null when prim_paths1_count is zero.

  • prim_paths1_count – Number of entries in prim_paths1.

  • prim_paths2 – Array of second-scope prim paths. May be null when prim_paths2_count is zero.

  • prim_paths2_count – Number of entries in prim_paths2.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the scope is accepted. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when runtime is null, an async pipeline or a fetch is alive, either array pointer is null with a non-zero count, any string span is invalid or non-UTF-8, the engine rejects an entry (empty, containing an embedded NUL character, or not an absolute prim path), memory allocation fails, or a C++ exception is caught. Error detail is available through ovclash_suite_get_last_error(runtime) and ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_create_pipeline(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t *out_step_count,
)#

Builds the runtime pipeline for the currently opened stage, settings, and scope.

Preconditions: configure settings and scope first when non-default behavior is needed. The runtime must not be running an async pipeline. Building the pipeline needs no stage; a missing stage surfaces from ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_step or the async run.

Side effects: applies the scope set by ovclash_suite_set_scope again and, on success, replaces any previously prepared pipeline and stores the new step count. A failed ovstage build keeps the previous pipeline. Runtime result buffers are populated only when ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_step or ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async runs. A failure to apply the scope or to create the pipeline leaves *out_step_count at 0.

Ownership: the caller keeps owning runtime. out_step_count receives a scalar value and owns no memory.

Threading: callers serialize access to runtime while creating or running a pipeline. Independent ovstage runtime handles may create pipelines concurrently.

Example: 

uint32_t steps = 0;
if (ovclash_suite_create_pipeline(runtime, &steps).status == OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS) {
    for (uint32_t index = 0; index < steps; ++index) {
        ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_step(runtime, index);
    }
}

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_step_count – Receives the number of pipeline steps. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the pipeline is prepared and out_step_count is initialized. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when runtime or out_step_count is null, an async pipeline or a fetch is alive, applying the scope again fails, backend pipeline creation fails, an unsupported backend capability is requested, allocation fails, or a C++ exception is caught. ovclash_suite_get_last_error(runtime) and ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error return the failure detail.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_pipeline_step_data(

uint32_t step_index,
ovclash_suite_step_data_t *out_step_data,
)#

Describes one planned pipeline step.

progress is step_index / nb_steps and finished marks the last step; neither reflects execution. Use ovclash_suite_async_get_step_data for live progress.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • step_index – Zero-based pipeline step index.

  • out_step_data – Receives step name, index, count, progress, and finished state. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async(

Starts asynchronous execution of the prepared pipeline.
