ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_async_is_running(
ovclash_suite_async_t *async_handle,
uint32_t *out_running,
)#

Polls whether an asynchronous pipeline is still running.

Parameters:

  • async_handle – Async handle returned by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. Must not be null.

  • out_running – Receives 1 while execution is still active, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_async_get_step_data(
ovclash_suite_async_t *async_handle,
ovclash_suite_step_data_t *out_step_data,
)#

Reads progress information from an asynchronous pipeline.

progress is forwarded unclamped from ovclash_get_pipeline_step_data_async. On OpenUSD, a poll that races the work-counter reset of a phase can report it outside [0, 1] or non-finite. Consumers clamp it and treat a non-finite value as unknown. ovstage reports a locked, clamped snapshot. Clash results are unaffected.

Parameters:

  • async_handle – Async handle returned by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. Must not be null.

  • out_step_data – Receives the active step information. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_async_finish(
ovclash_suite_async_t *async_handle,
)#

Waits for asynchronous pipeline execution to finish and consumes the engine run.

After finish or cancel, polling, finish, and cancel calls on the same handle return OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR. Release the remaining handle with ovclash_suite_async_destroy.

Parameters:

async_handle – Async handle returned by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_async_cancel(
ovclash_suite_async_t *async_handle,
)#

Requests cancellation of asynchronous pipeline execution.

Blocks until the worker stops and consumes the engine run. Release the remaining handle with ovclash_suite_async_destroy; a later ovclash_suite_async_finish on it returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR.

Parameters:

async_handle – Async handle returned by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_async_destroy(
ovclash_suite_async_t *async_handle,
)#

Releases an asynchronous pipeline handle.

An unfinished run is finished first, blocking until it completes. The handle may outlive its runtime; after ovclash_suite_destroy_runtime this only frees it. While the runtime is alive, this call, like every other call on the handle, must not overlap a call on that runtime.

Parameters:

async_handle – Async handle returned by ovclash_suite_run_pipeline_async. May be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_nb_overlaps(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t *out_overlap_count,
)#

Queries the number of detected overlap groups.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_overlap_count – Receives the overlap group count. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_nb_duplicates(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t *out_duplicate_count,
)#

Queries the number of detected duplicate mesh pairs.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_duplicate_count – Receives the duplicate pair count. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_overlap_data(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t overlap_index,
uint32_t record_index,
ovclash_suite_overlap_data_t *out_data,
)#

Reads detailed data for one overlap record.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • overlap_index – Zero-based overlap group index.

  • record_index – Zero-based record/frame index inside the overlap group.

  • out_data – Receives overlap names, hashes, counts, type, time, distance, and depth. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_duplicate_data(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t duplicate_index,
ovclash_suite_duplicate_mesh_data_t *out_data,
)#

Reads duplicate mesh data for one duplicate pair.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • duplicate_index – Zero-based duplicate mesh pair index.

  • out_data – Receives duplicate names, hashes, triangle count and time; the matrices stay zero. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_query_stats(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_query_stats_t *out_stats,
)#

Queries runtime statistics for the last pipeline execution.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • out_stats – Receives mesh and point cloud counters. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_compute_overlap_max_local_depth(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t overlap_index,
uint32_t record_index,
double *out_depth,
)#

Computes the maximum local depth for an already detected overlap record.

Not supported for point-cloud overlaps. The backends compute the depth from the mesh pair behind the record, so an overlap whose ovclash_suite_overlap_data_t::type is OVCLASH_SUITE_OVERLAP_POINT_CLOUD_MESH fails here. Test the overlap type before the call.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • overlap_index – Zero-based overlap group index.

  • record_index – Zero-based record/frame index inside the overlap group.

  • out_depth – Receives the computed maximum local depth. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_compute_max_local_depth(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_string_t mesh_path0,
const double *matrix0,
ovclash_suite_string_t mesh_path1,
const double *matrix1,
double *out_depth,
)#

Computes maximum local depth between two mesh instances.

Both paths must resolve to UsdGeomMesh prims. A UsdGeomPoints path is never loaded as a mesh, so the call fails for it. A stage must be open, but no pipeline run is required: the call loads and cooks the two meshes with the settings in effect. It fails unless those settings enable compute_max_local_depth, which the engine defaults do not. max_local_depth_mode selects the algorithm. *out_depth is unchanged on failure.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • mesh_path0 – Length-prefixed USD path of the first mesh.

  • matrix0 – Row-major 4x4 transform for the first mesh. Must point to 16 doubles.

  • mesh_path1 – Length-prefixed USD path of the second mesh.

  • matrix1 – Row-major 4x4 transform for the second mesh. Must point to 16 doubles.

  • out_depth – Receives the computed maximum local depth. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_compute_penetration_depth(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_string_t mesh_path0,
const double *matrix0,
ovclash_suite_string_t mesh_path1,
const double *matrix1,
double dir_x,
double dir_y,
double dir_z,
ovclash_suite_depenetration_data_t *out_data,
)#

Computes penetration depth along a supplied direction between two mesh instances.

Both paths must resolve to UsdGeomMesh prims. A UsdGeomPoints path is never loaded as a mesh, so the call fails for it.

The direction need not be normalized; it is converted to float before the query. Each component must be finite and no larger in magnitude than FLT_MAX. The square of at least one float component must be a normal float; squares below FLT_MIN count as zero, because PhysX flushes them. The squared float length must not overflow. A zero direction, a direction too small to survive the conversion, and a direction whose length overflows float are rejected with an error rather than queried.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • mesh_path0 – Length-prefixed USD path of the first mesh.

  • matrix0 – Row-major 4x4 transform for the first mesh. Must point to 16 doubles.

  • mesh_path1 – Length-prefixed USD path of the second mesh.

  • matrix1 – Row-major 4x4 transform for the second mesh. Must point to 16 doubles.

  • dir_x – X component of the query direction.

  • dir_y – Y component of the query direction.

  • dir_z – Z component of the query direction.

  • out_data – Receives penetration direction and depth. Must not be null. A failure other than the rejection while a fetch is alive, or a call made from inside an ovstage owner operation, leaves a zero direction and depth -1.0.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_create_overlap_report(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t overlap_index,
uint32_t record_index,
uint32_t flags,
ovclash_suite_overlap_report_t **out_report,
)#

Creates a detailed overlap report containing requested face, point, outline, and matrix buffers.

Destroy the report before advancing another pipeline step, rerunning or resetting the runtime, invalidating its results, or destroying the runtime. The runtime must stay alive until the report is destroyed. On ovstage, report buffers borrow storage from the runtime results; creating a report does not extend the lifetime of that storage.

Point-cloud overlaps are supported. For them the report holds the indices of the clashing points (OVCLASH_SUITE_OVERLAP_REPORT_POINTS0) and the cloud-wide point_size0. That size is 0.0 when per-point authored widths that actually vary size the cloud; this API does not resolve those widths. A uniform widths array holds one value repeated per point. USD’s default “vertex” interpolation makes an exporter write such an array for a cloud with one size. For such an array the report holds that single width on the ovstage backend, and 0.0 on the OpenUSD backend, whose sizing lives in the shared engine. See “Point-cloud widths in reports” in the Limitations guide of the ovclash documentation.

Faces and collision outlines are reported for mesh-vs-mesh pairs only. Both backends ignore the flags that do not apply to the pair type, and OVCLASH_SUITE_OVERLAP_REPORT_DEFAULT and OVCLASH_SUITE_OVERLAP_REPORT_FACES select nothing here. Both backends compute collision outlines under the floating-point controls of the calling thread, so reports created under different rounding or denormal modes can differ. A Suite runtime always uses the default ovstage matrix decomposition, so its outlines always follow the calling thread’s controls.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • overlap_index – Zero-based overlap group index.

  • record_index – Zero-based record/frame index inside the overlap group.

  • flags – Bitmask of ovclash_suite_overlap_report_flag_t values selecting report buffers.

  • out_report – Receives the created report handle. Must not be null and must be destroyed with ovclash_suite_destroy_overlap_report.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS with a report; OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE with a null report when the record exists but cannot provide report data; OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR for invalid arguments, extraction failures, cancellation, or allocation failure.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_overlap_report_view(
ovclash_suite_overlap_report_t *report,
ovclash_suite_overlap_report_view_t *out_view,
)#

Returns the buffer view for an overlap report.

Parameters:

  • report – Report handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_overlap_report. Must not be null.

  • out_view – Receives borrowed buffer pointers and copied counts, point size and transforms. Must not be null. The view does not extend the report or runtime-buffer lifetime.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_destroy_overlap_report(
ovclash_suite_overlap_report_t *report,
)#

Destroys an overlap report handle and invalidates views that reference its buffers.

The runtime that created the report must still be alive.

Parameters:

report – Report handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_overlap_report. May be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_create_clash_info(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
uint32_t overlap_index,
uint32_t record_index,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
ovclash_suite_clash_info_view_t *out_clash_info,
ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_view_t *out_frame_info,
ovclash_suite_overlap_report_t **out_report,
)#

Builds suite-level clash info and frame info records for one overlap record.

num_records of the clash info is the engine record count of the whole overlap group, not the number of records that can be reported. ovclash_suite_runtime_save_overlap_to_data persists the surviving count instead, so the two disagree for an overlap that loses records. The report is created with FACES0, FACES1 and OUTLINE for a mesh pair, and with POINTS0 for a point-cloud pair. The returned report and the borrowed frame buffers follow the runtime and report lifetime rules of ovclash_suite_create_overlap_report.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null.

  • overlap_index – Zero-based overlap group index.

  • record_index – Zero-based record/frame index inside the overlap group.

  • query_id – Query identifier to store in the returned clash info.

  • tolerance – Tolerance recorded in the returned clash info.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon recorded in the returned clash info.

  • out_clash_info – Receives the clash info view. Must not be null. Its strings are runtime-owned: they stay valid after the report is destroyed, but only until the next ovclash_suite_create_clash_info, ovclash_suite_runtime_save_overlap_to_data or fetch-and-save capture on the same runtime, whether or not that call succeeds, or until the runtime is destroyed. Copy them to keep them longer.

  • out_frame_info – Receives the frame info view. Its buffers are borrowed through out_report and follow the lifetime rules of ovclash_suite_create_overlap_report. Must not be null.

  • out_report – Receives the report associated with borrowed frame buffers. Must not be null and must be destroyed with ovclash_suite_destroy_overlap_report.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the clash-info views are populated. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_UNAVAILABLE when a valid record has no available report; the output views are then empty and out_report is null. Only this status permits skipping a frame. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when the runtime, an output pointer, a backend index, the report buffers or an allocation fails. ovclash_suite_get_last_error(runtime) and ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error return the failure detail.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_save_overlap_to_data(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
uint32_t overlap_index,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
uint32_t commit,
int64_t *out_identifier,
uint32_t *out_frame_count,
)#

Processes and persists one runtime overlap directly into a suite data store.

It persists one overlap through the fetch-and-save engine, without approval comparison or reconciliation. It keeps the editable metadata of an existing overlap with the same query_id and overlap id, and updates runtime-owned fields from the current clash result. It replaces frame rows in bulk, and commits explicitly like the data-store APIs.

A record that the engine still resolves but cannot produce an overlap report for is dropped, as in the Kit extension, rather than failing the whole overlap. A record index that the engine does not know still fails the save, and an overlap whose records all fail to report is an error. The persisted overlap therefore describes only the surviving records. Its num_records and *out_frame_count are the surviving count, and its start_time and end_time are the sample times of the first and last surviving record. An *out_frame_count below the engine record count of the overlap (nb_records from ovclash_suite_get_overlap_data) is thus a legitimate SUCCESS outcome. A caller that needs to know whether records were lost compares the two itself. ovclash_suite_create_clash_info reports the engine count in its num_records, so the two APIs disagree about the same overlap once a record is dropped.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime handle returned by ovclash_suite_create_runtime. Must not be null and must own completed results. Rejected while an async pipeline or a fetch is alive on it.

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null and must be writable. Rejected while a fetch is alive on it.

  • overlap_index – Zero-based overlap group index in runtime results.

  • query_id – Query identifier to assign to the persisted overlap.

  • tolerance – Tolerance stored on the persisted overlap.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon stored on the persisted overlap.

  • commit – Non-zero to commit after this overlap. Zero leaves the serializer transaction open for a later commit.

  • out_identifier – Receives the persisted overlap identifier. Must not be null.

  • out_frame_count – Receives the number of persisted frame records, which can be fewer than the overlap’s engine record count. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS on success; OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when arguments, runtime results, report buffers, data store state, or storage writes fail. Failure text is available through ovclash_suite_get_last_error(runtime), ovclash_suite_data_get_last_error(data), or ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t *serializer,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
uint32_t include_duplicates,
uint32_t resolve_stale,
ovclash_suite_fetch_and_save_t **out_fetch,
)#

Begins incremental fetching, serialization and saving of the runtime’s completed results into a query.

Pass a null serializer to use the built-in SQLite or directory serializer of the live data handle. For a custom destination, pass a serializer callback table and null data. Exactly one of data and serializer must be non-null; both or neither returns an error. The custom table is copied, and its user_data and destination must outlive the operation. The required callbacks must be non-null, and prepare_frame and release_frame must be both null or both set. See the callback contract in ovclash_suite_serializer.h.

Threading: the operation uses the runtime threading settings single_threaded, new_task_manager and nb_tasks: the applied ones or, before any successful ovclash_suite_set_run_settings, the engine defaults. Frame preparation of the directory serializer and of an optional custom serializer captures these settings at begin and may use workers. Built-in SQLite frame encoding stays on the driving thread. Report extraction reads the live runtime settings, so set threading before begin and leave it unchanged until destroy. Serializer writes and report acquisition are serialized. On ovstage, face and outline preparation can use workers on immutable captured inputs. Every started worker drains before prepared buffers are published, or released after a failure or cancellation. Report release and SQLite frame encoding stay on the driving thread. last_modified_by uses the user name captured once at begin, refreshed for each new operation. No fetch work runs between calls.

Reservation: the operation reserves its runtime and built-in destination until it is destroyed, also after completion or failure. In that time, runtime destruction, reset and settings changes are rejected, as are destination writes, reopen, save-as, close and destruction. A custom destination must enforce its own lifetime and connection stability. Serialize access to these handles; the reservation does not make concurrent API calls safe.

States: existing overlap identifiers and annotations are kept. With resolve_stale nonzero, re-detected normal and duplicate overlaps become ACTIVE, except an APPROVED clash whose detected contents are exactly unchanged. Built-in data handles supply the comparison reader automatically. A custom serializer without a reader conservatively sets re-detected clashes to ACTIVE. The comparison covers type, tolerance, depth epsilon, object paths and mesh checksums, aggregate results, and the complete ordered frame contents (times, matrices, metrics and geometry). Floating-point equality uses no epsilon and ignores the denormal controls of the caller. Signed zeros compare equal, while NaN never proves unchanged contents. Stored overlap and frame row identifiers, review fields, timestamps and user penetration-depth annotations are excluded. The query and the ordered pair hash establish result identity; a matching overlap hash alone does not prove unchanged contents. With resolve_stale zero, stored states are kept. New overlaps start NEW and are not promoted during their first fetch. Absent results are marked not present in either mode, and become RESOLVED when resolve_stale is nonzero.

Transactions: after capture, the reconciliation of absent results can span several next calls, and its changes stay pending until the final commit. Destroying an unfinished operation performs no further reconciliation. It keeps completed writes and earlier reconciliation changes, unless the cleanup of an incomplete overlap fails and requires a full rollback. Fetch-and-save is not all-or-nothing; ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_next describes the rollback rules. The storage transaction belongs to the data handle, so completion or a full rollback also affects unrelated writes already pending on that handle. An initialization failure does not roll back those earlier writes.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime with completed results. Must not be null or have an active async pipeline.

  • data – Live built-in destination when serializer is null; otherwise must be null.

  • serializer – Optional custom serializer. Null selects the data handle’s storage backend.

  • query_id – Identifier of the owning stored query.

  • tolerance – Tolerance recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • include_duplicates – Nonzero to persist duplicate results. Pass the setting of the owning query; it does not depend on runtime settings changed after detection.

  • resolve_stale – Nonzero to resolve absent clashes and set re-detected normal and duplicate overlaps to ACTIVE, preserving APPROVED only when detected contents are exactly unchanged. Zero preserves stored states.

  • out_fetch – Receives an owned operation; cleared on failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success after initialization, or error for invalid arguments or destination reads. Error text is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin_with_reader(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t *serializer,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_saved_data_reader_t *reader,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
uint32_t include_duplicates,
uint32_t resolve_stale,
ovclash_suite_fetch_and_save_t **out_fetch,
)#

Begins fetching with an optional saved-data reader for a custom serializer.

Follows the lifetime, transaction and state rules of fetch_and_save_begin. A reader enables the exact comparison of approved overlaps before replacement. Built-in data supplies its own reader, so pass a null reader with a built-in destination. With resolve_stale nonzero and no custom reader, unchanged content cannot be proven, and re-detected approved custom overlaps become ACTIVE. The reader table is copied, and both callbacks are required when it is supplied. Its user_data and saved destination must outlive the operation. The reader runs on the driving thread and must return the complete detected header and the ordered saved frame payload. Its optional close callback releases saved-reader resources on that same thread, also when an unfinished operation is destroyed. Drive and destroy synchronous fetching on a thread that suits the custom reader resources. A failed close may be retried during cleanup. See ovclash_suite_fetch_saved_data_reader_t for the lifetimes of callback outputs.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime with completed results. Must not be null or have an active async pipeline.

  • data – Live built-in destination when serializer is null; otherwise must be null.

  • serializer – Optional custom serializer. Null selects the data handle’s storage backend.

  • reader – Optional custom saved-data reader. Must be null with a built-in data handle.

  • query_id – Identifier of the owning stored query.

  • tolerance – Tolerance recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • include_duplicates – Nonzero to persist the owning query’s duplicate results.

  • resolve_stale – Nonzero to update states, retaining APPROVED only for exactly unchanged detected contents. Zero preserves stored states.

  • out_fetch – Receives an owned operation; cleared on failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success after initialization, or error for invalid arguments or destination reads. Error text is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_next(
ovclash_suite_fetch_and_save_t *fetch,
double *out_progress,
uint32_t *out_complete,
)#

Fetches, serializes and saves the next part of the work.

Each call attempts at most 1024 runtime frame reports, across approval comparison and capture, and advances at most 1024 overlaps. It also stops when the acquired runtime report payload reaches 8 MiB; one indivisible report may exceed that threshold. A long overlap resumes on a later call, with its savepoint kept open. Reconciliation scans at most 1024 stored identifiers per call. These are work bounds, not wall-clock guarantees; begin enumerates all existing identifiers. No borrowed report or active preparation task survives a return; serializer scratch allocations may be reused. Serialize access to the operation, runtime and destination; reentrant next and destroy calls are rejected.

Failure and transaction behavior, identical in single-threaded and parallel modes:

  • A serializer callback that reports failure during saved-result reads, writes, reconciliation or transaction handling requests a ROLLBACK of the entire pending transaction. That includes the batches of earlier calls and any other uncommitted writes on the destination. Data committed earlier is kept.

  • Extraction, frame preparation, scheduling or other native processing failures keep the pending overlaps completed earlier. ABORT_OVERLAP restores an incomplete streamed overlap. When that cleanup reports failure, the engine requests a full ROLLBACK instead.

  • Completion reconciles absent overlaps and calls the idempotent BEGIN before COMMIT, even for empty results, which publishes other pending writes too. Stopping between calls leaves completed writes pending. Destroying the operation restores an unfinished overlap. It keeps completed writes, unless ABORT_OVERLAP fails and cleanup must fall back to a full ROLLBACK.

Custom serializers must implement these transaction callbacks; the engine cannot guarantee recovery when their rollback fails. Closing or destroying built-in data attempts to commit the remaining pending writes. Cleanup after an extraction or preparation failure, or after abandonment, can therefore persist partial results.

A failed operation must be destroyed; it cannot be resumed.

Parameters:

  • fetch – Operation returned by ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin. Must not be null.

  • out_progress – Receives monotone progress in [0,1]. Must not be null.

  • out_complete – Receives 1 after reconciliation and commit, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success after advancing, or error for invalid arguments, extraction, encoding or storage failures. Error text is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_get_counts(
ovclash_suite_fetch_and_save_t *fetch,
uint64_t *out_written,
uint64_t *out_total,
)#

Reads the exact counts of this operation, before its first step or after a successful step.

The counts include normal overlap groups and the duplicates selected at begin, not frames or destination rows that existed before. An incomplete streamed overlap does not count as written. Written results stay pending until next reports completion after reconciliation and commit, so written == total alone does not imply a commit. A later failure may roll pending writes back. The call performs no work. Serialize access as for next. Failed or executing operations are rejected.

Parameters:

  • fetch – Live operation returned by begin. Must not be null, failed or executing callbacks.

  • out_written – Receives the number of fully written result groups. Must not be null.

  • out_total – Receives the number of result groups selected at begin. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success with both counts, or error for invalid arguments or operation state. Error text is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_destroy(
ovclash_suite_fetch_and_save_t *fetch,
)#

Destroys an operation and releases its reservation of the runtime and destination.

Null is accepted. An unfinished overlap is aborted. Completed writes stay pending, unless the abort fails and requires a full rollback. Destroy the operation before its runtime or destination. Unlike this destructor, closing or destroying built-in data attempts to commit pending writes, including results kept after a fetch failure. A cleanup failure returns an error and still consumes the operation, so do not retry the destruction. A failed overlap abort is reported even when the fallback rollback succeeds. The one exception is a rejected reentrant destroy from a running callback, which leaves the operation alive.

Parameters:

fetch – Operation to consume. May be null. Destroy after success, failure or abandonment.

Returns:

Success after release, or error for cleanup failure or rejected reentrant destruction. Read ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error for the diagnostic.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_async(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t *serializer,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
uint32_t include_duplicates,
uint32_t resolve_stale,
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t **out_async,
)#

Starts fetch and save on one background worker, including serializer initialization and cleanup.

This is the asynchronous equivalent of the bounded fetch-and-save API. Serializer writes stay sequential; eligible frame preparation may use the existing parallel scheduler of the runtime. The runtime and the built-in destination are leased exclusively until the returned handle is destroyed, also after finish or cancel. Calls from other threads cannot access the state of either owner, and the caller receives the rejection diagnostics. Native driver callbacks keep the read access that capture needs; preparation workers do not inherit it. Owner mutations still reject the lease. Finish or destroy the detection pipeline handle before launching this operation.

A custom serializer callback table is copied, but its user_data and the objects it references must stay alive until destruction. Callbacks run on the background worker, and eligible preparation callbacks can run on scheduler workers. Choosing this API opts those callbacks into background execution. The synchronous bounded API keeps running callbacks on the calling thread.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime containing completed detection results. Must not be null.

  • data – Built-in destination, or null when a custom serializer is supplied.

  • serializer – Optional custom serializer callbacks. The built-in destination is used when null.

  • query_id – Identifier of the owning stored query.

  • tolerance – Tolerance recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • include_duplicates – Non-zero to persist duplicate results too.

  • resolve_stale – Non-zero to reconcile stale overlap records after successful fetching.

  • out_async – Receives the owned operation handle, or null on launch failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS when launched; ERROR for invalid arguments, busy owners, live destination cursors, or launch failure. Worker failures are reported by finish and the operation error accessor.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_async_with_reader(
ovclash_suite_runtime_t *runtime,
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t *serializer,
const ovclash_suite_fetch_saved_data_reader_t *reader,
int64_t query_id,
double tolerance,
double depth_epsilon,
uint32_t include_duplicates,
uint32_t resolve_stale,
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t **out_async,
)#

Starts background fetch and save with a custom saved-history reader.

The ownership, synchronization and cleanup contracts of ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_async also apply here. A non-null reader requires a custom serializer and both read callbacks. Its table is copied before launch; user_data and the objects it references must stay alive until the async handle is destroyed. Saved-history reads run sequentially on the background worker before an overlap is replaced. The optional saved-reader close also runs on that worker, before the terminal outcome is published, also on cancellation and destruction. A close failure is reported without replacing an earlier processing diagnostic. A custom reader that keeps failing owns its remaining resources. With resolve_stale enabled, exactly unchanged APPROVED clashes keep their state, changed detected clashes become ACTIVE, and absent clashes become RESOLVED. With resolve_stale disabled, stored states are kept and saved-history reads are skipped.

Parameters:

  • runtime – Runtime containing completed detection results. Must not be null.

  • data – Built-in destination, or null when a custom serializer is supplied.

  • serializer – Optional custom serializer callbacks.

  • reader – Optional custom saved-history callbacks; null retains the reader-less behavior.

  • query_id – Identifier of the owning stored query.

  • tolerance – Tolerance recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • depth_epsilon – Depth epsilon recorded on normal overlaps; must be finite.

  • include_duplicates – Nonzero to persist duplicate results too.

  • resolve_stale – Nonzero to reconcile clash states after successful fetching.

  • out_async – Receives the owned handle, or null on launch failure. Must not be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS when launched; ERROR for invalid arguments, busy owners, live destination cursors, or launch failure. Worker failures are reported by finish and the operation error accessor.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_is_running(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
uint32_t *out_running,
)#

Reads a synchronized running snapshot.

Zero means that the worker and its cleanup have completed. Polling may overlap one finish or cancel call. Serialize control calls with each other; destruction must not overlap any call on the handle. The handle stays valid until it is explicitly destroyed.

Parameters:

  • async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null.

  • out_running – Receives non-zero while the worker runs. Must not be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS for a valid snapshot, or ERROR for invalid arguments.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_get_step_data(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
ovclash_suite_step_data_t *out_step_data,
)#

Reads a synchronized progress snapshot.

name is static storage. step_index names one of three phases: initialization, fetching, and reconciliation and commit; nb_steps is always 3. progress is the progress of the whole operation in [0, 1], independent of the phase index; only a successful committed completion reaches 1. finished is non-zero exactly when ovclash_suite_fetch_async_is_running would report zero: after success, failure or cancellation in any phase. step_index then still names the phase in which the operation stopped. Polling may overlap one finish or cancel call; destruction must not overlap any call on the handle.

Parameters:

  • async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null.

  • out_step_data – Receives the snapshot, including finished state. Must not be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS for a valid snapshot, or ERROR for invalid arguments.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_get_counts(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
uint64_t *out_written,
uint64_t *out_total,
uint32_t *out_initialized,
)#

Reads the synchronized written and total counters.

out_initialized is zero until initialization succeeds. An initialized total of zero denotes an empty result set. Output pointers must not be null. Polling may overlap one finish or cancel call; destruction must not overlap any call on the handle.

Parameters:

  • async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null.

  • out_written – Receives completed overlap and duplicate records.

  • out_total – Receives the total overlap and duplicate record count.

  • out_initialized – Receives non-zero once initialization succeeds.

Returns:

SUCCESS for a valid snapshot, or ERROR for invalid arguments.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_get_last_error(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
ovclash_suite_string_t *out_error,
)#

Reads the diagnostic of the operation.

The string storage stays valid until the handle is destroyed. Polling may overlap one finish or cancel call; destruction must not overlap any call on the handle.

Parameters:

  • async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null.

  • out_error – Receives an empty string while running, or the terminal diagnostic. Must not be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS for a valid snapshot, or ERROR for invalid arguments.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_finish(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
)#

Waits for the worker to complete and returns its outcome.

Failures are published on the calling thread. Repeated calls return the same outcome. The owner lease stays held until the handle is destroyed.

Parameters:

async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null; worker callback reentry is rejected.

Returns:

SUCCESS after committed completion; ERROR after cancellation, processing/cleanup failure, or invalid/reentrant use. Read the operation error accessor for terminal failure detail.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_cancel(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
)#

Requests cooperative cancellation and waits for cleanup.

Completed overlap records keep the partial-write semantics of the bounded API; an incomplete current overlap is aborted. A successful cancellation cleanup returns success, and a later finish reports the cancellation outcome. A cleanup failure returns an error. A call after completion is harmless.

Parameters:

async – Owned async fetch handle. Must not be null; worker callback reentry is rejected.

Returns:

SUCCESS after clean cancellation or successful completion; ERROR for processing/cleanup failure or invalid/reentrant use. Read the operation error accessor for failure detail.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_destroy(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t *async,
)#

Cancels and drains unfinished work, releases both owner leases, and consumes the handle.

The handle is consumed even when processing or cleanup failed. Destruction from the worker callbacks of the operation is rejected and leaves the handle alive, because those callbacks cannot join themselves. A failed wait also keeps ownership. Null is harmless. A foreign-language caller that can be interrupted while it handles the return can use ovclash_suite_fetch_async_destroy_owned to observe the consumption.

Parameters:

async – Owned async fetch handle to consume, or null.

Returns:

SUCCESS after clean cancellation/completion or for null; ERROR for processing/cleanup failure or reentrant use. When a consumed handle failed, the detail is published to the thread-local last error of the caller.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_fetch_async_destroy_owned(
ovclash_suite_fetch_async_t **async,
)#

Cancels and drains an owned handle, and publishes the consumption through the caller-owned pointer.

Once draining succeeds and destruction is accepted, sets *async to null before it releases the handle or publishes its terminal diagnostic, also when processing or cleanup failed. A rejected callback reentry or a failed wait leaves *async unchanged for a later retry. A pointer to a null handle succeeds. Serialize access to the pointer and the handle; destruction must not overlap another call on that handle.

Parameters:

async – Caller-owned handle pointer to consume. Must not be null; *async may be null.

Returns:

SUCCESS after clean cancellation/completion or for a null handle; ERROR for invalid arguments, processing/cleanup failure, a failed wait, or reentrant use. Read *async to distinguish accepted consumption from rejection before retrying destruction.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_format_int128_hex(
uint64_t hi,
uint64_t lo,
char *out_buffer,
size_t out_buffer_size,
size_t *out_required_size,
)#

Formats a 128-bit integer as the hexadecimal string used by clash identifiers.

The text is 0x followed by lowercase hexadecimal digits without leading zeros, for example 0x0 for zero. The locale does not affect it.

Parameters:

  • hi – High 64 bits of the integer.

  • lo – Low 64 bits of the integer.

  • out_buffer – Destination UTF-8 buffer. May be null when out_buffer_size is zero to query size.

  • out_buffer_size – Size of out_buffer in bytes, including room for the trailing null when a buffer is supplied.

size_t out_buffer_size,
size_t *out_required_size,
)#

Escapes text for HTML output using the suite export escaping rules.

Replaces the ampersand, less-than, greater-than, double-quote and apostrophe characters with HTML character references; every other byte is copied unchanged.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_current_timestamp(
char *out_buffer,
size_t out_buffer_size,
size_t *out_required_size,
)#

Returns the current timestamp using the suite storage timestamp format.

The text is the local time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff, with microseconds.

  • out_buffer_size – Size of out_buffer in bytes, including room for the trailing null when a buffer is supplied.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_current_user_name(
char *out_buffer,
size_t out_buffer_size,
size_t *out_required_size,
)#

Returns the current user name used for clash metadata.

Resolved from LOGNAME, USER, LNAME and USERNAME, then from the OS account: the password database entry of the real user ID on POSIX, GetUserNameW on Windows. A value that is not valid UTF-8 is skipped. The name is empty when no value qualifies.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_file_exists(
ovclash_suite_string_t path,
uint32_t *out_exists,
)#

Checks whether path names a regular file, following symbolic links (os.path.isfile parity).

Parameters:

  • path – Length-prefixed filesystem path to test.

  • out_exists – Receives 1 for a regular file, 0 for an empty or missing path, a directory, another file type, or a path containing an embedded NUL character. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_copy_file(
ovclash_suite_string_t source_path,
ovclash_suite_string_t target_path,
uint32_t follow_symlinks,
uint32_t *out_copied,
)#

Copies a regular file, or recreates a symbolic link, with shutil.copy semantics.

When target_path names an existing directory, the copy is written into it under the file name of the source. An existing target file is overwritten. The permission bits of the source are then applied to the target. With follow_symlinks zero and a symbolic-link source, the link itself is recreated at the target, which fails when the target already exists. Copy failures are reported through out_copied, not through the result code.

Parameters:

  • source_path – Length-prefixed source filesystem path.

  • target_path – Length-prefixed target filesystem path.

  • follow_symlinks – Non-zero to copy the linked target when source_path is a symbolic link.

  • out_copied – Receives 1 when the copy and the permission-bit copy both succeeded, otherwise 0: for an empty path, a missing or directory source, a failed copy, or a failed permission copy, which leaves the target already written. Must not be null.

Returns:

Failure when out_copied is null or a path is an invalid span, is not valid UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character; nothing is copied then.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_delete_file(
ovclash_suite_string_t path,
uint32_t *out_deleted,
)#

Deletes a non-directory filesystem entry without following symbolic links, with os.remove semantics: a symbolic link is removed, never its target.

Parameters:

  • path – Length-prefixed filesystem path to delete.

  • out_deleted – Receives 1 when an entry was removed, otherwise 0: for an empty or missing path, a directory, or a failed removal. Must not be null.

Returns:

Failure when out_deleted is null or path is an invalid span, is not valid UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character; nothing is deleted then.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_probe_legacy_clash_detection_file(
ovclash_suite_string_t file_path,
uint32_t *out_is_legacy_container,
uint32_t *out_has_sqlite_payload,
)#

Probes whether a file is a legacy .clashDetection container.

The legacy container format starts with a 16-byte clashDetection header, followed by a SQLite database payload. This function only probes the format; it neither opens the SQLite database nor migrates schemas.

Parameters:

  • file_path – Length-prefixed filesystem path to inspect. ptr may be null only when length is zero.

  • out_is_legacy_container – Receives 1 when the file starts with the legacy clashDetection magic, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

  • out_has_sqlite_payload – Receives 1 when the file is a legacy container and the embedded payload starts with a SQLite database header, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when the probe completed. Missing files, empty paths, short files and non-legacy files are reported through zero output values. Failure is reserved for invalid arguments, an invalid string span, invalid UTF-8, a path containing an embedded NUL character, or a caught exception.

Exports tabular rows to JSON.

Error behavior: fails when an input pointer and count pair is inconsistent, when an input string span has a null ptr with a non-zero length, or when a column name, row value or additional-info name or value is not valid UTF-8. It also fails when a column order is out of range for column_count, when row_value_count cannot cover row_count * column_count without overflow, or when a non-null out_buffer is too small. A null out_buffer with size zero remains the supported size query and succeeds when the export inputs are valid.

  • out_required_size – Receives the required byte count excluding the trailing null. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_export_text_destroy(
ovclash_suite_export_text_t *text,
)#

Destroys an owned export text handle.

Parameters:

text – Export text handle returned by an *_text export function. May be null.

Data Serialization API

Per-function error catalogue for the data API: each data function returning ovclash_suite_result_t returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the requested query, mutation, migration or serialization step completed and the documented outputs are initialized.

It returns OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when:

  • the data handle is invalid, an output pointer is null, or a required store is not open;

  • a string span is invalid or not UTF-8;

  • a counted array or nested frame buffer is null with a non-zero count;

  • a row, index or identifier is out of range;

  • schema compatibility or migration fails, or a legacy .clashDetection container cannot be extracted or written;

  • SQLite reports an error, or a filesystem operation fails;

  • an allocation fails, or a C++ exception is caught.

The handle-local ovclash_suite_data_get_last_error(data) and the thread-local ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error carry the concrete reason.

Scalar overlap and frame values stored in SQLite REAL columns reject NaN with OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR, rather than storing NULL and reading it back as zero. Infinities and finite values are supported. SQLite REAL does not preserve the sign of zero. Frame matrices still require finite values. Numeric BLOB arrays keep their bit-exact storage. Directory JSON records encode NaN and the infinities as the string tags “NaN”, “+Infinity” and “-Infinity”, default-time NaN values included, and keep the sign of a finite zero. Matrices require finite values on both backends.

Transactions: the storage transaction belongs to the data handle. Writes made with commit = 0 stay pending until ovclash_suite_data_commit, a later call with commit != 0, or close, which commits them. A mutation that fails after its storage write began rolls back the whole pending transaction, including earlier uncommitted writes that returned success; committed data is kept. Such failures include the value checks that the store makes while writing: a NaN REAL value on a SQLite store, a non-finite frame matrix on either store and, on a directory store, a record string containing NUL. They also include constraint, SQLite and filesystem errors, and a failed commit. Argument, open-state, fetch-reservation and not-found failures are reported before the write begins and leave pending writes untouched. When earlier batched writes must survive, validate the inputs, or commit, before a write that may fail.

Threading: callers serialize all access to a shared data handle. Independent data handles may be used concurrently, subject to SQLite and filesystem locking on the same database path. A directory root permits one open handle at a time; opening the same root elsewhere fails until the owning handle closes. For a deferred directory that does not exist yet, ownership begins at the first write. A live fetch reserves its destination until it is destroyed, and rejects public mutations. An asynchronous fetch also rejects reads of a built-in destination from every thread but its worker. Live overlap and frame cursors, even exhausted or empty ones, prevent open, save, save-as, migrate, close and destroy. Destroy dependent operations and cursors before changing the store lifecycle.

Ownership: the query, overlap, frame and point-cloud-settings getters that are not cursors borrow the per-kind scratch record of the data handle. Copy a view before another getter of the same kind, any mutation of the data handle, close or destroy. A cursor view belongs to its cursor instead and lasts until the next advance or the destruction of that cursor. Insert, update and replace functions copy all supplied views during the call.

Example: 

ovclash_suite_data_t* data = 0;
if (ovclash_suite_data_create(&data).status == OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS) {
    ovclash_suite_data_open(data, (ovclash_suite_string_t){ "scene.ovclashdb", 15 });
    uint32_t query_count = 0;
    ovclash_suite_data_get_query_count(data, &query_count);
    ovclash_suite_data_destroy(data);
}

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_create(
ovclash_suite_data_t **out_data,
)#

Creates a suite data/serialization handle backed by SQLite.

Parameters:

out_data – Receives the created data handle. Must not be null and must be destroyed with ovclash_suite_data_destroy.

Returns:

Success when the handle is allocated. Failure when out_data is null, allocation fails, or an exception is caught.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_create_directory(
ovclash_suite_data_t **out_data,
)#

Creates a Suite data handle backed by a human-readable directory of JSON records.

All data, cursor and runtime-save functions accept this handle. Open supplies the root directory path; file name extensions have no special meaning for this backend. Each query, point-cloud setting, overlap header and frame is stored separately. Existing SQLite stores keep using ovclash_suite_data_create. A record string containing an embedded NUL is rejected on write; an escaped NUL inside opaque query settings JSON is still supported. Symbolic links are rejected in the normalized absolute root path and its ancestors, in record paths and in reserved internal paths, also for save-as destinations. Callers may resolve trusted aliases explicitly before supplying a path. Windows directory junctions and volume mount points count as symbolic links, so a volume mounted only into a folder needs a drive letter to hold a store. Unnamed stores also require a system temporary-directory path without symbolic-link components.

Parameters:

out_data – Receives the allocated handle. Must not be null; destroy it with ovclash_suite_data_destroy after releasing its cursors and fetch operations.

Returns:

Success when the handle is allocated; failure for a null output or allocation failure.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_destroy(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
)#

Destroys a Suite data and serialization handle.

Attempts to commit pending writes before it closes and releases the handle. This is not a rollback operation: partial results kept after a failed or abandoned fetch can be saved. Destroy any fetch operations and cursors first. A failed commit requests a rollback and returns failure without freeing the data handle, so the caller can inspect it and clean up or retry.

Parameters:

data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. May be null.

Returns:

Success when the handle is released or data is null. Failure if a dependent operation/cursor is alive, commit/close fails, or cleanup throws. On failure the data handle remains owned by the caller; inspect its error and retry cleanup.

ovclash_suite_string_t ovclash_suite_data_get_last_error(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
)#

Returns the last error message recorded on a data handle.

While an async fetch owner is alive, returns the thread-local access-rejection diagnostic of the caller without reading store state. ovclash_suite_fetch_async_get_last_error returns the diagnostic of the operation. Destroy that owner before querying store state.

Parameters:

data – Data handle to query. May be null. A null handle, or one with no recorded error, falls back to the thread-local last error; the view is empty only when that is empty too.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_get_file_path(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
ovclash_suite_string_t *out_file_path,
)#

Returns the stored data path, a SQLite file or a directory root.

The path can stay set after close or a failed open; ovclash_suite_data_is_open reports the state. Unnamed stores return an empty path.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • out_file_path – Receives a string view owned by the data handle, valid until the stored path changes or the handle is destroyed. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when out_file_path is initialized. Failure follows the data API catalogue.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_get_file_size(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
uint64_t *out_file_size,
)#

Returns the on-disk size of an open, named store.

SQLite reports the size of its database file. Directory stores sum the regular files under the root, including internal files and unrelated exports. Unnamed stores fail.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • out_file_size – Receives the size in bytes. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when the size is known. Failure when no named store is open, the filesystem query fails, or the data API catalogue applies.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_structures_compatible(

)#

Checks whether the opened data structures match the supported schema versions.

Parameters:

  • out_compatible – Receives 1 when the opened structures are compatible, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when compatibility state is reported. Failure follows the data API catalogue.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_migration_to_latest_possible(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,

)#

Checks whether the opened data structures can be migrated to the latest supported schema.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • out_possible – Receives 1 when migration is possible, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when migration-possible state is reported. Failure follows the data API catalogue.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_deferred_file_creation_until_first_write_op(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
uint32_t *out_deferred,
)#

Queries whether file creation is deferred until the first write operation.

A new data handle defers creation (1).

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • out_deferred – Receives 1 when creation is deferred, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

Returns:

Success when the flag is reported. Failure follows the data API catalogue.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_set_deferred_file_creation_until_first_write_op(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
uint32_t value,
)#

Sets whether file creation is deferred until the first write operation.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • value – Non-zero to defer file creation until first write, otherwise zero.

Returns:

Success when the flag is updated. Failure follows the data API catalogue.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_open(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
ovclash_suite_string_t file_path,
)#

Opens or creates a suite data store.

A SQLite handle treats a path ending in .clashDetection, or a file with a valid legacy clashDetection header, as a legacy read container. It extracts the embedded SQLite payload to a temporary .ovclashdb file and opens that through the normal SQLite backend. Open and commit leave the original .clashDetection file unchanged. To write the legacy container format, pass a .clashDetection target to ovclash_suite_data_save or ovclash_suite_data_save_as. After a failed open of a .clashDetection path, a write fails rather than create a plain SQLite database under the container name. A directory handle opens a directory of individual JSON records, and suffixes such as .clashDetection have no special meaning for it. Neither backend converts the format of the other.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • file_path – Length-prefixed data file path. ptr may be null only when length is zero.

Returns:

Success when the store is opened or deferred creation is active. Failure when arguments are invalid, the path string span is invalid, non-UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character (rejected before the current store is touched), a SQLite handle’s path names a directory, the legacy header is corrupt/unsupported, SQLite cannot be loaded/opened, or the schema is incompatible. Incompatible schema failures leave the handle not-open but preserve compatibility and migration-possible flags for callers that want to migrate explicitly.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_is_open(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
uint32_t *out_open,
)#

Checks whether the data handle has an open store.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • out_open – Receives 1 when the data store is open, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_save(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
ovclash_suite_string_t file_path,
)#

Saves the current data store.

SQLite handles write normal targets as .ovclashdb stores. A target ending in .clashDetection is written in the legacy container format: a 16-byte clashDetection header followed by the SQLite database bytes. Directory handles keep their JSON directory format for every target path. A named target also persists an unnamed SQLite store, including its pending writes, and becomes its current path. A legacy container target exports a snapshot and keeps the current path.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • file_path – Length-prefixed target file path, or an empty string to use the current path. ptr may be null only when length is zero.

Returns:

Success when the current store is saved. Failure when arguments are invalid, the path string span is invalid, non-UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character, or a SQLite/IO operation fails.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_save_as(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
ovclash_suite_string_t file_path,
)#

Saves the current data store to a new path.

SQLite handles create a normal target through a database backup, including committed WAL rows and pending writes. They adopt the destination only after the backup and the source close succeed. Saving to the current file or to an existing hard-link alias keeps the current store identity. A private database extracted from a legacy container may instead move to an unused destination after closing, provided no source WAL and no destination SQLite sidecars remain. A target ending in .clashDetection is written in the legacy container format: a 16-byte clashDetection header followed by the SQLite database bytes. Directory handles keep their JSON directory format for every target path.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • file_path – Length-prefixed target file path. ptr may be null only when length is zero.

Returns:

Success after adopting a database snapshot, preserving the current store identity, moving/reopening a private extraction, or writing the legacy container. Failure when arguments are invalid, no store is open, file_path is empty, the path string span is invalid, non-UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character, or a SQLite/IO operation fails.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_close(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
)#

Closes the current data store.

Attempts to commit pending writes, including partial results kept after a failed or abandoned fetch. This is not a rollback operation. Destroy fetch operations and cursors first. A failed SQLite commit requests a rollback and returns failure. A commit or close failure keeps the data handle and storage backend for cleanup or retry, and never reports a successful close.

Parameters:

data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. May be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_commit(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
)#

Commits pending data-store changes.

Parameters:

data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_migrate_to_latest(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
ovclash_suite_string_t file_path,
)#

Migrates a data store to the latest supported schema when possible.

Migration of a legacy .clashDetection file is non-destructive. The embedded SQLite payload is extracted to a temporary .ovclashdb file, and that temporary database is migrated and opened. ovclash_suite_data_save_as persists it as a sidecar database or as a rewritten legacy container. Directory handles accept an existing directory with the supported format version. They reject unknown versions without converting or creating the store.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • file_path – Length-prefixed data file path to migrate. ptr may be null only when length is zero.

Returns:

Success when the current or supplied database is compatible or migrated. Failure when the arguments are invalid, the path string span is invalid, not UTF-8 or contains an embedded NUL character, neither a supplied nor a current data path is available, the supplied path does not exist, the legacy header is corrupt or unsupported, no schema migration path exists, the database is locked or not writable, or SQLite or IO fails. Migration never creates a missing target path. For a SQLite handle, some failures are rejected before the current store is disturbed: a call with neither a supplied nor a current path, a supplied path that is not a readable regular file, and a SQLite target that this process cannot write. The store then keeps its connection, pending writes, open state and compatibility flags, so an unnamed store keeps its private database. An extracted legacy payload is not discarded either, so the caller can still migrate in place. A legacy container, recognized by its suffix or header, is only read and need not be writable. Other target failures (a corrupt or unmigratable file, a lock, a read-only directory) are found only after the current store is closed. An invalid file-path string span, invalid UTF-8 or an embedded NUL character keeps the earlier open state. After string and path validation succeed, a SQLite migration failure leaves the handle not open. Directory migration validates the destination manifest before it closes the current store; a rejected manifest keeps the open state and the pending writes. A later close or open failure follows the matching lifecycle contract. The last-error text describes the reason.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_insert_query(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_query_view_t *query,
uint32_t update_identifier,
int64_t *out_identifier,
)#

Inserts a query and commits, like ovclash_suite_data_insert_query_with_commit with commit 1.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • query – Query view to insert. String views are copied by the data store.

  • update_identifier – Non-zero to generate a new identifier. Zero stores the view’s identifier, or generates one when it is negative.

  • out_identifier – Receives the inserted query identifier. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_insert_query_with_commit(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
const ovclash_suite_query_view_t *query,
uint32_t update_identifier,
uint32_t commit,
int64_t *out_identifier,
)#

Inserts a query with explicit commit control.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • query – Query view to insert. String views are copied by the data store.

  • update_identifier – Non-zero to generate a new identifier. Zero stores the view’s identifier, or generates one when it is negative.

  • commit – Non-zero to commit after the insert. Zero leaves the write pending; a later write that fails after its storage write began rolls back every pending write (see Data Serialization API).

  • out_identifier – Receives the inserted query identifier. Must not be null.

  • commit – Non-zero to commit after the update. Zero leaves the write pending; a later write that fails after its storage write began rolls back every pending write (see Data Serialization API).

)#

  • overlap – Overlap record view to insert. String and buffer views are copied by the data store.

const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t query_id,
uint32_t index,
ovclash_suite_state_count_view_t *out_count,
)#

Reads one state-count bucket for overlaps belonging to a query.

Buckets are ordered by ascending state value.

  • query_id – Query identifier used to filter overlaps.

  • index – Zero-based state-count row index.

  • out_count – Receives the state value and row count. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_get_overlap_by_query_at(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t query_id,
uint32_t index,
ovclash_suite_clash_info_record_view_t *out_overlap,
)#

Reads an overlap belonging to a query by zero-based filtered index.

On a SQLite store a call skips index rows. Past the first 1024 indices, a call for the index right after that of the previous call on the same query continues from the previous row instead, unless a cursor is open or the store was written in between. Prefer ovclash_suite_data_get_overlaps_by_query for sequential reads.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • query_id – Query identifier used to filter overlaps.

  • index – Zero-based overlap index within the query.

  • out_overlap – Receives the overlap record view. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_get_overlaps_by_query(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t query_id,
int64_t offset,
int64_t limit,
ovclash_suite_overlap_cursor_t **out_cursor,
)#

Opens a forward-only cursor over the overlaps of a query, ordered by overlap_id, then identifier.

The cursor reads overlap headers incrementally, including the frame count of each overlap; it does not load frame payloads. The offset is skipped once for the whole range. Serialize access with other calls on the same data handle. Destroy the cursor before closing, reopening or destroying that handle. The visibility of writes made while a cursor is open follows the backend; the cursor is not an immutable snapshot. SQLite uses one ordered statement. Directory cursors keep the ordered identifiers and load each header when advanced.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • query_id – Query identifier used to filter overlaps.

  • offset – Initial overlap offset; negative values start at zero.

  • limit – Maximum number of overlaps; zero means all remaining overlaps. Must be nonnegative.

  • out_cursor – Receives an owned cursor, including for an empty range. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_overlap_cursor_next(
ovclash_suite_overlap_cursor_t *cursor,
ovclash_suite_clash_info_record_view_t *out_view,
uint32_t *out_has_value,
)#

Advances an overlap cursor by one record.

Exhaustion succeeds with out_has_value=0 and out_view cleared, also on repeated calls. A returned view borrows cursor-owned memory until the next advance or the destruction of this cursor. Other cursors and data reads do not invalidate it.

Parameters:

  • cursor – Cursor returned by ovclash_suite_data_get_overlaps_by_query. Must not be null.

  • out_view – Receives a borrowed overlap record view. Must not be null.

  • out_has_value – Receives one for a row and zero for exhaustion or error. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_overlap_cursor_t *cursor,
)#

Destroys an overlap cursor.

Passing null succeeds and does nothing.

Parameters:

cursor – Cursor returned by ovclash_suite_data_get_overlaps_by_query.

)#

Removes all overlaps of a query with their frame records, with explicit commit control.

Like any write, the removal opens a store’s database or directory on demand, so a store that has none yet removes nothing and reports 0.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • query_id – Query identifier used to select overlaps for removal.

  • commit – Non-zero to commit after removal. Zero leaves the write pending; a later write that fails after its storage write began rolls back every pending write (see Data Serialization API).

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_remove_overlap(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t identifier,
)#

Removes an overlap with its frame records, and commits, like ovclash_suite_data_remove_overlap_with_commit with commit 1.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t overlap_identifier,
uint32_t index,
ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *out_frame,
)#

Reads a frame record belonging to an overlap by zero-based filtered index.

On a SQLite store each call skips index rows, so reading the frames of an overlap one index at a time is quadratic in the frame count. Use ovclash_suite_data_get_frames_by_overlap for sequential reads.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • overlap_identifier – Overlap identifier used to filter frame records.

  • index – Zero-based frame index within the overlap.

  • out_frame – Receives the frame record view. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_get_frames_by_overlap(
const ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t overlap_identifier,
int64_t max_frame_count,
int64_t first_frame_offset,
ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_t **out_cursor,
)#

Opens a forward-only cursor over the frame records of an overlap, in the same timecode-then-identifier order ovclash_suite_data_get_frame_by_overlap_at reads.

The cursor skips the requested offset once, unlike repeated indexed reads. SQLite steps one ordered statement. Directory cursors keep the ordered identifiers and load one frame file per advance. Changes made while the cursor is active have no guaranteed visibility; finish the cursor before modifying the queried rows.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null.

  • overlap_identifier – Overlap identifier used to filter frame records.

  • max_frame_count – Maximum number of frames to read, or a negative value for all of them; zero reads none.

  • first_frame_offset – Zero-based frame index to start at. Negative values start at zero.

  • out_cursor – Receives the cursor. Must not be null. Destroy it with ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_destroy, before destroying the data handle.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_next(
ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_t *cursor,
ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *out_frame,
uint32_t *out_has_frame,
)#

Advances a frame cursor by one record.

Running out of frames is not an error: the call succeeds with *out_has_frame set to zero and out_frame cleared. out_frame borrows cursor-owned memory, which the next ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_next or ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_destroy on the same cursor invalidates. Copy the needed data before advancing.

Parameters:

  • cursor – Cursor returned by ovclash_suite_data_get_frames_by_overlap. Must not be null.

  • out_frame – Receives the frame record view. Must not be null.

  • out_has_frame – Receives non-zero when a frame was read. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_destroy(
ovclash_suite_frame_cursor_t *cursor,
)#

Destroys a frame cursor.

Passing null succeeds and does nothing.

Parameters:

cursor – Cursor returned by ovclash_suite_data_get_frames_by_overlap.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_data_replace_frames_by_overlap_with_commit(
ovclash_suite_data_t *data,
int64_t overlap_identifier,
const ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *frames,
size_t frame_count,
uint32_t commit,
uint32_t *out_inserted_count,
)#

Replaces all frame records for an overlap with explicit commit control.

This is the bulk equivalent of removing frames with ovclash_suite_data_remove_frames_by_overlap_with_commit, then inserting each frame with ovclash_suite_data_insert_frame_with_commit. The function validates the counted frame array and each nested counted buffer before it mutates the data store. All input frame views are copied, and no pointer in frames is retained. Each stored frame gets overlap_identifier as its clash_info_id, whatever the view holds.

Parameters:

  • data – Suite data handle created by either data factory. Must not be null and must be writable.

  • overlap_identifier – Existing overlap identifier whose frame rows are replaced.

  • frames – Array of frame record views. May be null only when frame_count is zero.

  • frame_count – Number of frame views in frames. At most 1000000.

  • commit – Non-zero to commit after replacement. Zero leaves the write pending; a later write that fails after its storage write began rolls back every pending write (see Data Serialization API).

  • out_inserted_count – Receives the number of inserted frame records. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS on success; OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when data, frames, nested buffers, or overlap_identifier is invalid, or the store write fails. Failure text is available through ovclash_suite_data_get_last_error(data) and ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_get_default_run_settings(
ovclash_suite_run_settings_t *out_settings,
)#

Fills a run-settings struct with the suite defaults.

The defaults are the engine defaults of ovclash_reset_settings, expressed as Suite fields. The exceptions: pose_epsilon and area_epsilon hold the exact double 1e-6, bounds_epsilon the exact double 0.01, and the Suite-only depth_epsilon is -1.0.

Parameters:

out_settings – Receives the default run settings. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_run_settings_to_query_settings_json(
const ovclash_suite_run_settings_t *settings,
char *out_buffer,
size_t out_buffer_size,
size_t *out_required_size,
)#

Serializes run settings into the legacy clash-query settings JSON object.

The native Suite layer owns this serializer, so C and Python callers share the setting names, defaults and numeric formatting of the persisted clash_detect_settings. The keys are the ovclash_suite_setting_id_t names without their OVCLASH_SUITE_ prefix.

Finite doubles are written in printf %.17g form, with up to 17 significant digits and trailing zeros dropped, so they round-trip exactly. This is deliberately not the shortest form: a default epsilon of 1e-6 is written as 9.9999999999999995e-07. The text is persisted verbatim, so its spelling is part of the format. Negative zero is written as -0.0. Formatting uses the classic numeric locale and temporarily selects the default floating-point environment, then restores the complete environment of the caller. Directed rounding or flushed denormals therefore do not change the saved text.

Parameters:

  • settings – Run settings to serialize. Must not be null.

  • out_buffer – Destination UTF-8 buffer. May be null when out_buffer_size is zero to query size.

  • out_buffer_size – Size of out_buffer in bytes, including room for the trailing null when supplied.

  • out_required_size – Receives the required byte count excluding the trailing null. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when serialization completed or a size query succeeded. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when settings/out_required_size are null, any settings double is non-finite, out_buffer is null with non-zero out_buffer_size, out_buffer is too small, allocation fails, or an exception is caught. The thread-local last-error string contains the concrete reason.
