struct ovclash_suite_backend_info_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite.h>

Capability and load-path information for the native clash backend the library was built with.

Every value is a compile-time constant. Field catalogue:

  • backend_name: “openusd” or “ovstage”; borrows a static library-owned string valid for the process lifetime.

  • native_openusd_linked: 1 for the OpenUSD backend, otherwise 0.

  • ovpopulation_runtime_loaded: 1 for the ovstage backend, otherwise 0.

  • ovstage_cuda_enabled: 1 only for an ovstage backend built with CUDA support.

Public Members

ovclash_suite_string_t backend_name#
uint32_t native_openusd_linked#
uint32_t ovpopulation_runtime_loaded#
uint32_t ovstage_cuda_enabled#

Suite model C API#

The ClashQuery, ClashInfo, ClashFrameInfo and PointCloudSettings objects, as owned handles with getters, mutators and JSON serializers. Ownership rules for the Suite models gives their copy-in and borrow-out rules, the size-query rule of the serializers and their numeric rules, which the header states only in a group comment that does not render.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_query_reset_identifier(
ovclash_suite_query_t *query,
)#

Resets a clash query identifier to the unsaved value -1.

Preconditions: query must be a valid handle returned by a query create function. Passing null is invalid.

Side effects: mutates only the identifier field; the query remains otherwise unchanged and no persistent data store is touched.

Ownership: query remains owned by the caller and must still be destroyed with ovclash_suite_query_destroy. No borrowed views are returned.

Threading: callers must serialize access to query while mutating it. Independent query handles may be reset concurrently.

Example: 

ovclash_suite_query_t* query = 0;
ovclash_suite_query_create(&query);
ovclash_suite_query_reset_identifier(query);
ovclash_suite_query_destroy(query);

Parameters:

query – Query handle to mutate. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when the identifier is reset. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when query is null or a C++ exception is caught. Failure detail is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_query_update_last_modified(
ovclash_suite_query_t *query,
)#

Updates the last-modified timestamp and user fields from the Suite clock and user name.

Preconditions: query must be a valid handle returned by a query create function. Passing null is invalid.

Side effects: sets last_modified_timestamp to ovclash_suite_current_timestamp text and last_modified_by to ovclash_suite_current_user_name text, which is empty when no user name is available. No persistent data store is touched until the caller writes the query through a data API.

Ownership: query remains owned by the caller and must still be destroyed with ovclash_suite_query_destroy. Generated string storage is owned by query.

Threading: callers must serialize access to query while mutating it. Independent query handles may update timestamps concurrently.

Example: 

ovclash_suite_query_t* query = 0;
ovclash_suite_query_create(&query);
ovclash_suite_query_update_last_modified(query);
ovclash_suite_query_destroy(query);

Parameters:

query – Query handle to mutate. Must not be null.

Returns:

OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_SUCCESS when metadata is updated. OVCLASH_SUITE_STATUS_ERROR when query is null, allocation fails, or a C++ exception is caught. Failure detail is available through ovclash_suite_get_thread_last_error.

ovclash_suite_string_t value,
)#

Sets the settings JSON text and updates the last-modified metadata.

Parameters:

  • query – Query handle to mutate. Must not be null.

  • value – Length-prefixed settings JSON text to copy. Updates last-modified metadata.

Returns:

Success when value is empty or a syntactically valid JSON value of any kind (object, array, string, number, true, false or null), and was copied. Failure when query is null, value has an invalid span or invalid UTF-8, value is neither valid JSON nor empty, allocation fails, or an exception is caught.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_query_load_settings_json(
ovclash_suite_query_t *query,
ovclash_suite_string_t value,
)#

Loads the settings JSON text without updating the last-modified metadata.

The Python ClashQuery.load_settings_from_str wraps this function as a bool-return helper. That helper returns False for empty or invalid JSON, although this function accepts empty text.

Parameters:

  • query – Query handle to mutate. Must not be null.

  • value – Length-prefixed settings JSON text to copy without updating last-modified metadata.

Returns:

Success when value is empty or a syntactically valid JSON value of any kind (object, array, string, number, true, false or null), and was copied without touching the last-modified metadata. Failure when query is null, value has an invalid span or invalid UTF-8, value is neither valid JSON nor empty, allocation fails, or an exception is caught.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_clash_info_get_frame_info(
const ovclash_suite_clash_info_t *info,
uint32_t index,
ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *out_frame,
uint32_t *out_found,
)#

Reads one frame of a clash info.

A frame is found only after ovclash_suite_clash_info_set_frame_views, in one of two cases. When num_records equals the number of frames set, every index below it finds its frame. When num_records is 1 and the last ovclash_suite_clash_info_set_frame_views call passed no frames, any index finds a frame synthesized from the header: start_time, min_distance, max_local_depth and overlap_elements, with identity matrices. A synthesized view lasts only until the next frame read on info.

Parameters:

  • info – Clash-info handle to inspect. Must not be null.

  • index – Zero-based frame index to query.

  • out_frame – Receives the selected frame view when found. Must not be null.

  • out_found – Receives 1 when a frame was returned, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_clash_info_get_last_frame_info(
const ovclash_suite_clash_info_t *info,
ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *out_frame,
uint32_t *out_found,
)#

Reads the frame at index num_records - 1, following the rules of ovclash_suite_clash_info_get_frame_info; nothing is found when num_records is 0.

Parameters:

  • info – Clash-info handle to inspect. Must not be null.

  • out_frame – Receives the selected frame view when found. Must not be null.

  • out_found – Receives 1 when a frame was returned, otherwise 0. Must not be null.

ovclash_suite_result_t ovclash_suite_clash_info_get_frame_info_index_by_timecode(
const ovclash_suite_clash_info_t *info,
double timecode,
uint32_t *out_index,
)#

Finds the index of the set frame closest to a timecode.

Parameters:

  • info – Clash-info handle to inspect. Must not be null.

  • timecode – Timecode to search for.

  • out_index – Receives the index of the set frame whose timecode is closest to timecode, the later one on a tie, or 0 when no frames are set. Frames must be set in ascending timecode order. Must not be null.

Suite fetch serializer C API#

Fetch-and-save writes through a persistence callback table, ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t, or through the built-in SQLite and directory stores, which follow the same contract. A custom C or C++ store also passes an ovclash_suite_fetch_saved_data_reader_t, so that a re-detected approved clash can keep its approval. Saving detection results owns the transaction contract, and Clash states the state reconciliation and the approval comparison. The generated declarations of this section document the callback threads, the reader’s close rules and its output lifetimes.

Typedefs

typedef void (*ovclash_suite_visit_identifier_fn)(void *visitor_data, int64_t identifier)#

Engine-owned callback that a visit_existing implementation calls for each stored identifier.

Call it once for each stored overlap identifier of the requested query. Every signed int64 value, including -1, is a valid identifier. Duplicates are allowed; the engine removes them. Pass visitor_data unchanged. Call the visitor synchronously on the thread running visit_existing, and do not retain the function or visitor_data after visit_existing returns. The visitor reports no status and never throws across this ABI.

Param visitor_data:

Engine-owned context supplied to visit_existing; pass it unchanged.

Param identifier:

One stored signed int64 identifier of the requested query.

Enums

enum ovclash_suite_serializer_transaction_t#

Transaction operations that the fetch engine requests through the transaction callback.

An overlap written before all its reports are captured is called streamed. BEGIN_OVERLAP and END_OVERLAP bracket each streamed overlap.

Fetch-and-save is not all-or-nothing:

  • When a serializer or saved-data reader callback reports failure while the fetch advances, the engine requests ROLLBACK. A prepare_frame failure is the exception; it counts as a processing failure. ROLLBACK discards earlier fetch batches and unrelated writes already pending on the destination. Previously committed data is retained.

  • On an extraction, frame preparation or other native processing failure, the engine requests ABORT_OVERLAP, but only while a streamed overlap is incomplete. ABORT_OVERLAP restores that overlap and keeps earlier completed pending writes. A failed ABORT_OVERLAP leads to ROLLBACK. Without an incomplete overlap, these failures leave pending writes unchanged.

  • A failure during begin or initialization leaves pre-existing pending writes unchanged.

  • Destroying an operation aborts an incomplete overlap in the same way, with the same ROLLBACK fallback. Completed writes stay pending. Destroy never commits.

  • Successful finalization requests BEGIN before COMMIT, even when no results were written.

  • Reconciliation may span several calls. mark_absent changes already applied stay pending when the operation is abandoned.

ROLLBACK is requested at most once per operation and need not be idempotent. A custom destination must implement these semantics, because the engine cannot undo writes when the destination’s ROLLBACK fails. Built-in data close and destroy attempt to commit retained pending writes.

Values:

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_BEGIN#

Starts the pending transaction or reuses the open one; the callback must be idempotent.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_COMMIT#

Publishes all pending writes.

Requested only when the fetch completes successfully.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_ROLLBACK#

Discards the entire pending transaction, including unrelated pending writes.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_BEGIN_OVERLAP#

Sets a restore point before a streamed overlap is replaced.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_END_OVERLAP#

Releases the restore point after the final header of the streamed overlap is written.

enumerator OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_ABORT_OVERLAP#

Restores the incomplete streamed overlap to its restore point and keeps other pending writes.

struct ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_serializer.h>

Persistence callback table for native incremental fetch-and-save, usable from C or C++.

The table is copied at synchronous begin or at async launch. user_data must outlive the operation. Inputs are borrowed for the duration of a callback unless a member documents a longer lifetime.

Completion: before each callback the engine sets out_success to 0. A callback writes exactly 1 only after all its work and output construction succeed; any other value means failure. Callbacks return void, so out_success is the only completion signal. No callback may throw across this ABI. The engine ignores the outputs of a failed callback, except that it takes ownership of a nonnull prepare_frame output. Reporting failure cannot undo side effects that a callback already published. A destination whose COMMIT or ROLLBACK fails may need application-level recovery.

Threading: every callback except prepare_frame runs on the driving thread, one call at a time. With the synchronous bounded API, the driving thread is the thread calling ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin, next or destroy; no callback runs between those calls. With ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_async, it is the operation’s background worker. Storage writes follow runtime result order. The order of release_frame calls is unspecified.

Public Members

void *user_data#

Caller-owned context passed unchanged as the first argument of every callback.

May be null when the implementation needs no context. The table is copied, but this pointer and the state it names must stay valid until destroying the operation has drained all callbacks.

void (*visit_existing)(void *user_data, int64_t query_id, ovclash_suite_visit_identifier_fn visitor, void *visitor_data, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: enumerates the stored identifiers of query_id once, during fetch initialization.

Runs on the driving thread before any fetch write. Include every stored row of the query, including absent and resolved rows and separate rows that share an overlap hash. Frames are not needed. Call visitor(visitor_data, identifier) once per row, in any order. The engine deduplicates and sorts the identifiers for the later stale-row reconciliation. Do not retain visitor or visitor_data. Set out_success to 1 only after the enumeration completes. A failure here does not request ROLLBACK and leaves pre-existing pending writes unchanged.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param query_id:

Query whose stored overlap identifiers are enumerated.

Param visitor:

Engine-owned callback to call synchronously for each identifier.

Param visitor_data:

Engine-owned context to pass unchanged to visitor.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after a successful enumeration; initially 0.

void (*find_overlap)(void *user_data, int64_t query_id, ovclash_suite_string_t overlap_id, ovclash_suite_clash_info_record_view_t *out_record, uint32_t *out_found, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: looks up one stored header by query_id and the borrowed UTF-8 overlap hash overlap_id.

Runs on the driving thread before the first header write of an overlap, and again before the final header of a streamed overlap. The engine zero-initializes out_record and out_found. Set out_success to 1 for a successful lookup, including when no row exists. Set out_found to 0 when the row is absent, or to nonzero when it is found. The engine reads out_record only for a found row whose lookup succeeded. Its strings must be valid UTF-8 spans that stay alive until the next serializer callback; the engine copies them. No frame reads or writes are needed here.

From a found row the engine keeps identifier, state, priority, person_in_charge, creation_timestamp, comment and penetration_depth_px/nx/py/ny/pz/nz, and regenerates every other field. Filling only these fields, with the rest zero-initialized, is enough. state is required: the engine writes it back, and a found APPROVED state enables the approval comparison described below.

With resolve_stale zero, the stored state is kept. Otherwise a re-detected normal or duplicate overlap becomes ACTIVE. The exception is an APPROVED clash whose detected header and complete ordered frame contents match through the optional saved-data reader; it stays APPROVED. Without that reader, a custom fetch makes every re-detected clash ACTIVE. A new header starts NEW and is not promoted during its first fetch. Its final streamed header keeps any state that the serializer applied on insertion.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param query_id:

Query of the stored header.

Param overlap_id:

Borrowed UTF-8 overlap hash of the stored header.

Param out_record:

Receives the found header; initially zero-initialized.

Param out_found:

Receives 0 when the row is absent, or nonzero when it is found; initially 0.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 when the lookup succeeds, including absence; initially 0.

void (*write_overlap)(void *user_data, const ovclash_suite_clash_info_record_view_t *record, int64_t *out_identifier, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: inserts or updates the borrowed overlap header record.

Runs on the driving thread after find_overlap. Write only the header. Do not commit, delete existing frames, or create placeholder frames from num_records or frame_count. On success, publish the row’s stable signed int64 identifier through out_identifier and set out_success to 1. Every signed value, including -1, is a valid identifier. The engine sets out_identifier to 0 first and ignores it on failure. Do not retain record or its borrowed strings. A streamed overlap gets an initial header before clear_frames and append_frame, and a final refreshed header after its last captured frame. Frame batches in between reuse the stable identifier.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param record:

Borrowed overlap header to insert or update, without frame contents.

Param out_identifier:

Receives the stable stored identifier on success; initially 0.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after the header write succeeds; initially 0.

void (*clear_frames)(void *user_data, int64_t identifier, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: removes all stored frame records of identifier.

Keep the overlap’s identity and editable annotations, and do not commit. Runs on the driving thread once per written overlap, after its initial write_overlap and before its first append_frame. A streamed overlap is cleared inside its restore point. Set out_success to 1 after the deletion succeeds. Failure requests ROLLBACK.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param identifier:

Stable identifier returned by write_overlap.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after the existing frames are removed; initially 0.

void (*append_frame)(void *user_data, int64_t identifier, const ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_view_t *frame, const void *prepared, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: appends the borrowed frame view to the overlap named by identifier.

Runs on the driving thread in runtime result order, after clear_frames. Do not commit. prepared is the matching output of a successful prepare_frame. It is null when preparation is not used or produced no payload. prepared stays engine-owned; do not free or retain it. Copy the view and its arrays if storage needs them after this callback. Set out_success to 1 only after the frame is stored. Failure requests ROLLBACK. The order in which preparations complete never changes the append order. release_frame runs only after the payload is used.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param identifier:

Stable identifier returned by write_overlap.

Param frame:

Borrowed runtime frame view and arrays to append.

Param prepared:

Matching engine-owned encoding from prepare_frame, or null.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after the frame is stored; initially 0.

void (*mark_absent)(void *user_data, int64_t identifier, uint32_t resolve, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: marks the stored row identifier absent, and also RESOLVED when resolve is nonzero.

Leave its frame records intact and do not commit. Runs on the driving thread after the result writes, once for each initially enumerated identifier that no completed overlap write matched, in ascending identifier order. Reconciliation may span several next calls; changes already applied stay pending if the operation is abandoned. Set out_success to 1 on success. Failure requests ROLLBACK.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param identifier:

Initially enumerated stored row that no completed write matched.

Param resolve:

Nonzero requests RESOLVED state as well as absence; zero keeps the state.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after the absence update succeeds; initially 0.

void (*transaction)(void *user_data, uint32_t operation, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: applies one ovclash_suite_serializer_transaction_t operation on the driving thread.

BEGIN must be idempotent. It precedes each write batch and each reconciliation batch, so COMMIT always follows a BEGIN, even for an empty fetch. COMMIT is requested only when the fetch completes. It publishes every pending write, including unrelated ones. ROLLBACK is requested at most once per operation, after a persistence failure. It discards the whole pending transaction, including earlier batches and unrelated pending writes. BEGIN_OVERLAP sets a restore point before a streamed overlap is replaced. END_OVERLAP releases it after the final header of that overlap is written. ABORT_OVERLAP restores only the incomplete overlap, after a processing failure or on abandonment, and keeps earlier completed pending writes. A failed ABORT_OVERLAP requests ROLLBACK. An initialization failure leaves existing pending writes unchanged. Destruction never commits. Set out_success to 1 only after the operation succeeds. A failed COMMIT or ROLLBACK cannot undo side effects already published and may need application-level recovery.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param operation:

One OVCLASH_SUITE_SERIALIZER_* transaction operation.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after the operation succeeds; initially 0.

void (*prepare_frame)(void *user_data, const ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_view_t *frame, void **out_prepared, uint32_t *out_success)#

Optional, set together with release_frame: encodes the borrowed frame view for a later append_frame.

Calls may run concurrently on preparation workers, as the runtime threading settings allow, or serially on the driving thread, for example in single-threaded mode. Access only immutable input and the output of this call. Do not use a connection or any other shared mutable state, including serializer diagnostics. Do not retain the pointer to the view struct. A copy of the view may keep its borrowed geometry arrays until the matching release_frame, which runs before the report is released. The engine sets out_prepared to null first. Publish an optional owned encoding there, then set out_success to 1. The engine takes every nonnull published payload, even on failure, and releases it exactly once. A failed preparation is never appended. It gets a generic diagnostic, and last_error is not queried. A successful null payload is allowed.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context; access only immutable state during preparation.

Param frame:

Borrowed frame view. Do not retain this pointer.

Param out_prepared:

Receives an optional owned encoding; initially null.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after a successful preparation; initially 0.

void (*release_frame)(void *user_data, void *prepared, uint32_t *out_success)#

Optional, set together with prepare_frame: releases one nonnull prepared payload on the driving thread.

Runs before the runtime report that the payload borrows from is released. It is called exactly once for every published nonnull payload, including failed preparations and work that was abandoned or never appended. Release order is unspecified. Release all ownership even when reporting failure, and set out_success to 1 only after cleanup succeeds. The engine never retries this callback. A failed release gets a generic diagnostic and requests ROLLBACK once the remaining cleanup has drained.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param prepared:

One nonnull encoding whose ownership is released.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 after cleanup succeeds; initially 0.

void (*last_error)(void *user_data, ovclash_suite_string_t *out_error, uint32_t *out_success)#

Optional: publishes the serializer’s diagnostic through out_error on the driving thread.

The engine sets the view empty and out_success to 0 first. Set out_success to 1 after publishing a valid borrowed UTF-8 view. The engine copies a nonempty message before the next callback. Empty text, a null callback or a failed acknowledgement yields a generic diagnostic, and the engine does not read failed outputs. This callback may follow a failed storage action on the driving thread. It is not queried for prepare_frame or release_frame failures, nor during secondary cleanup that preserves an earlier failure. Cleanup that is itself the first failure may query it. Do not throw across this ABI.

Param user_data:

Caller-owned context from this callback table.

Param out_error:

Receives the borrowed UTF-8 diagnostic view; initially empty.

Param out_success:

Receives exactly 1 when the diagnostic is published; initially 0.

struct ovclash_suite_fetch_saved_data_reader_t#
#include <include/ovclash_suite/ovclash_suite_serializer.h>

Optional saved-data reader for exact comparison of previously approved custom overlaps.

Pass this table to ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_begin_with_reader or ovclash_suite_runtime_fetch_and_save_async_with_reader. The table is copied at synchronous begin or at async launch. user_data and the saved destination must outlive the operation. read_overlap and read_frame are required; close is optional. All three run on the driving thread. The read callbacks run before the overlap’s header and frames are replaced. Set out_success to exactly 1 only after building complete outputs, and never throw across this ABI. Calls and borrowed outputs follow the same serialized access rule as the fetch operation.

The query and the ordered pair hash establish result identity. The comparison covers type, tolerance, depth epsilon, paths, mesh checksums, aggregates and the ordered runtime frame contents. It excludes stored overlap and frame row identifiers, review fields, timestamps and user penetration-depth annotations. Floating-point equality uses no epsilon and ignores the caller’s denormal controls. Signed zeros compare equal, and a NaN never proves contents unchanged.

The reader is a separate table so that ovclash_suite_fetch_serializer_t keeps its ABI. Without a reader, a nonzero resolve_stale makes every re-detected approved custom clash ACTIVE, because unchanged detected contents cannot be proven.

Public Members

void *user_data#

Caller-owned context passed unchanged as the first argument of every reader callback.

void (*read_overlap)(void*, int64_t identifier, ovclash_suite_clash_info_record_view_t *out_overlap, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: reads the stored header of identifier into out_overlap.

identifier is the stable identifier that find_overlap returned. Fill every detected header field and the actual saved frame_count; unlike find_overlap, do not leave detected fields zero. Output strings stay valid until the next reader callback.

void (*read_frame)(void*, int64_t identifier, uint32_t frame_index, ovclash_suite_clash_frame_info_record_view_t *out_frame, uint32_t *out_success)#

Required: reads the complete saved frame at zero-based frame_index of identifier into out_frame.

Frames are indexed in persisted order. identifier is the one that find_overlap returned, not the identifier inside the header from read_overlap. Output strings and arrays stay valid until the next reader callback.

void (*close)(void*, uint32_t *out_success)#

Optional: releases any reader-owned cursor.

Runs on the driving thread after each overlap comparison that read saved data, before the overlap is replaced, and when an unfinished fetch is destroyed. It must succeed when no cursor is open. A failed close is reported and may be retried on the same thread during failure or destruction cleanup; a successful close is not retried. Async fetching closes on its original worker before it publishes its terminal state. Synchronous callers must drive and destroy the operation on a thread compatible with the reader’s resources. A reader whose close keeps failing remains responsible for its resources.
